title.en: Volume 135 Biographies 85: Lu Qi, Bai Zhizhen, Pei Yanling, Wei Qumou, Li Qiyun, Li Shi, Wei Zhiyi, Wang Shuwen, Cheng Yi, Huang Fubian

sentences.zh: 盧杞，字子良，故相懷慎之孫。

translations.literal: Lu Qi, styled Ziliang, was the grandson of the former chancellor Lu Huaijian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, styled Ziliang, was the grandson of the former chancellor Lu Huaijian.

sentences.zh: 父奕，天寶末為東臺御史中丞；

translations.literal: His father Yi, at the end of the Tianbao era, served as Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Eastern Bureau;
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi, at the end of the Tianbao era, served as Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Eastern Bureau;

sentences.zh: 洛城為安祿山所陷，奕守司而遇害。

translations.literal: when Luoyang fell to An Lushan, Yi held his post and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: when Luoyang fell to An Lushan, Yi held his post and was killed.

sentences.zh: 杞以門廕，解褐清道率府兵曹。

translations.literal: Qi, through hereditary privilege, began his career as a military staff officer of the Qingdao Command.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege, Qi began his career as a military staff officer of the Qingdao Command.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使仆固懷恩辟為掌書記、試大理評事、監察御史，以病免。

translations.literal: The Shuofang military commissioner Pugu Huai'en recruited him as chief secretary, acting Grand Councilor of the Court of Judicial Review, and investigating censor; he was dismissed on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang military commissioner Pugu Huai'en recruited him as chief secretary, acting Grand Councilor of the Court of Judicial Review, and investigating censor; he was dismissed on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 入補鴻臚丞，遷殿中侍御史、膳部員外郎，出為忠州刺史。

translations.literal: He entered service as an assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was promoted to palace censor and a staff member of the Ministry of Rites, and went out as prefect of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was promoted to palace censor and a staff member of the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed prefect of Zhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至荊南，謁節度使衛伯玉，伯玉不悅。

translations.literal: When he reached Jingnan, he called on the military commissioner Wei Boyu, who was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jingnan, he called on military commissioner Wei Boyu, who was displeased.

sentences.zh: 杞移病歸京師，歷刑部員外郎、金部吏部二郎中。

translations.literal: Qi pleaded illness and returned to the capital, serving successively as a staff member of the Ministry of Justice and as director in the Ministries of Revenue and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Qi pleaded illness and returned to the capital, serving successively as a staff member of the Ministry of Justice and as director in the Ministries of Revenue and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 杞貌陋而色如藍，人皆鬼視之。

translations.literal: Qi was ugly in appearance and his complexion was bluish; people all looked at him as though he were a ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was ugly in appearance and his complexion had a bluish cast; people looked at him as though he were a ghost.

sentences.zh: 不恥惡衣糲食，人以為能嗣懷慎之清節，亦未識其心。

translations.literal: He was not ashamed to wear shabby clothes and eat coarse food, and people thought he could inherit Huaijian's reputation for integrity—yet they did not yet know his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He was not ashamed to wear shabby clothes and eat coarse food, and people thought he could inherit Huaijian's reputation for integrity—yet they did not yet know his heart.

sentences.zh: 頗有口辯。

translations.literal: He was quite gifted in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He was quite gifted in debate.

sentences.zh: 出為虢州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建中初，徵為御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, he was summoned as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, he was summoned to serve as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時尚父子儀病，百官造問，皆不屏姬侍。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Shang, Guo Ziyi, was ill, and officials of all ranks came to inquire after him without dismissing their concubines and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Shang, Guo Ziyi, was ill, and officials of all ranks came to inquire after him without dismissing their concubines and attendants.

sentences.zh: 及聞杞至，子儀悉令屏去，獨隱几以待之。

translations.literal: When he heard that Qi had arrived, Ziyi had them all sent away and sat alone behind a screen to await him.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Qi had arrived, Ziyi had them all sent away and sat alone behind a screen to await him.

sentences.zh: 杞去，家人問其故，子儀曰：「杞形陋而心險，左右見之必笑。

translations.literal: After Qi left, his family asked the reason. Ziyi said: "Qi is ugly in form but treacherous at heart. If those beside me see him, they will surely laugh.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi left, his family asked the reason. Ziyi said, "Qi is ugly in form but treacherous at heart. If those beside me see him, they will surely laugh.

sentences.zh: 若此人得權，即吾族無類矣。」

translations.literal: If this man gains power, then there will be none left of our clan."
translations.idiomatic: If this man gains power, there will be none left of our clan."

sentences.zh: 及居糾彈顧問之地，論奏稱旨，遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: Once he occupied the post of investigation and consultation, his memorials and discussions pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Once he occupied the post of investigation and consultation, his memorials and discussions pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 旬日，為門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Within ten days he became Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Concurrent Regular Second-Rank Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he became Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Concurrent Regular Second-Rank Counselor.

sentences.zh: 既居相位，忌能妒賢，迎吠陰害，小不附者，必致之於死，將起勢立威，以久其權。

translations.literal: Once he held the chancellorship, he envied ability and hated worth, fawned on the powerful and harmed in secret; anyone who did not submit even slightly, he was sure to bring to death, intending to raise his prestige and establish his authority so as to prolong his power.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the chancellorship, he envied ability and hated worth, fawned on the powerful and harmed in secret; anyone who did not submit even slightly, he was sure to bring to death, intending to raise his prestige and establish his authority so as to prolong his power.

sentences.zh: 楊炎以杞陋貌無識，同處臺司，心甚不悅，為杞所譖，逐於崖州。

translations.literal: Yang Yan regarded Qi as ugly, lacking in judgment, and ill at ease sharing the censorate; Qi slandered him and had him banished to Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan regarded Qi as ugly, lacking in judgment, and ill at ease sharing the censorate; Qi slandered him and had him banished to Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸奉天，崔寧流涕論時事，杞聞惡之，譖於德宗，言寧與硃泚盟誓，故至遲回，寧遂見殺。

translations.literal: When Dezong went to Fengtian, Cui Ning wept as he discussed current affairs; Qi heard and hated this, slandered Ning to Dezong, saying Ning had sworn an oath with Zhu Ci, and so Ning was delayed in returning and was eventually killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong went to Fengtian, Cui Ning wept as he discussed current affairs; Qi heard and hated this, slandered Ning to Dezong, saying Ning had sworn an oath with Zhu Ci, and so Ning was delayed in returning and was eventually killed.

sentences.zh: 惡顏真卿之直言，令奉使李希烈，竟歿於賊。

translations.literal: He hated Yan Zhenqing's outspokenness and sent him on a mission to Li Xilie, who ultimately died among the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He hated Yan Zhenqing's outspokenness and sent him on a mission to Li Xilie, who ultimately died among the rebels.

sentences.zh: 初，京兆尹嚴郢與楊炎有隙，杞乃擢郢為御史大夫以傾炎；

translations.literal: At first, the metropolitan magistrate Yan Yi had a rift with Yang Yan; Qi then promoted Yi to Censor-in-Chief in order to topple Yan;
translations.idiomatic: At first, metropolitan magistrate Yan Yi had a rift with Yang Yan; Qi then promoted Yi to Censor-in-Chief in order to topple Yan;

sentences.zh: 炎既貶死，心又惡郢，圖欲去之。

translations.literal: after Yan was demoted and died, he again hated Yi and plotted to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: after Yan was demoted and died, he again hated Yi and plotted to remove him.

sentences.zh: 宰相張鎰忠正有才，上所委信，杞頗惡之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhang Yi was upright, talented, and deeply trusted by the emperor; Qi greatly hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhang Yi was upright, talented, and deeply trusted by the emperor; Qi greatly hated him.

sentences.zh: 會硃滔、硃泚弟兄不睦，有泚判官蔡廷玉者離間滔，滔論奏，請殺之。

translations.literal: It happened that the brothers Zhu Tao and Zhu Ci were not on good terms; there was Ci's aide Cai Tingyu, who sowed discord with Tao, and Tao memorialized requesting Tingyu's execution.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the brothers Zhu Tao and Zhu Ci were not on good terms; there was Ci's aide Cai Tingyu, who sowed discord with Tao, and Tao memorialized requesting Tingyu's execution.

sentences.zh: 廷玉既貶，殿中侍御史鄭詹遣吏監送，廷玉投水而卒。

translations.literal: After Tingyu was demoted, palace censor Zheng Zhan sent officers to escort him; Tingyu threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Tingyu was demoted, palace censor Zheng Zhan sent officers to escort him; Tingyu threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 杞因奏曰：「恐硃泚疑為詔旨，請三司按鞠詹；

translations.literal: Qi therefore memorialized, saying: "I fear Zhu Ci may suspect this was an imperial order; please have the Three Offices investigate Zhan;
translations.idiomatic: Qi therefore memorialized, saying, "I fear Zhu Ci may suspect this was an imperial order; please have the Three Offices investigate Zhan;

sentences.zh: 又御史所為，稟大夫命，並令按郢。」

translations.literal: and since what censors do is carried out on the Censor-in-Chief's orders, have Yi investigated as well."
translations.idiomatic: and since what censors do is carried out on the Censor-in-Chief's orders, have Yi investigated as well."

sentences.zh: 詹與張鎰善，每伺杞晝眠，輒詣鎰，杞知之。

translations.literal: Zhan was on good terms with Zhang Yi; whenever Qi dozed by day, Zhan would go to Yi, and Qi learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was on good terms with Zhang Yi; whenever Qi dozed by day, Zhan would go to Yi, and Qi learned of it.

sentences.zh: 他日，杞假寢佯熟，伺詹果來，方與鎰語，杞遽至鎰閣中，詹趨避杞，杞遽言密事，鎰曰：「殿中鄭侍御在此。」

translations.literal: Another day Qi feigned sleep and pretended to be deep in slumber; when Zhan indeed came and was speaking with Yi, Qi suddenly entered Yi's pavilion. Zhan hurried to avoid Qi; Qi immediately began speaking of secret matters. Yi said: "Palace Censor Zheng is here."
translations.idiomatic: Another day Qi feigned sleep and pretended to be deep in slumber; when Zhan indeed came and was speaking with Yi, Qi suddenly entered Yi's pavilion. Zhan hurried to avoid Qi; Qi immediately began speaking of secret matters. Yi said, "Palace Censor Zheng is here."

sentences.zh: 杞佯愕曰：「向者所言，非他人所宜聞。」

translations.literal: Qi feigned astonishment and said: "What was just spoken is not for others to hear."
translations.idiomatic: Qi feigned astonishment and said, "What was just spoken is not for others to hear."

sentences.zh: 時三司使方按詹、郢，獄未具而奏殺詹，貶郢為驩州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Offices commissioners were investigating Zhan and Yi; before the case was complete he memorialized for Zhan's execution and demoted Yi to prefect of Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Three Offices commissioners were investigating Zhan and Yi; before the case was complete he memorialized for Zhan's execution and demoted Yi to prefect of Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鎰尋罷相，出鎮鳳翔。

translations.literal: Yi was soon dismissed from the chancellorship and went out to command Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was soon dismissed from the chancellorship and went out to command Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 其陰禍賊物如此。

translations.literal: His hidden harm to worthy men was like this.
translations.idiomatic: His hidden harm to worthy men was like this.

sentences.zh: 李揆舊德，慮德宗復用，乃遣使西蕃，天下無不扼腕痛憤，然無敢言者。

translations.literal: Li Kui was a man of old virtue; fearing Dezong might employ him again, he sent an envoy to the Western Regions; throughout the realm all clench their fists in grief and rage, yet none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui was a man of old virtue; fearing Dezong might employ him again, he sent an envoy to the Western Regions; throughout the realm all clench their fists in grief and rage, yet none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎、判度支杜佑，甚承恩顧，為杞媒孽，貶饒州刺史。

translations.literal: Du You, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting director of the Department of Public Works, enjoyed great imperial favor; Qi slandered him and had him demoted to prefect of Rao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Du You, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting director of the Department of Public Works, enjoyed great imperial favor; Qi slandered him and had him demoted to prefect of Rao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，上即位，擢崔祐甫為相，頗用道德寬大，以弘上意，故建中初政聲藹然，海內想望貞觀之理；

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor took the throne, he promoted Cui Youfu as chancellor and greatly employed moral breadth and magnanimity to carry out the emperor's intent; therefore at the beginning of Jianzhong the government's reputation was serene, and within the seas people looked toward the governance of the Zhenguan era;
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the emperor took the throne, he promoted Cui Youfu as chancellor and greatly employed moral breadth and magnanimity to carry out the emperor's intent; therefore at the beginning of Jianzhong the government's reputation was serene, and throughout the realm people looked toward the governance of the Zhenguan era;

sentences.zh: 及杞為相，諷上以刑名整齊天下。

translations.literal: once Qi became chancellor, he urged the emperor to use penal law to put the realm in order.
translations.idiomatic: once Qi became chancellor, he urged the emperor to use penal law to put the realm in order.

sentences.zh: 初，李希烈請討梁崇義，崇義誅而希烈叛，盡據淮右、襄、鄧之郡邑。

translations.literal: At first Li Xilie requested to campaign against Liang Chongyi; after Chongyi was executed Xilie rebelled and seized all the prefectures and counties of the Huai region, Xiang, and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Xilie requested to campaign against Liang Chongyi; after Chongyi was executed Xilie rebelled and seized all the prefectures and counties of the Huai region, Xiang, and Deng.

sentences.zh: 恆州李寶臣死，其子惟嶽邀節鉞，遂與田悅締結以抗王師，由是河北、河南連兵不息。

translations.literal: Li Baochen of Heng Prefecture died; his son Weiyue sought the command, then joined Tian Yue in alliance to resist the imperial army; from this the armies of Hebei and Henan fought without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baochen of Heng Prefecture died; his son Weiyue sought the command, then joined Tian Yue in alliance to resist the imperial army; from this the armies of Hebei and Henan fought without cease.

sentences.zh: 度支使杜佑計諸道用軍月費一百余萬貫，京師帑廩不支數月；

translations.literal: Du You, director of the Department of Public Works, calculated that the monthly military expenses of the various circuits exceeded more than a million strings of cash, and the capital's storehouses could not support them for several months;
translations.idiomatic: Du You, director of the Department of Public Works, calculated that the monthly military expenses of the various circuits exceeded more than a million strings of cash, and the capital's storehouses could not support them for several months;

sentences.zh: 且得五百萬貫，可支半歲，則用兵濟矣。

translations.literal: yet if five million strings could be obtained, they could last half a year, and then military operations could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: yet if five million strings could be obtained, they could last half a year, and then military operations could succeed.

sentences.zh: 杞乃以戶部侍郎趙贊判度支，贊亦無計可施，乃與其黨太常博士韋都賓等謀行括率，以為泉貨所聚，在於富商，錢出萬貫者，留萬貫為業，有余，官借以給軍，冀得五百萬貫。

translations.literal: Qi then had Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zan act as director of the Department of Public Works; Zan too had no plan, and with his faction, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Dubin and others, plotted to carry out forced requisitioning, thinking that where currency gathered was among wealthy merchants: those with more than ten thousand strings would keep ten thousand for their business, and the surplus would be borrowed by the state to supply the army, hoping to obtain five million strings.
translations.idiomatic: Qi then had Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zan act as director of the Department of Public Works; Zan too had no plan, and with his faction, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Dubin and others, plotted to carry out forced requisitioning, thinking that where currency gathered was among wealthy merchants: those with more than ten thousand strings would keep ten thousand for their business, and the surplus would be borrowed by the state to supply the army, hoping to obtain five million strings.

sentences.zh: 上許之，約以罷兵後以公錢還。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, with the agreement that after the troops were withdrawn public funds would be repaid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, with the agreement that after the troops were withdrawn public funds would be repaid.

sentences.zh: 敕即下，京兆少尹韋禎督責頗峻，長安尉薛萃荷校乘車，搜人財貨，意其不實，即行搒箠，人不勝冤痛，或有自縊而死者，京師囂然如被賊盜。

translations.literal: Once the edict was issued, metropolitan vice magistrate Wei Zhen supervised collection with great severity; Chang'an bailiff Xue Cui carried cangues in his carriage, searched people's property, and if he thought the declarations false, immediately had them beaten; people could not bear the injustice and pain, and some hanged themselves; the capital seethed as though plundered by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Once the edict was issued, metropolitan vice magistrate Wei Zhen supervised collection with great severity; Chang'an bailiff Xue Cui carried cangues in his carriage, searched people's property, and if he thought the declarations false, immediately had them beaten; people could not bear the injustice and pain, and some hanged themselves; the capital seethed as though plundered by bandits.

sentences.zh: 都計富戶田宅奴婢等估，才及八十八萬貫。

translations.literal: In all, the wealthy households' estates, mansions, slaves, and the like were assessed at only 880,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the wealthy households' estates, mansions, slaves, and the like were assessed at only 880,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 又以僦櫃納質積錢貨貯粟麥等，一切借四分之一，封其櫃窖，長安為之罷市，百姓相率千萬眾邀宰相於道訴之。

translations.literal: They also borrowed a quarter of all pawned goods, deposits, stored currency, grain, and millet, sealed their chests and cellars, and Chang'an ceased trading; the common people in groups of tens of millions blocked the chancellors on the road to plead.
translations.idiomatic: They also borrowed a quarter of all pawned goods, deposits, stored currency, grain, and millet, sealed their chests and cellars, and Chang'an ceased trading; the common people in groups of tens of millions blocked the chancellors on the road to plead.

sentences.zh: 杞初雖慰諭，後無以遏，即疾驅而歸。

translations.literal: At first Qi consoled and instructed them, but afterward could not restrain them and hurried home at a gallop.
translations.idiomatic: At first Qi consoled and instructed them, but afterward could not restrain them and hurried home at a gallop.

sentences.zh: 計僦質與借商，才二百萬貫。

translations.literal: The pawned deposits and merchant loans together amounted to only two million strings.
translations.idiomatic: The pawned deposits and merchant loans together amounted to only two million strings.

sentences.zh: 德宗知下民流怨，詔皆罷之，然宿師在野，日須供饋。

translations.literal: Dezong knew the people below were full of resentment and ordered all these measures abolished, yet troops remained in the field and daily required supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong knew the people below were full of resentment and ordered all these measures abolished, yet troops remained in the field and daily required supplies.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，趙贊又請稅間架、算除陌。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year Zhao Zan again requested taxes on partitioned rooms and calculations on removed cash marks.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the following year Zhao Zan again requested taxes on partitioned rooms and calculations on removed cash marks.

sentences.zh: 凡屋兩架為一間，分為三等：上等每間二千，中等一千，下等五百。

translations.literal: Every two bays of a building counted as one room, divided into three grades: upper-grade rooms two thousand per room, middle-grade one thousand, lower-grade five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Every two bays of a building counted as one room, divided into three grades: upper-grade rooms two thousand per room, middle-grade one thousand, lower-grade five hundred.

sentences.zh: 所由吏秉筆執籌，入人第舍而計之。

translations.literal: The responsible clerks carried brushes and counting rods and entered people's dwellings to calculate.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible clerks carried brushes and counting rods and entered people's dwellings to calculate.

sentences.zh: 凡沒一間，杖六十，告者賞錢五十貫文。

translations.literal: For every room concealed, sixty blows with the staff; informers were rewarded fifty strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: For every room concealed, sixty blows with the staff; informers were rewarded fifty strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 除陌法，天下公私給與貿易，率一貫舊算二十，益加算為五十，給與物或兩換者，約錢為率算之。

translations.literal: Under the removed-cash-mark law, all public and private gifts and trade throughout the realm were taxed at twenty per old string, increased to fifty; when goods were exchanged in barter, the value in cash was used as the rate for calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the removed-cash-mark law, all public and private gifts and trade throughout the realm were taxed at twenty per old string, increased to fifty; when goods were exchanged in barter, the value in cash was used as the rate for calculation.

sentences.zh: 市主人牙子各給印紙，人有買賣，隨自署記，翌日合算之。

translations.literal: Market masters and brokers were each given stamped papers; when people bought and sold they signed themselves, and the next day all was calculated together.
translations.idiomatic: Market masters and brokers were each given stamped papers; when people bought and sold they signed themselves, and the next day all was calculated together.

sentences.zh: 有自貿易不用市牙子者，驗其私簿，投狀自其有私簿投狀。

translations.literal: Those who traded on their own without using market brokers had their private ledgers inspected and submitted petitions declaring their accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Those who traded on their own without using market brokers had their private ledgers inspected and submitted petitions declaring their accounts.

sentences.zh: 其有隱錢百，沒入；

translations.literal: If a hundred strings were concealed, confiscation;
translations.idiomatic: If a hundred strings were concealed, confiscation;

sentences.zh: 二千，杖六十；

translations.literal: two thousand, sixty blows with the staff;
translations.idiomatic: two thousand, sixty blows with the staff;

sentences.zh: 告者賞錢十千，出於其家。

translations.literal: informers were rewarded ten thousand, taken from the offender's household.
translations.idiomatic: informers were rewarded ten thousand, taken from the offender's household.

sentences.zh: 法既行，主人市牙得專其柄，率多隱盜，公家所入，百不得半，怨讟之聲，囂然滿於天下。

translations.literal: Once the law was implemented, market masters and brokers monopolized control, mostly concealing and stealing; what the public treasury received was not even half; sounds of resentment filled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Once the law was implemented, market masters and brokers monopolized control, mostly concealing and stealing; what the public treasury received was not even half; sounds of resentment filled the realm.

sentences.zh: 及十月，涇師犯闕，亂兵呼於市曰：「不奪汝商戶僦質矣！

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Jing army attacked the capital; rebel soldiers shouted in the markets: "We won't seize your merchants' pawn deposits!
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Jing army attacked the capital; rebel soldiers shouted in the markets, "We won't seize your merchants' pawn deposits!

sentences.zh: 不稅汝間架除陌矣！」

translations.literal: We won't tax your partitioned rooms and removed cash marks!"
translations.idiomatic: We won't tax your partitioned rooms and removed cash marks!"

sentences.zh: 是時人心悉怨，涇師乘間謀亂，奉天之奔播，職杞之由。

translations.literal: At that time everyone's heart was full of resentment; the Jing army seized the opportunity to plot rebellion; the emperor's flight to Fengtian was due to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time everyone's heart was full of resentment; the Jing army seized the opportunity to plot rebellion; the emperor's flight to Fengtian was due to Qi.

sentences.zh: 故天下無賢不肖，視杞如仇。

translations.literal: Therefore throughout the realm, worthy and unworthy alike regarded Qi as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore throughout the realm, worthy and unworthy alike regarded Qi as an enemy.

sentences.zh: 德宗在奉天，為硃泚攻圍，李懷光自魏縣赴難。

translations.literal: Dezong was at Fengtian, besieged by Zhu Ci; Li Huaiguang came from Wei County to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was at Fengtian, besieged by Zhu Ci; Li Huaiguang came from Wei County to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 或謂王翃、趙贊曰：「懷光累嘆憤，以為宰相謀議乖方，度支賦斂煩重，京尹刻薄軍糧，乘輿播遷，三臣之罪也。

translations.literal: Someone said to Wang Hong and Zhao Zan: "Huaiguang has repeatedly sighed in anger, thinking the chancellors' counsel was misguided, the Department of Public Works' levies burdensome, and the metropolitan magistrate harsh in military grain, and that the imperial carriage's displacement was the fault of these three ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Wang Hong and Zhao Zan, "Huaiguang has repeatedly sighed in anger, thinking the chancellors' counsel was misguided, the Department of Public Works' levies burdensome, and the metropolitan magistrate harsh in military grain, and that the imperial carriage's displacement was the fault of these three ministers.

sentences.zh: 今懷光勛業崇重，聖上必開襟布誠，詢問得失，使其言入，豈不殆哉！」

translations.literal: Now Huaiguang's achievements are lofty and weighty; the sage emperor is sure to open his heart in sincerity and inquire about right and wrong—if his words get through, will we not be in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Huaiguang's achievements are lofty and weighty; the sage emperor is sure to open his heart in sincerity and inquire about right and wrong—if his words get through, will we not be in peril!"

sentences.zh: 翃、贊白於杞，杞大駭懼，從容奏曰：「懷光勛業，宗社是賴。

translations.literal: Hong and Zan reported to Qi; Qi was greatly alarmed and, with composure, memorialized: "Huaiguang's achievements are what the altars of state rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Zan reported to Qi; Qi was greatly alarmed and, with composure, memorialized, "Huaiguang's achievements are what the altars of state rely upon.

sentences.zh: 臣聞賊徒破膽，皆無守心。

translations.literal: I hear the rebel bandits' courage is broken and they all lack the will to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the rebel bandits' courage is broken and they all lack the will to hold out.

sentences.zh: 若因其兵威，可以一舉破賊；

translations.literal: If we use his military prestige, we can destroy the rebels in one stroke;
translations.idiomatic: If we use his military prestige, we can destroy the rebels in one stroke;

sentences.zh: 今若許其朝覲，則必賜宴，賜宴則留連，使賊得京城，則從容完備，恐難圖之。

translations.literal: if we now permit him to attend court, he will surely be given a banquet; given a banquet he will linger, and while the rebels hold the capital they will leisurely make complete preparations—I'm afraid it will be hard to deal with them.
translations.idiomatic: if we now permit him to attend court, he will surely be given a banquet; given a banquet he will linger, and while the rebels hold the capital they will leisurely make complete preparations—I'm afraid it will be hard to deal with them.

sentences.zh: 不如使懷光乘勝進收京城，破竹之勢，不可失也。」

translations.literal: Better to have Huaiguang advance while victory is at hand and recover the capital—the momentum of splitting bamboo cannot be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Better to have Huaiguang advance while victory is at hand and recover the capital—the momentum of splitting bamboo cannot be lost."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，乃詔懷光率眾屯便橋，克期齊進。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and ordered Huaiguang to lead his troops to camp at Bian Bridge, with a set date for a joint advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered Huaiguang to lead his troops to camp at Bian Bridge, with a set date for a joint advance.

sentences.zh: 懷光大怒，遂謀異志，德宗方悟為杞所構。

translations.literal: Huaiguang was greatly angered and then plotted disloyalty; Dezong only then realized he had been framed by Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was greatly angered and then plotted disloyalty; Dezong only then realized he had been framed by Qi.

sentences.zh: 物議喧騰，歸咎於杞，乃貶為新州司馬，白誌貞恩州司馬，趙贊為播州司馬。

translations.literal: Public discussion seethed and blamed Qi; he was demoted to military advisor of Xin Prefecture, Bai Zhizhen to military advisor of En Prefecture, and Zhao Zan to military advisor of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Public discussion seethed and blamed Qi; he was demoted to military advisor of Xin Prefecture, Bai Zhizhen to military advisor of En Prefecture, and Zhao Zan to military advisor of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，移吉州長史。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was granted, he was transferred to chief administrator of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty was granted, he was transferred to chief administrator of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在貶所謂人曰：「吾必再入用。」

translations.literal: At his place of demotion he told people: "I shall certainly be employed again."
translations.idiomatic: At his place of demotion he told people, "I shall certainly be employed again."

sentences.zh: 是日，上果用杞為饒州刺史。

translations.literal: That very day the emperor indeed appointed Qi prefect of Rao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That very day the emperor indeed appointed Qi prefect of Rao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 給事中袁高宿直，當草杞制，遂執以謁宰相盧翰、劉從一曰：「杞作相三年，矯誣陰賊，排斥忠良，朋附者咳唾立至青雲，睚眥者顧盼已擠溝壑。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretariat Drafter Yuan Gao was on night duty and was to draft Qi's appointment; he took it and went to see chancellors Lu Han and Liu Congyi, saying: "Qi served as chancellor for three years, fabricating slander and harming in secret, expelling the loyal and good; those who joined his faction rose to the clouds with a spit, while those who crossed him in a glance were already pushed into the ditch.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretariat Drafter Yuan Gao was on night duty and was to draft Qi's appointment; he took it and went to see chancellors Lu Han and Liu Congyi, saying, "Qi served as chancellor for three years, fabricating slander and harming in secret, expelling the loyal and good; those who joined his faction rose to the clouds with a spit, while those who crossed him in a glance were already pushed into the ditch.

sentences.zh: 傲很背德，反亂天常，播越鑾輿，瘡痍天下，皆杞之為也。

translations.literal: Arrogant, harsh, and contrary to virtue, he overturned heaven's constants, drove the imperial carriage into exile, and wounded the realm—all was Qi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant, harsh, and contrary to virtue, he overturned heaven's constants, drove the imperial carriage into exile, and wounded the realm—all was Qi's doing.

sentences.zh: 幸免誅戮，唯示貶黜，尋已稍遷近地，更授大郡，恐失天下望，惟相公執奏之，事尚可救。」

translations.literal: He narrowly escaped execution and was only demoted; he has already been gradually moved to a nearer place and is again given a great prefecture—I fear the realm's hopes will be lost. I beg you, lords, to memorialize and hold firm; the matter can still be saved."
translations.idiomatic: He narrowly escaped execution and was only demoted; he has already been gradually moved to a nearer place and is again given a great prefecture—I fear the realm's hopes will be lost. I beg you, lords, to memorialize and hold firm; the matter can still be saved."

sentences.zh: 翰、從一不悅，遂改命舍人草制。

translations.literal: Han and Congyi were displeased and had a drafting official rewrite the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Congyi were displeased and had a drafting official rewrite the appointment.

sentences.zh: 明日詔下，袁高執奏曰：「盧杞為政，極恣兇惡，三軍將校，願食其肉，百辟卿士，嫉之若仇。」

translations.literal: The next day the edict was issued; Yuan Gao held it and memorialized, saying: "Lu Qi governed with the utmost wanton cruelty; the three armies' officers and men wished to eat his flesh, and the hundred ministers and courtiers hated him as an enemy."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the edict was issued; Yuan Gao held it and memorialized, saying, "Lu Qi governed with the utmost wanton cruelty; the three armies' officers and men wished to eat his flesh, and the hundred ministers and courtiers hated him as an enemy."

sentences.zh: 諫官趙需、裴佶、宇文炫、盧景亮、張薦等上疏曰：「伏以吉州長史盧杞，外矯儉簡，內藏奸邪，三年擅權，百揆失序，惡直醜正，亂國殄人，天地神祗所知，蠻夷華夏同棄。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials Zhao Xu, Pei Ji, Yuwen Xuan, Lu Jingliang, Zhang Jian, and others submitted a memorial, saying: "We submit that Chief Administrator Lu Qi of Ji Prefecture outwardly feigned frugality and simplicity while inwardly harbored treachery; for three years he monopolized power and the hundred offices lost order; he hated the upright and detested the good, throwing the state into chaos and destroying people—heaven and earth and the spirits know it, and barbarians and Chinese alike cast him off.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials Zhao Xu, Pei Ji, Yuwen Xuan, Lu Jingliang, Zhang Jian, and others submitted a memorial, saying, "We submit that Chief Administrator Lu Qi of Ji Prefecture outwardly feigned frugality and simplicity while inwardly harbored treachery; for three years he monopolized power and the hundred offices lost order; he hated the upright and detested the good, throwing the state into chaos and destroying people—heaven and earth and the spirits know it, and barbarians and Chinese alike cast him off.

sentences.zh: 伏惟故事，皆得上聞，自杞為相，要官大臣，動逾月不敢奏聞，百僚惴惴，常懼顛危。

translations.literal: We submit that by precedent all matters could reach the emperor's ears; since Qi became chancellor, important officials and great ministers often dared not memorialize for more than a month; the hundred officials were fearful, constantly dreading ruin.
translations.idiomatic: We submit that by precedent all matters could reach the emperor's ears; since Qi became chancellor, important officials and great ministers often dared not memorialize for more than a month; the hundred officials were fearful, constantly dreading ruin.

sentences.zh: 及京邑傾淪，皇輿播越，陛下炳然覺悟，出棄遐荒，制曰：『忠讜壅於上聞，朝野為之側目。』

translations.literal: When the capital fell and the imperial carriage was driven into exile, Your Majesty clearly awakened and cast him to the distant wilds, with an edict saying: 'Loyal remonstrance was blocked from reaching above, and court and countryside turned their eyes in dismay.'
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell and the imperial carriage was driven into exile, Your Majesty clearly awakened and cast him to the distant wilds, with an edict saying, 'Loyal remonstrance was blocked from reaching above, and court and countryside turned their eyes in dismay.'

sentences.zh: 由是忠良激勸，內外歡欣；

translations.literal: From this the loyal and good were stirred to effort and inside and outside rejoiced;
translations.idiomatic: From this the loyal and good were stirred to effort and inside and outside rejoiced;

sentences.zh: 今復用為饒州刺史，眾情失望，皆謂非宜。

translations.literal: now he is again appointed prefect of Rao Prefecture; public sentiment is disappointed and all say it is improper.
translations.idiomatic: now he is again appointed prefect of Rao Prefecture; public sentiment is disappointed and all say it is improper.

sentences.zh: 臣聞君之所以臨萬姓者，政也；

translations.literal: We have heard that what the ruler uses to face the myriad people is government;
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that what the ruler uses to face the myriad people is government;

sentences.zh: 萬姓之所以載君者，心也。

translations.literal: what the myriad people use to bear up the ruler is the heart.
translations.idiomatic: what the myriad people use to bear up the ruler is the heart.

sentences.zh: 倘加巨奸之寵，必失萬姓之心，乞回聖慈，遽輟新命。」

translations.literal: If great villainy is further favored, the myriad people's hearts will surely be lost; we beg Your Sacred Kindness to turn back and swiftly halt the new appointment."
translations.idiomatic: If great villainy is further favored, the myriad people's hearts will surely be lost; we beg Your Sacred Kindness to turn back and swiftly halt the new appointment."

sentences.zh: 疏奏不答。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted without reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted without reply.

sentences.zh: 諫官又論曰：「盧杞蒙蔽天聽，隳紊朝典，致亂危國，職杞之由，可謂公私巨蠹，中外棄物。

translations.literal: The remonstrating officials again argued: "Lu Qi deceived heaven's hearing, destroyed and disordered court regulations, brought chaos and endangered the state—the fault was Qi's; he may be called a great pest of public and private, cast off inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrating officials again argued, "Lu Qi deceived heaven's hearing, destroyed and disordered court regulations, brought chaos and endangered the state—the fault was Qi's; he may be called a great pest of public and private, cast off inside and outside.

sentences.zh: 自聞再加擢用，忠良痛骨，士庶寒心。

translations.literal: Since we heard of his further promotion, the loyal and good are pierced to the bone and scholars and commoners are chilled at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Since we heard of his further promotion, the loyal and good are pierced to the bone and scholars and commoners are chilled at heart.

sentences.zh: 臣昨者瀝肝上聞，冒死不恐，冀回宸睠，用快群情；

translations.literal: We yesterday poured out our livers and reported above, daring death without fear, hoping to turn back the imperial gaze and satisfy the feelings of the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: We yesterday poured out our livers and reported above, daring death without fear, hoping to turn back the imperial gaze and satisfy the feelings of the multitude;

sentences.zh: 至今拳拳，未奉聖旨，物議騰沸，行路驚嗟。

translations.literal: until now we remain earnest, yet have not received the sacred edict; public discussion boils, and travelers on the road gasp in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: until now we remain earnest, yet have not received the sacred edict; public discussion boils, and travelers on the road gasp in alarm.

sentences.zh: 人之無良，一至於此。

translations.literal: That men can be so devoid of conscience reaches this point.
translations.idiomatic: That men can be so devoid of conscience reaches this point.

sentences.zh: 伏乞俯從眾望，永棄奸臣。

translations.literal: We humbly beg you to follow the multitude's hope and forever cast off the wicked minister.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg you to follow the multitude's hope and forever cast off the wicked minister.

sentences.zh: 幸免誅夷，足明恩貸；

translations.literal: That he narrowly escaped execution is enough to show imperial grace;
translations.idiomatic: That he narrowly escaped execution is enough to show imperial grace;

sentences.zh: 特加榮寵，恐造禍階。

translations.literal: to add further honors and favor is to fear creating a source of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: to add further honors and favor is to fear creating a source of calamity.

sentences.zh: 臣等忝列諫司，今陳狂瞽。」

translations.literal: We, your remonstrating officials, now offer this reckless counsel."
translations.idiomatic: We, your remonstrating officials, now offer this reckless counsel."

sentences.zh: 給事中袁高堅執不下，乃改授澧州別駕。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretariat Drafter Yuan Gao firmly held and would not issue it; he was therefore changed to vice prefect of Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretariat Drafter Yuan Gao firmly held and would not issue it; he was therefore changed to vice prefect of Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 翌日延英，上謂臣曰：「朕欲授杞一小州刺史，可乎？」

translations.literal: The next day at Yanying the emperor said to his ministers: "I wish to appoint Qi prefect of a small prefecture—would that be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day at Yanying the emperor said to his ministers, "I wish to appoint Qi prefect of a small prefecture—would that be acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 李勉對曰：「陛下授杞大郡亦可，其如兆庶失望何？」

translations.literal: Li Mian replied: "Your Majesty may appoint Qi to a great prefecture as well—but what of the myriad people's disappointment?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian replied, "Your Majesty may appoint Qi to a great prefecture as well—but what of the myriad people's disappointment?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「眾人論杞奸邪，朕何不知？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Everyone says Qi is treacherous and wicked—how would I not know?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Everyone says Qi is treacherous and wicked—how would I not know?"

sentences.zh: 勉曰：「盧杞奸邪，天下人皆知；

translations.literal: Mian said: "Lu Qi is treacherous and wicked; everyone in the realm knows it—
translations.idiomatic: Mian said, "Lu Qi is treacherous and wicked; everyone in the realm knows it—

sentences.zh: 唯陛下不知，此所以為奸邪也！」

translations.literal: only Your Majesty does not know it; that is why he is treacherous and wicked!"
translations.idiomatic: only Your Majesty does not know it; that is why he is treacherous and wicked!"

sentences.zh: 德宗默然良久。

translations.literal: Dezong was silent for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was silent for a long while.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍李泌復對，上曰：「盧杞之事，朕已可袁高所奏，如何？」

translations.literal: Regular Attendant Li Bi again responded; the emperor said: "On the matter of Lu Qi, I have already approved Yuan Gao's memorial—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant Li Bi again responded; the emperor said, "On the matter of Lu Qi, I have already approved Yuan Gao's memorial—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 泌拜而言曰：「累日外人竊議，以陛下同漢之桓、靈；

translations.literal: Bi bowed and said: "For days outsiders have privately discussed, thinking Your Majesty like Han's Huan and Ling;
translations.idiomatic: Bi bowed and said, "For days outsiders have privately discussed, thinking Your Majesty like Han's Huan and Ling;

sentences.zh: 臣今親承聖旨，乃知堯、舜之不迨也！」

translations.literal: now I personally receive the sacred instruction and know that even Yao and Shun do not reach this!"
translations.idiomatic: now I personally receive the sacred instruction and know that even Yao and Shun do not reach this!"

sentences.zh: 德宗大悅，慰勉之。

translations.literal: Dezong was greatly pleased and comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was greatly pleased and comforted and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 杞尋卒於澧州。

translations.literal: Qi soon died at Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qi soon died at Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子元輔，字子望，少以清行聞於時。

translations.literal: His son Yuanfu, styled Ziwang, was known in his youth for upright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanfu, styled Ziwang, was known in his youth for upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 進士擢第，授崇文館校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed collator of the Chongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed collator of the Chongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 德宗思杞不已，乃求其後，特恩拜左拾遺，再遷左司員外郎，歷杭、常、絳三州刺史。

translations.literal: Dezong missed Qi without cease and sought his descendants; by special grace Yuanfu was appointed Left Reminder, then promoted to Left Department staff member, and served as prefect of Hang, Chang, and Jiang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong missed Qi without cease and sought his descendants; by special grace Yuanfu was appointed Left Reminder, then promoted to Left Department staff member, and served as prefect of Hang, Chang, and Jiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 以課最高，征為吏部郎中，遷給事中，改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Because his administrative ratings were highest, he was summoned as director of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to supervising secretariat drafter, and changed to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Because his administrative ratings were highest, he was summoned as director of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to supervising secretariat drafter, and changed to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 自兵部侍郎出為華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍等使，復為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: From Vice Minister of War he went out as prefect of Hua Prefecture, defender of Tong Pass, and commander of the Zhenguo Army and related forces; he again became Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: From Vice Minister of War he went out as prefect of Hua Prefecture, defender of Tong Pass, and commander of the Zhenguo Army and related forces; he again became Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 元輔自祖至曾，以名節著於史冊。

translations.literal: From his grandfather to his great-grandfather, their reputations for integrity were recorded in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: From his grandfather to his great-grandfather, their reputations for integrity were recorded in the histories.

sentences.zh: 元輔簡絜貞方，綽繼門風，歷踐清貫，人亦不以父之醜行為累，人士歸美。

translations.literal: Yuanfu was simple, pure, and upright, broadly continuing the family tradition; he passed through pure offices, and people did not hold his father's ugly conduct against him—scholars praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu was simple, pure, and upright, broadly continuing the family tradition; he passed through pure offices, and people did not hold his father's ugly conduct against him—scholars praised him.

sentences.zh: 大和三年八月卒，時年五十六。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Dahe he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Dahe he died, aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 白誌貞者，太原人，本名琇珪。

translations.literal: Bai Zhizhen was a native of Taiyuan; his original name was Xiugui.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zhizhen was a native of Taiyuan; his original name was Xiugui.

sentences.zh: 出於胥吏，事節度使李光弼，小心勤恪，動多計數，光弼深委信之，帳中之事，與琇珪參決。

translations.literal: Coming from clerical ranks, he served military commissioner Li Guangbi with careful diligence and many stratagems; Guangbi deeply entrusted him, and matters within the headquarters were decided with Xiugui's participation.
translations.idiomatic: Coming from clerical ranks, he served military commissioner Li Guangbi with careful diligence and many stratagems; Guangbi deeply entrusted him, and matters within the headquarters were decided with Xiugui's participation.

sentences.zh: 代宗素知之，光弼薨後，用為司農少卿，遷太卿，在寺十余年。

translations.literal: Daizong had long known him; after Guangbi died he was used as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries, promoted to Director, and served in that office for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong had long known him; after Guangbi died he was used as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries, promoted to Director, and served in that office for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘗召見與語，引為腹心，遂用為神策軍使、檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，賜名誌貞。

translations.literal: Dezong once summoned and conversed with him, took him to his inner circle, and then appointed him commissioner of the Shence Army, Acting Regular Attendant of the Left and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and granted the name Zhizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong once summoned and conversed with him, took him to his inner circle, and then appointed him commissioner of the Shence Army, Acting Regular Attendant of the Left and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and granted the name Zhizhen.

sentences.zh: 善伺候上意，言無不從。

translations.literal: He was skilled at reading the emperor's intent; nothing he said went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at reading the emperor's intent; nothing he said went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，李希烈陷汝州，命誌貞為京城召募使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong Li Xilie seized Ru Prefecture; Zhizhen was ordered commissioner for recruiting in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianzhong Li Xilie seized Ru Prefecture; Zhizhen was ordered commissioner for recruiting in the capital.

sentences.zh: 時尚父子儀端王傅吳仲孺家財巨萬，以國家召募有急，懼不自安，乃上表請以子弟率奴客從軍，德宗嘉之，超授五品官。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Shang's son Guo Ziyi's heir as Prince of Duan, Wu Zhongru, had family wealth in the tens of millions; because the state urgently needed recruitment he feared for himself and therefore submitted a memorial requesting that his sons and younger brothers lead household slaves to join the army; Dezong commended this and exceptionally granted them fifth-rank offices.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Shang's son Guo Ziyi's heir as Prince of Duan, Wu Zhongru, had family wealth in the tens of millions; because the state urgently needed recruitment he feared for himself and therefore submitted a memorial requesting that his sons and younger brothers lead household slaves to join the army; Dezong commended this and exceptionally granted them fifth-rank offices.

sentences.zh: 由是誌貞請令節度、觀察、團練等使並嘗為是官者，令家出子弟甲馬從軍，亦與其男官。

translations.literal: From this Zhizhen requested that military commissioners, observation commissioners, and regimental commissioners who had once held such offices have their families send out sons and younger brothers with armor and horses to join the army, also granting their sons offices.
translations.idiomatic: From this Zhizhen requested that military commissioners, observation commissioners, and regimental commissioners who had once held such offices have their families send out sons and younger brothers with armor and horses to join the army, also granting their sons offices.

sentences.zh: 是時豪家不肖子幸之，貧而有知者苦之。

translations.literal: At that time unworthy sons of great families were pleased; the poor who had understanding suffered.
translations.idiomatic: At that time unworthy sons of great families were pleased; the poor who had understanding suffered.

sentences.zh: 自是京師人心搖震，不保家室。

translations.literal: From this the hearts of the capital were shaken and households could not be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: From this the hearts of the capital were shaken and households could not be preserved.

sentences.zh: 時禁軍募致，悉委誌貞，兩軍應赴京師，殺傷殆盡，都不奏聞，皆以京師沽販之徒以填其闕。

translations.literal: At that time recruitment for the forbidden armies was entirely entrusted to Zhizhen; the two armies that should have gone to the capital were nearly all killed and wounded, yet he did not report to the court and filled their vacancies with peddlers from the capital markets.
translations.idiomatic: At that time recruitment for the forbidden armies was entirely entrusted to Zhizhen; the two armies that should have gone to the capital were nearly all killed and wounded, yet he did not report to the court and filled their vacancies with peddlers from the capital markets.

sentences.zh: 其人皆在市廛，及涇師犯闕，詔誌貞以神策軍拒賊，無人至者，上無以禦寇，乃圖出幸。

translations.literal: These men were all in the markets; when the Jing army attacked the capital the emperor ordered Zhizhen to use the Shence Army to resist the rebels, but no one came; the emperor had no means to repel the enemy and then planned flight.
translations.idiomatic: These men were all in the markets; when the Jing army attacked the capital the emperor ordered Zhizhen to use the Shence Army to resist the rebels, but no one came; the emperor had no means to repel the enemy and then planned flight.

sentences.zh: 時令狐建以龍武軍四百人從駕至奉天，仍以誌貞為行在都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: At that time Linghu Jian led four hundred Dragon Martial troops to follow the emperor to Fengtian, and Zhizhen was still made director of military affairs at the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Linghu Jian led four hundred Dragon Martial troops to follow the emperor to Fengtian, and Zhizhen was still made director of military affairs at the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 聞李懷光至，恐暴揚其罪，乃與盧杞同沮懷光入朝，眾議喧沸，言致播遷，盧杞、誌貞之罪也。

translations.literal: When he heard Li Huaiguang had arrived, fearing his crimes would be exposed, he joined Lu Qi in obstructing Huaiguang's audience at court; public discussion boiled, saying the displacement was the fault of Lu Qi and Zhizhen.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Li Huaiguang had arrived, fearing his crimes would be exposed, he joined Lu Qi in obstructing Huaiguang's audience at court; public discussion boiled, saying the displacement was the fault of Lu Qi and Zhizhen.

sentences.zh: 故與杞同貶，遇赦量移閬州別駕。

translations.literal: Therefore he was demoted together with Qi; when an amnesty was granted he was transferred by measure to vice prefect of Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he was demoted together with Qi; when an amnesty was granted he was transferred by measure to vice prefect of Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，遷果州刺史，宰臣李勉及諫官表疏論列，言誌貞與盧杞罪均，未宜敘用，固執不許，凡旬日，方下其詔。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he was transferred to prefect of Guo Prefecture; Chancellor Li Mian and remonstrating officials submitted memorials arguing that Zhizhen's crime equaled Qi's and he should not yet be reemployed; they held firm and it was not permitted; only after ten days was the edict issued.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan he was transferred to prefect of Guo Prefecture; Chancellor Li Mian and remonstrating officials submitted memorials arguing that Zhizhen's crime equaled Qi's and he should not yet be reemployed; they held firm and it was not permitted; only after ten days was the edict issued.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，遷潤州刺史、兼御史大夫、浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan he was transferred to prefect of Run Prefecture, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Zhexi observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan he was transferred to prefect of Run Prefecture, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Zhexi observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是年六月卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year he died.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡，河東人。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling was a native of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父旭，和州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xu was prefect of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu was prefect of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 延齡，乾元末為汜水縣尉，遇東都陷賊，因寓居鄂州，綴緝裴骃所註《史記》之闕遺，自號小裴。

translations.literal: Yanling, at the end of the Qianyuan era, was bailiff of Sishui County; when the Eastern Capital fell to rebels he lodged in E Prefecture, patching gaps in Pei Yin's commentary on the Records of the Grand Historian, styling himself Little Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling, at the end of the Qianyuan era, was bailiff of Sishui County; when the Eastern Capital fell to rebels he lodged in E Prefecture, patching gaps in Pei Yin's commentary on the Records of the Grand Historian, styling himself Little Pei.

sentences.zh: 後華州刺史董晉辟為防禦判官；

translations.literal: Later Hua Prefecture governor Dong Jin recruited him as defense aide;
translations.idiomatic: Later Hua Prefecture governor Dong Jin recruited him as defense aide;

sentences.zh: 黜陟使薦其能，調授太常博士。

translations.literal: the touring commissioner recommended his ability and he was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: the touring commissioner recommended his ability and he was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 盧杞為相，擢為膳部員外郎、集賢院直學士，改祠部郎中。

translations.literal: When Lu Qi was chancellor he was promoted to staff member of the Ministry of Rites and direct scholar of the Jixian Academy, then changed to director of the Ministry of Sacrificial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qi was chancellor he was promoted to staff member of the Ministry of Rites and direct scholar of the Jixian Academy, then changed to director of the Ministry of Sacrificial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 崔造作相，改易度支之務，令延齡知東都度支院。

translations.literal: When Cui Zao became chancellor he changed the Department of Public Works' affairs and had Yanling manage the Eastern Capital branch of the Department of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Zao became chancellor he changed the Department of Public Works' affairs and had Yanling manage the Eastern Capital branch of the Department of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 及韓滉領度支，召赴京，守本官，延齡不待詔命，遽入集賢院視事。

translations.literal: When Han Huang took charge of the Department of Public Works he summoned Yanling to the capital to keep his original office; Yanling did not await the edict and hurried into the Jixian Academy to attend to business.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Huang took charge of the Department of Public Works he summoned Yanling to the capital to keep his original office; Yanling did not await the edict and hurried into the Jixian Academy to attend to business.

sentences.zh: 宰相延賞惡其輕率，出為昭應令，與京兆尹鄭叔則論辨是非，攻訐叔則之短。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yanshang disliked his frivolity and had him sent out as magistrate of Zhaoying, where he debated right and wrong with metropolitan magistrate Zheng Shize and attacked Shize's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yanshang disliked his frivolity and had him sent out as magistrate of Zhaoying, where he debated right and wrong with metropolitan magistrate Zheng Shize and attacked Shize's faults.

sentences.zh: 時李泌為相，厚於叔則；

translations.literal: At that time Li Mi was chancellor and was close to Shize;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Mi was chancellor and was close to Shize;

sentences.zh: 中丞竇參恃恩寵，惡泌而佑延齡。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Dou Can, relying on imperial favor, hated Mi and supported Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Dou Can, relying on imperial favor, hated Mi and supported Yanling.

sentences.zh: 叔則坐貶為永州刺史，延齡改著作郎。

translations.literal: Shize was demoted to prefect of Yong Prefecture, and Yanling was changed to Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shize was demoted to prefect of Yong Prefecture, and Yanling was changed to Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 竇參尋作相，用為太府少卿，轉司農少卿。

translations.literal: Dou Can soon became chancellor and had Yanling appointed Vice Director of the Grand Treasury, then transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can soon became chancellor and had Yanling appointed Vice Director of the Grand Treasury, then transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Grain.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年，班宏卒，以延齡守本官，權領度支。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan, Ban Hong died, and Yanling was ordered to keep his original office and act as head of the Department of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan, Ban Hong died, and Yanling was ordered to keep his original office and act as head of the Department of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 自揣不通殖貨之務，乃多設鉤距，召度支老吏與謀，以求恩顧，乃奏云：「天下每年出入錢物，新陳相因，常不減六七千萬貫，唯有一庫，差舛散失，莫可知之。

translations.literal: Reflecting that he did not understand the business of accumulating wealth, he set many traps and summoned veteran clerks of the Department of Public Works to plot with him, seeking imperial favor; he then memorialized: "Each year the realm's incoming and outgoing funds and goods, old and new succeeding one another, regularly amount to no less than sixty or seventy million strings, yet there is only one treasury in which discrepancies and losses scatter and disappear, and none can know what becomes of them.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that he did not understand the business of accumulating wealth, he set many traps and summoned veteran clerks of the Department of Public Works to plot with him, seeking imperial favor; he then memorialized, "Each year the realm's incoming and outgoing funds and goods, old and new succeeding one another, regularly amount to no less than sixty or seventy million strings, yet there is only one treasury in which discrepancies and losses scatter and disappear, and none can know what becomes of them.

sentences.zh: 請於左藏庫中分置別庫：欠、負、耗、剩等庫及季庫、月庫，納諸色錢物。」

translations.literal: I request that within the Left Treasury separate treasuries be established: treasuries for deficit, debt, waste, surplus, and the like, as well as seasonal and monthly treasuries, to receive funds and goods of every kind."
translations.idiomatic: I request that within the Left Treasury separate treasuries be established: treasuries for deficit, debt, waste, surplus, and the like, as well as seasonal and monthly treasuries, to receive funds and goods of every kind."

sentences.zh: 上皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 且欲多張名目以惑上聽，其實於錢物更無增加，唯虛費簿書、人吏耳。

translations.literal: He also wished to multiply categories to confuse what the emperor heard; in fact there was no increase in funds or goods—only a wasteful expenditure of ledgers and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to multiply categories to confuse what the emperor heard; in fact there was no increase in funds or goods—only a wasteful expenditure of ledgers and clerks.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷戶部侍郎、判度支，奏請令京兆府以兩稅青苗錢市草百萬圍送苑中。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent director of the Department of Public Works, and memorialized requesting that the metropolitan government use green-shoot money from the two-tax system to purchase a million bundles of fodder for delivery to the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent director of the Department of Public Works, and memorialized requesting that the metropolitan government use green-shoot money from the two-tax system to purchase a million bundles of fodder for delivery to the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 宰相陸贄、趙憬議，以為：「若市送百萬圍草，即一府百姓，自冬歷夏，般載不了，百役供應，須悉停罷，又妨奪農務。

translations.literal: Chancellors Lu Zhi and Zhao Jing discussed the matter and said: "If the metropolitan government were to purchase and deliver a million bundles of fodder, then the people of that one prefecture, from winter through summer, could not finish transporting them; all corvée labor and supply services would have to be halted, and farm work would also be obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Lu Zhi and Zhao Jing discussed the matter and said, "If the metropolitan government were to purchase and deliver a million bundles of fodder, then the people of that one prefecture, from winter through summer, could not finish transporting them; all corvée labor and supply services would have to be halted, and farm work would also be obstructed.

sentences.zh: 請令府縣量市三二萬圍，各貯側近處，他時要即支用。」

translations.literal: We request that the prefecture and counties purchase only twenty or thirty thousand bundles by measure and store them nearby, to be drawn upon when needed later."
translations.idiomatic: We request that the prefecture and counties purchase only twenty or thirty thousand bundles by measure and store them nearby, to be drawn upon when needed later."

sentences.zh: 京西有汙池卑濕處，時有蘆葦生焉，亦不過數畝，延齡乃奏曰：「廊馬冬月合在槽櫪秣飼，夏中即須牧放。

translations.literal: In the west of the capital there were foul pools in low, damp places where reeds sometimes grew, covering no more than a few acres; Yanling then memorialized: "The palace horses in winter should be kept in stalls and fed fodder; in midsummer they must be turned out to pasture.
translations.idiomatic: In the west of the capital there were foul pools in low, damp places where reeds sometimes grew, covering no more than a few acres; Yanling then memorialized, "The palace horses in winter should be kept in stalls and fed fodder; in midsummer they must be turned out to pasture.

sentences.zh: 臣近尋訪知長安、咸陽兩縣界有陂池數百頃，請以為內廊牧馬之地；

translations.literal: I have recently learned that on the border between Chang'an and Xianyang counties there are pools and marshes of several hundred qing; I request that they be made pasture for the inner palace horses;
translations.idiomatic: I have recently learned that on the border between Chang'an and Xianyang counties there are pools and marshes of several hundred qing; I request that they be made pasture for the inner palace horses;

sentences.zh: 且去京城十數里，與苑廊中無別。」

translations.literal: moreover they lie only a dozen or so li from the capital and are no different from the park and palace grounds."
translations.idiomatic: moreover they lie only a dozen or so li from the capital and are no different from the park and palace grounds."

sentences.zh: 上初信之，言於宰相，對曰：「恐必無此。」

translations.literal: At first the emperor believed him and spoke of it to the chancellors, who replied: "We fear there surely is nothing of the kind."
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor believed him and spoke of it to the chancellors, who replied, "We fear there surely is nothing of the kind."

sentences.zh: 上乃差官閱視，事皆虛妄，延齡既慚且怒。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent officials to inspect; everything proved false, and Yanling was both ashamed and angry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent officials to inspect; everything proved false, and Yanling was both ashamed and angry.

sentences.zh: 又誣奏李充為百姓妄請積年和市物價，特敕令折填，謂之「底折錢」。

translations.literal: He also falsely memorialized that Li Chong had had the people petition without cause for accumulated years of market prices for goods purchased by the state, and by special edict ordered reconciliation deductions, calling this "reconciliation deduction money."
translations.idiomatic: He also falsely memorialized that Li Chong had had the people petition without cause for accumulated years of market prices for goods purchased by the state, and by special edict ordered reconciliation deductions, calling this "reconciliation deduction money."

sentences.zh: 嘗因奏對請積年錢帛以實帑藏，上曰：「若為可得錢物？」

translations.literal: Once, during an audience memorial, he requested accumulated years of cash and silk to fill the treasury stores; the emperor asked: "How can funds and goods be obtained?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, during an audience memorial, he requested accumulated years of cash and silk to fill the treasury stores; the emperor asked, "How can funds and goods be obtained?"

sentences.zh: 延齡奏曰：「開元、天寶中，天下戶僅千萬，百司公務殷繁，官員尚或有闕；

translations.literal: Yanling memorialized: "In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, households throughout the realm numbered barely ten million; the hundred offices had abundant public business and officials were sometimes still lacking;
translations.idiomatic: Yanling memorialized, "In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, households throughout the realm numbered barely ten million; the hundred offices had abundant public business and officials were sometimes still lacking;

sentences.zh: 自兵興已來，戶口減耗大半，今一官可兼領數司。

translations.literal: since warfare arose, households and population have been reduced by more than half, and today one official can hold several offices concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: since warfare arose, households and population have been reduced by more than half, and today one official can hold several offices concurrently.

sentences.zh: 伏請自今已後，內外百司官闕，未須補置，收其闕官祿俸，以實帑藏。」

translations.literal: I respectfully request that from now on, whenever offices throughout the inner and outer administration are vacant, they need not be filled; collect the salaries of those vacant posts and use them to fill the treasury stores."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully request that from now on, whenever offices throughout the inner and outer administration are vacant, they need not be filled; collect the salaries of those vacant posts and use them to fill the treasury stores."

sentences.zh: 後因對事，上謂延齡曰：「朕所居浴堂院殿一栿，以年多之故，似有損蠹，欲換之未能。」

translations.literal: Later, during discussion of affairs, the emperor said to Yanling: "One rafter in the hall of the Bathing Hall courtyard where I dwell, because of its many years, seems damaged by rot and insects; I wish to replace it but have not yet been able."
translations.idiomatic: Later, during discussion of affairs, the emperor said to Yanling, "One rafter in the hall of the Bathing Hall courtyard where I dwell, because of its many years, seems damaged by rot and insects; I wish to replace it but have not yet been able."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「宗廟事至重，殿栿事至輕。

translations.literal: He replied: "Affairs of the ancestral temple are supremely weighty; a hall rafter is supremely light.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Affairs of the ancestral temple are supremely weighty; a hall rafter is supremely light.

sentences.zh: 況陛下自有本分錢物，用之不竭。」

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty has your own allotted funds and goods, which in use are inexhaustible."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty has your own allotted funds and goods, which in use are inexhaustible."

sentences.zh: 上驚曰：「本分錢何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and asked: "What are allotted funds?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled and asked, "What are allotted funds?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此是經義證據，愚儒常材不能知，陛下正合問臣，唯臣知之。

translations.literal: He replied: "This has proof in the meaning of the classics; foolish Confucians of ordinary talent cannot know it. Your Majesty should properly ask me, for I alone know it.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "This has proof in the meaning of the classics; foolish Confucians of ordinary talent cannot know it. Your Majesty should properly ask me, for I alone know it.

sentences.zh: 準《禮經》，天下賦稅當為三分：一分充乾豆，一分充賓客，一分充君之庖廚。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Rites, the realm's taxes and levies should be divided into three parts: one part for dried sacrificial meats, one part for guests, and one part for the ruler's kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Book of Rites, the realm's taxes and levies should be divided into three parts: one part for dried sacrificial meats, one part for guests, and one part for the ruler's kitchen.

sentences.zh: 乾豆者，供宗廟也。

translations.literal: Dried sacrificial meats supply the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Dried sacrificial meats supply the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 今陛下奉宗廟，雖至敬至嚴，至豐至厚，亦不能一分財物也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty serves the ancestral temple with utmost reverence and strictness, utmost abundance and generosity, yet even so you cannot use one part of the funds and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty serves the ancestral temple with utmost reverence and strictness, utmost abundance and generosity, yet even so you cannot use one part of the funds and goods.

sentences.zh: 只如鴻臚禮賓、諸國蕃客，至於回紇馬價，用一分錢物，尚有贏羨甚多。

translations.literal: Take only the Grand Master of Ceremonies receiving guests and the various foreign envoys—even for Uyghur horse prices, if one part of funds and goods were used, there would still be a great surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Take only the Grand Master of Ceremonies receiving guests and the various foreign envoys—even for Uyghur horse prices, if one part of funds and goods were used, there would still be a great surplus.

sentences.zh: 況陛下禦膳宮廚皆極簡儉，所用外分賜百官充俸料、飧錢等，猶未能盡。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty's imperial meals and palace kitchens are all extremely simple and frugal; of what is used, the portion distributed outside to the hundred officials as salary and meal money and the like still cannot be fully spent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty's imperial meals and palace kitchens are all extremely simple and frugal; of what is used, the portion distributed outside to the hundred officials as salary and meal money and the like still cannot be fully spent.

sentences.zh: 據此而言，庖廚者之余，其數尚多，皆陛下本分也。

translations.literal: Judging by this, the remainder from the kitchen portion is still great in number—all of it is Your Majesty's allotted share.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by this, the remainder from the kitchen portion is still great in number—all of it is Your Majesty's allotted share.

sentences.zh: 用修數十殿亦不合疑慮，何況一栿。」

translations.literal: Using it to repair several dozen halls should not give rise to doubt; how much less one rafter."
translations.idiomatic: Using it to repair several dozen halls should not give rise to doubt; how much less one rafter."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「經義如此，人總不曾言之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The meaning of the classics is like this; no one has ever spoken of it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The meaning of the classics is like this; no one has ever spoken of it."

sentences.zh: 頷之而已。

translations.literal: He nodded and said no more.
translations.idiomatic: He nodded and said no more.

sentences.zh: 又因計料造神龍寺，須長五十尺松木，延齡奏曰：「臣近於同州檢得一谷木，可數千條，皆長八十尺。」

translations.literal: Again, when calculating materials to build Shenlong Temple, pine timbers fifty feet long were needed; Yanling memorialized: "I have recently inspected a valley in Tong Prefecture and found timber numbering several thousand pieces, all eighty feet long."
translations.idiomatic: Again, when calculating materials to build Shenlong Temple, pine timbers fifty feet long were needed; Yanling memorialized, "I have recently inspected a valley in Tong Prefecture and found timber numbering several thousand pieces, all eighty feet long."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「人言開元、天寶中側近求覓長五六十尺木，尚未易，須於嵐、勝州采市，如今何為近處便有此木？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "People say that in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, when those nearby sought timbers fifty or sixty feet long, it was still not easy and one had to procure them in Lan and Sheng prefectures; how is it that such timber exists nearby now?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "People say that in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, when those nearby sought timbers fifty or sixty feet long, it was still not easy and one had to procure them in Lan and Sheng prefectures; how is it that such timber exists nearby now?"

sentences.zh: 延齡奏曰：「臣聞賢材、珍寶、異物，皆在處常有，但遇聖君即出見。

translations.literal: Yanling memorialized: "I have heard that worthy timber, precious treasures, and rare things exist everywhere; they appear only when they meet a sage ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling memorialized, "I have heard that worthy timber, precious treasures, and rare things exist everywhere; they appear only when they meet a sage ruler.

sentences.zh: 今此木生關輔，蓋為聖君，豈開元、天寶合得有也！」

translations.literal: Now this timber grows in the Guanzhong region—it is because there is a sage ruler; how could Kaiyuan and Tianbao have deserved to possess it!"
translations.idiomatic: Now this timber grows in the Guanzhong region—it is because there is a sage ruler; how could Kaiyuan and Tianbao have deserved to possess it!"

sentences.zh: 時陸贄秉政，上素所禮重，每於延英極論其誕妄，不可令掌財賦。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Zhi held power; the emperor had always honored and valued him, and at every Yanying audience argued at length that Yanling's claims were absurd and that he must not be allowed to manage finances.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lu Zhi held power; the emperor had always honored and valued him, and at every Yanying audience argued at length that Yanling's claims were absurd and that he must not be allowed to manage finances.

sentences.zh: 德宗以為排擯，待延齡益厚。

translations.literal: Dezong thought this was factional exclusion and treated Yanling all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong thought this was factional exclusion and treated Yanling all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 贄上書疏其失曰：

translations.literal: Lu Zhi submitted a memorial detailing his faults:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi submitted a memorial detailing his faults:

sentences.zh: 總制邦用，度支是司；

translations.literal: Overall control of state expenditure is the charge of the Department of Public Works;
translations.idiomatic: Overall control of state expenditure is the charge of the Department of Public Works;

sentences.zh: 出納貨財，太府攸職。

translations.literal: receipt and disbursement of funds and goods is the duty of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: receipt and disbursement of funds and goods is the duty of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 凡是太府出納，皆稟度支文符，太府依符以奉行，度支憑案以勘覆，互相關鍵，用絕奸欺。

translations.literal: All disbursements from the Grand Treasury are authorized by documents from the Department of Public Works; the Grand Treasury follows the documents in execution, and the Department of Public Works relies on the records for audit and verification—they interlock with one another to cut off fraud.
translations.idiomatic: All disbursements from the Grand Treasury are authorized by documents from the Department of Public Works; the Grand Treasury follows the documents in execution, and the Department of Public Works relies on the records for audit and verification—they interlock with one another to cut off fraud.

sentences.zh: 其出納之數，則每旬申聞；

translations.literal: As for the numbers disbursed, they are reported every ten days;
translations.idiomatic: As for the numbers disbursed, they are reported every ten days;

sentences.zh: 見在之數，則每月計奏。

translations.literal: as for the numbers on hand, they are calculated and memorialized every month.
translations.idiomatic: as for the numbers on hand, they are calculated and memorialized every month.

sentences.zh: 皆經度支勾覆，又有御史監臨，旬旬相承，月月相繼。

translations.literal: All pass through audit by the Department of Public Works, and censors also supervise; ten-day periods succeed one another, month follows month.
translations.idiomatic: All pass through audit by the Department of Public Works, and censors also supervise; ten-day periods succeed one another, month follows month.

sentences.zh: 明若指掌，端如貫珠，財貨多少，無容隱漏。

translations.literal: Clear as though in the palm of the hand, aligned like beads on a string—how much wealth there is admits no concealment or leakage.
translations.idiomatic: Clear as though in the palm of the hand, aligned like beads on a string—how much wealth there is admits no concealment or leakage.

sentences.zh: 延齡務行邪諂，公肆誣欺，遂奏雲「左藏庫司多有失落，近因檢閱使置簿書，乃於糞土之中收得十三萬兩，其匹段雜貨又百萬有余，皆是文帳脫遺，並同已棄之物。

translations.literal: Yanling devoted himself to wicked flattery and openly practiced false accusation; he then memorialized that "the Left Treasury office had many losses; recently, because an inspection was ordered and ledgers were set up, one hundred thirty thousand taels were recovered from among filth and dust, and the bolts and miscellaneous goods numbered more than a million—all were items whose written accounts had been lost and were treated as already discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling devoted himself to wicked flattery and openly practiced false accusation; he then memorialized that "the Left Treasury office had many losses; recently, because an inspection was ordered and ledgers were set up, one hundred thirty thousand taels were recovered from among filth and dust, and the bolts and miscellaneous goods numbered more than a million—all were items whose written accounts had been lost and were treated as already discarded.

sentences.zh: 今所收獲，即是羨余，悉合移入雜庫，以供別敕支用者。」

translations.literal: What is now recovered is surplus; it should all be moved into the miscellaneous treasury to supply expenditures under separate edicts."
translations.idiomatic: What is now recovered is surplus; it should all be moved into the miscellaneous treasury to supply expenditures under separate edicts."

sentences.zh: 其時特宣進止，並依所奏施行。
