translations.literal: At that time special orders were issued and everything was carried out as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: At that time special orders were issued and everything was carried out as memorialized.

sentences.zh: 太府卿韋少華抗疏上陳，殊不引伏，確稱「每月申奏，皆是見在數中，請令推尋，足驗奸詐。」

translations.literal: Grand Treasury Director Wei Shaohua submitted a forceful memorial and absolutely would not concede, firmly stating: "The monthly memorials are all among the numbers on hand; I request that this be traced and verified—it is enough to prove the fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Treasury Director Wei Shaohua submitted a forceful memorial and absolutely would not concede, firmly stating, "The monthly memorials are all among the numbers on hand; I request that this be traced and verified—it is enough to prove the fraud."

sentences.zh: 兩司既有論執，理須詳辦是非，陛下縱其妄欺，不加按問。

translations.literal: Since the two offices had a dispute, the rights and wrongs ought in principle to have been thoroughly adjudicated; yet Your Majesty indulged his false deceit and did not order investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Since the two offices had a dispute, the rights and wrongs ought in principle to have been thoroughly adjudicated; yet Your Majesty indulged his false deceit and did not order investigation.

sentences.zh: 以在庫之物為收獲之功，以常賦之財為羨余之費，罔上無畏，示人不慚，此又罪之大者也。

translations.literal: To treat goods already in the treasury as recovered achievement, and regular tax revenues as surplus expenditure—deceiving superiors without fear, showing others without shame—this too is among the greatest of crimes.
translations.idiomatic: To treat goods already in the treasury as recovered achievement, and regular tax revenues as surplus expenditure—deceiving superiors without fear, showing others without shame—this too is among the greatest of crimes.

sentences.zh: 國家府庫，出納有常，延齡險猾售奸，詭譎求媚，遂於左藏之內，分建六庫之名，意在別貯贏余，以奉人主私欲。

translations.literal: The state's treasuries have fixed rules for receipt and disbursement; Yanling, treacherous and cunning, sold his wickedness and sought favor with devious flattery, and so within the Left Treasury established the names of six treasuries, intending to store surplus separately to supply the ruler's private desires.
translations.idiomatic: The state's treasuries have fixed rules for receipt and disbursement; Yanling, treacherous and cunning, sold his wickedness and sought favor with devious flattery, and so within the Left Treasury established the names of six treasuries, intending to store surplus separately to supply the ruler's private desires.

sentences.zh: 曾不知王者之體，天下為家，國不足則取之於人，人不足則資之於國，在國為官物，在人為私財，何謂贏余，須別收貯？

translations.literal: He did not understand that the body of a king takes all under Heaven as his household: when the state lacks, it takes from the people; when the people lack, it supplies from the state—what is in the state is public property, what is with the people is private wealth; why speak of surplus and need separate storage?
translations.idiomatic: He did not understand that the body of a king takes all under Heaven as his household: when the state lacks, it takes from the people; when the people lack, it supplies from the state—what is in the state is public property, what is with the people is private wealth; why speak of surplus and need separate storage?

sentences.zh: 是必巧詐以變移官物，暴法以刻削私財，舍此二途，其將安取？

translations.literal: He must by artful fraud shift public goods, and by harsh law pare away private wealth—apart from these two paths, where else would he obtain them?
translations.idiomatic: He must by artful fraud shift public goods, and by harsh law pare away private wealth—apart from these two paths, where else would he obtain them?

sentences.zh: 陛下方務崇信，不加檢裁，姑務保持，曾無詰責。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is now bent on honoring trust and adds no inspection or judgment, merely seeking to preserve him and never inquiring or assigning blame.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is now bent on honoring trust and adds no inspection or judgment, merely seeking to preserve him and never inquiring or assigning blame.

sentences.zh: 延齡謂能蔽惑，不復懼思，奸威既沮於四方，憸態復行於內府。

translations.literal: Yanling thought he could conceal and beguile and no longer feared reflection; though his wicked authority was checked in the four quarters, his sly conduct again operated within the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling thought he could conceal and beguile and no longer feared reflection; though his wicked authority was checked in the four quarters, his sly conduct again operated within the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 由是蹂躪官屬，傾倒貨財，移東就西，便為課績，取此適彼，遂號羨余，愚弄朝廷，有同兒戲。

translations.literal: From this he trampled office-holders, overturned funds and goods, moved east to west and called it achievement in duty, took from here to suit there and then labeled it surplus—he fooled the court as though it were child's play.
translations.idiomatic: From this he trampled office-holders, overturned funds and goods, moved east to west and called it achievement in duty, took from here to suit there and then labeled it surplus—he fooled the court as though it were child's play.

sentences.zh: 夫理天下者，以義為本，以利為末，以人為本，以財為末，本盛則其末自舉，末大則其本必傾。

translations.literal: One who governs all under Heaven takes righteousness as root and profit as branch, takes people as root and wealth as branch; when the root flourishes the branches rise of themselves, when the branches grow large the root must topple.
translations.idiomatic: One who governs all under Heaven takes righteousness as root and profit as branch, takes people as root and wealth as branch; when the root flourishes the branches rise of themselves, when the branches grow large the root must topple.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，德義立而利用不豐，人庶安而財貨不給，因以喪邦失位者，未之有也。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present, when virtue and righteousness were established yet profit and utility were not abundant, when the people were secure yet funds and goods were not sufficient—because of this states were lost and thrones forfeited—there has never been such a case.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, when virtue and righteousness were established yet profit and utility were not abundant, when the people were secure yet funds and goods were not sufficient—because of this states were lost and thrones forfeited—there has never been such a case.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「不患寡而患不均，不患貧而患不安。」

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "Do not worry about scarcity but about unequal distribution; do not worry about poverty but about instability."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said, "Do not worry about scarcity but about unequal distribution; do not worry about poverty but about instability."

sentences.zh: 「有德必有人，有土必有土，有人必有財。」

translations.literal: "When virtue is deep, one is sure to have officers; when one has officers, one is sure to have territory; when one has territory, one is sure to have wealth."
translations.idiomatic: "When virtue is deep, one is sure to have officers; when one has officers, one is sure to have territory; when one has territory, one is sure to have wealth."

sentences.zh: 「百姓足，君孰與不足？」

translations.literal: "When the common people have enough, how can the ruler alone not have enough?"
translations.idiomatic: "When the common people have enough, how can the ruler alone not have enough?"

sentences.zh: 蓋謂此也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，德義不立而利用克宣，人庶不安而財貨可保，因以興邦固位者，未之有也。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present, when virtue and righteousness were not established yet profit and utility were fully deployed, when the people were not secure yet funds and goods could be preserved—because of this states rose and thrones were secured—there has never been such a case.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, when virtue and righteousness were not established yet profit and utility were fully deployed, when the people were not secure yet funds and goods could be preserved—because of this states rose and thrones were secured—there has never been such a case.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「財散則人聚，財聚則人散。」

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "When wealth is dispersed, people gather; when wealth is hoarded, people scatter."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said, "When wealth is dispersed, people gather; when wealth is hoarded, people scatter."

sentences.zh: 「與其有聚斂之臣，寧有盜臣。」

translations.literal: "Better to have a thieving minister than a grasping, levying minister."
translations.idiomatic: "Better to have a thieving minister than a grasping, levying minister."

sentences.zh: 無令侵削兆人，為天子取怨於下也。

translations.literal: Do not let the myriad people be pared away and the Son of Heaven gather resentment below.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let the myriad people be pared away and the Son of Heaven gather resentment below.

sentences.zh: 且陛下初膺寶歷，誌翦群兇，師旅繁興，征求浸廣，榷算侵剝，下無聊生。

translations.literal: Moreover when Your Majesty first received the imperial succession, you resolved to cut down the mass of villains; armies and campaigns arose in profusion, levies and exactions gradually widened, monopolies and calculations encroached and stripped away, and below the people had no means to live.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover when Your Majesty first received the imperial succession, you resolved to cut down the mass of villains; armies and campaigns arose in profusion, levies and exactions gradually widened, monopolies and calculations encroached and stripped away, and below the people had no means to live.

sentences.zh: 是以涇原叛徒，乘人怨咨，白晝犯闕，都邑甿庶，恬然不驚，反與賊眾相從，比肩而入宮殿。

translations.literal: Therefore the Jingyuan mutineers, riding on popular resentment, in broad daylight violated the palace; the common people of the capital, undisturbed and unalarmed, instead followed the rebel masses shoulder to shoulder into the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Jingyuan mutineers, riding on popular resentment, in broad daylight violated the palace; the common people of the capital, undisturbed and unalarmed, instead followed the rebel masses shoulder to shoulder into the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 雖蚩蚩之性，靡所不為，然亦由德澤未浹，而暴令驅之，以至於是也。

translations.literal: Though the nature of the ignorant permits every deed, it was also because virtue and grace had not soaked through and harsh orders drove them, until it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Though the nature of the ignorant permits every deed, it was also because virtue and grace had not soaked through and harsh orders drove them, until it came to this.

sentences.zh: 於時內府之積，尚如丘山，竟資兇渠，以餌貪卒，此則陛下躬睹之矣。

translations.literal: At that time the inner treasury's accumulations were still like hills and mountains, yet in the end they supplied the wicked ringleaders to feed the greedy soldiers—this Your Majesty saw with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the inner treasury's accumulations were still like hills and mountains, yet in the end they supplied the wicked ringleaders to feed the greedy soldiers—this Your Majesty saw with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 是乃失人而聚貨，夫何利之有焉！

translations.literal: This was losing the people while hoarding goods—what profit was there in it!
translations.idiomatic: This was losing the people while hoarding goods—what profit was there in it!

sentences.zh: 車駕既幸奏天，逆泚旋肆圍逼，一壘之內，萬乘所屯，窘如涸流，庶物空匱。

translations.literal: Once the imperial carriage had reached Fengtian, the rebel Zhu Ci soon laid siege at will; within one fortress the ten-thousand-chariot ruler was encamped, straitened as a dried-up stream, with all goods empty and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Once the imperial carriage had reached Fengtian, the rebel Zhu Ci soon laid siege at will; within one fortress the ten-thousand-chariot ruler was encamped, straitened as a dried-up stream, with all goods empty and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲發一健步出覘賊軍，其人懇以苦寒為辭，跪奏乞一襦袴，陛下為之求覓不致，竟閔默而遣之。

translations.literal: Once the emperor wished to send a strong runner to reconnoiter the rebel army; the man earnestly pleaded the bitter cold, knelt and memorialized begging for one padded jacket and trousers, and the emperor searched for them but could not obtain them—he finally sent him away in silent pity.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor wished to send a strong runner to reconnoiter the rebel army; the man earnestly pleaded the bitter cold, knelt and memorialized begging for one padded jacket and trousers, and the emperor searched for them but could not obtain them—he finally sent him away in silent pity.

sentences.zh: 又嘗宮壺之中，服用有闕，聖旨方戎事為急，不忍重煩於人，乃剝親王飾帶之金，賣以給直。

translations.literal: Again, within the palace stores there were lacks in what was worn and used; the sacred intent held military affairs urgent and could not bear to burden the people further, so the gold from a prince's ornamental belt was stripped off and sold to supply the price.
translations.idiomatic: Again, within the palace stores there were lacks in what was worn and used; the sacred intent held military affairs urgent and could not bear to burden the people further, so the gold from a prince's ornamental belt was stripped off and sold to supply the price.

sentences.zh: 是時行從將吏，赴難師徒，蒼黃奔馳，鹹未冬服，漸屬凝冱，且無薪蒸，饑凍內攻，矢石外迫。

translations.literal: At that time the accompanying generals and officials, the armies rushing to the crisis, fled in panic—salt for winter clothing had not yet been obtained, cold gradually set in, and there was no fuel; hunger and cold attacked within, arrows and stones pressed from without.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the accompanying generals and officials, the armies rushing to the crisis, fled in panic—salt for winter clothing had not yet been obtained, cold gradually set in, and there was no fuel; hunger and cold attacked within, arrows and stones pressed from without.

sentences.zh: 晝則荷戈奮迅，夜則映堞呻吟，淩風飈，冒霜雪，逾四旬而眾無攜貳，卒能走強賊、全危城者，陛下豈有嚴刑重賞使之然耶？

translations.literal: By day they shouldered weapons and fought fiercely; by night they groaned along the battlements, braving wind and storm, enduring frost and snow—for more than forty days the masses had no disloyalty, and in the end they could drive off the strong rebels and preserve the endangered city: did Your Majesty accomplish this through severe punishments and heavy rewards?
translations.idiomatic: By day they shouldered weapons and fought fiercely; by night they groaned along the battlements, braving wind and storm, enduring frost and snow—for more than forty days the masses had no disloyalty, and in the end they could drive off the strong rebels and preserve the endangered city: did Your Majesty accomplish this through severe punishments and heavy rewards?

sentences.zh: 唯以不厚其身，不藏其貨，與眾庶同其憂患，與士伍共其有無，乃能使人捐軀命而扞寇仇，餒之不離，凍之不憾，臨危而不易其守，見死而不去其君，所謂「聖人感人心而天下和平」，此其效也。

translations.literal: Only because you did not enrich yourself, did not hoard goods, shared the people's afflictions with the common multitude, and shared possessions with the soldiers—only thus could you make men give their lives to repel the enemy, not leave you when hungry, not resent you when frozen, not change their loyalty in peril, and not abandon their ruler when facing death; this is what is meant by "When the sage moves people's hearts, all under Heaven is at peace"—this was the effect.
translations.idiomatic: Only because you did not enrich yourself, did not hoard goods, shared the people's afflictions with the common multitude, and shared possessions with the soldiers—only thus could you make men give their lives to repel the enemy, not leave you when hungry, not resent you when frozen, not change their loyalty in peril, and not abandon their ruler when facing death; this is what is meant by "When the sage moves people's hearts, all under Heaven is at peace"—this was the effect.

sentences.zh: 及乎重圍既解，諸路稍通，賦稅漸臻，貢獻繼至，乃於行宮外廡之下，別置瓊林、大盈之司。

translations.literal: When the heavy siege was lifted and the various routes gradually opened, taxes and levies gradually arrived and tribute followed in succession; then beneath the outer galleries of the traveling palace separate offices of Qiongl in and Daying were established.
translations.idiomatic: When the heavy siege was lifted and the various routes gradually opened, taxes and levies gradually arrived and tribute followed in succession; then beneath the outer galleries of the traveling palace separate offices of Qiongl in and Daying were established.

sentences.zh: 未賞功勞，遽私賄玩，甚沮惟新之望，頗攜死義之心，於是輿誦興譏，而軍士始怨矣。

translations.literal: Merit had not yet been rewarded when private gifts and curiosities were hurriedly hoarded—greatly dampening hopes for renewal and deeply wounding hearts that had died for righteousness; from this public rumor rose in mockery, and the soldiers began to resent.
translations.idiomatic: Merit had not yet been rewarded when private gifts and curiosities were hurriedly hoarded—greatly dampening hopes for renewal and deeply wounding hearts that had died for righteousness; from this public rumor rose in mockery, and the soldiers began to resent.

sentences.zh: 財聚人散，不其然乎！

translations.literal: Wealth hoarded and people scattered—is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: Wealth hoarded and people scattered—is it not so!

sentences.zh: 旋屬蟊賊內興，翠華南狩，奉天所積財貨，悉復殲於亂軍。

translations.literal: Soon after, internal mutiny arose and the imperial carriage hunted south; the funds and goods accumulated at Fengtian were all again destroyed by the mutinous army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, internal mutiny arose and the imperial carriage hunted south; the funds and goods accumulated at Fengtian were all again destroyed by the mutinous army.

sentences.zh: 即遷岷、梁，日不暇給，獨憑大順，遂復皇都。

translations.literal: Then the court moved to Min and Liang; days allowed no respite, yet relying on great fortune it recovered the imperial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Then the court moved to Min and Liang; days allowed no respite, yet relying on great fortune it recovered the imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 是知天子者，以得人為資，以蓄義為富，人茍歸附，何患蔑資？

translations.literal: From this one knows that the Son of Heaven takes gaining people as his resource and storing righteousness as his wealth; if people submit, why worry about lacking resources?
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that the Son of Heaven takes gaining people as his resource and storing righteousness as his wealth; if people submit, why worry about lacking resources?

sentences.zh: 義茍修崇，何憂不富？

translations.literal: If righteousness is cultivated and honored, why fear not being rich?
translations.idiomatic: If righteousness is cultivated and honored, why fear not being rich?

sentences.zh: 豈在貯之內府，方為己有哉！

translations.literal: Must one store within the inner treasury before it counts as one's own?
translations.idiomatic: Must one store within the inner treasury before it counts as one's own?

sentences.zh: 故藏於天下者，天子之富也；

translations.literal: Therefore what is stored throughout all under Heaven is the Son of Heaven's wealth;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore what is stored throughout all under Heaven is the Son of Heaven's wealth;

sentences.zh: 藏於境內者，諸侯之富也；

translations.literal: what is stored within the borders is the feudal lords' wealth;
translations.idiomatic: what is stored within the borders is the feudal lords' wealth;

sentences.zh: 藏於囷倉篋櫝者，農夫、商賈之富也。

translations.literal: what is stored in granaries, chests, and coffers is the wealth of farmers and merchants.
translations.idiomatic: what is stored in granaries, chests, and coffers is the wealth of farmers and merchants.

sentences.zh: 奈何以天子之貴，海內之富，面猥行諸侯之棄德，守農商之鄙業哉！

translations.literal: How can one of the Son of Heaven's exalted rank and the wealth of the inner seas basely practice the discarded virtue of feudal lords and cling to the base occupation of farmers and merchants!
translations.idiomatic: How can one of the Son of Heaven's exalted rank and the wealth of the inner seas basely practice the discarded virtue of feudal lords and cling to the base occupation of farmers and merchants!

sentences.zh: 陛下若謂厚取可以恢武功，則建中之取既無成矣；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty thinks heavy taking can expand military achievement, then the taking of Jianzhong already achieved nothing;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty thinks heavy taking can expand military achievement, then the taking of Jianzhong already achieved nothing;

sentences.zh: 若謂多積可以為己有，則建中之積又不在矣；

translations.literal: if you think much hoarding can be kept for yourself, then the hoarding of Jianzhong is no longer there;
translations.idiomatic: if you think much hoarding can be kept for yourself, then the hoarding of Jianzhong is no longer there;

sentences.zh: 若謂徇欲不足傷理化，則建中之失傷已甚矣；

translations.literal: if you think indulging desire does not harm governance and transformation, then the harm of Jianzhong's failure is already very great;
translations.idiomatic: if you think indulging desire does not harm governance and transformation, then the harm of Jianzhong's failure is already very great;

sentences.zh: 若謂斂怨不足致危亡，則建中之亂危亦至矣！

translations.literal: if you think gathering resentment does not bring crisis and ruin, then the crisis and peril of Jianzhong's disorder have also arrived!
translations.idiomatic: if you think gathering resentment does not bring crisis and ruin, then the crisis and peril of Jianzhong's disorder have also arrived!

sentences.zh: 然而遽能靖滔天之禍，成中興之功者，良以陛下有側身修勵之誌，有罪己悔懼之辭，罷息誅求，敦尚節儉，渙發大號，與人更新；

translations.literal: Yet you were able swiftly to still heaven-high calamity and accomplish the achievement of restoration—truly because Your Majesty had the resolve to examine yourself and exert effort, words of self-blame and repentant fear, ceased punitive exactions, honored and upheld frugality, issued a great proclamation, and renewed yourself with the people;
translations.idiomatic: Yet you were able swiftly to still heaven-high calamity and accomplish the achievement of restoration—truly because Your Majesty had the resolve to examine yourself and exert effort, words of self-blame and repentant fear, ceased punitive exactions, honored and upheld frugality, issued a great proclamation, and renewed yourself with the people;

sentences.zh: 故靈祗感陛下之誠，臣庶感陛下之意，釋憾回慮，化危為安。

translations.literal: therefore the numinous powers were moved by Your Majesty's sincerity, officials and people were moved by Your Majesty's intent, resentments were released and thoughts turned back, and danger was transformed into peace.
translations.idiomatic: therefore the numinous powers were moved by Your Majesty's sincerity, officials and people were moved by Your Majesty's intent, resentments were released and thoughts turned back, and danger was transformed into peace.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦當為宗廟社稷建不拔之永圖，為子孫黎元立可久之休業，懲前事徇欲之失，復日新盛德之言；

translations.literal: Your Majesty should also for the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain establish an enduring plan that cannot be uprooted, and for sons and grandsons and the black-haired people establish a lasting foundation of repose; take warning from the past error of indulging desire and restore words of daily renewal in flourishing virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should also for the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain establish an enduring plan that cannot be uprooted, and for sons and grandsons and the black-haired people establish a lasting foundation of repose; take warning from the past error of indulging desire and restore words of daily renewal in flourishing virtue;

sentences.zh: 豈宜更縱憸邪，復行克暴，事之追悔，其可再乎！

translations.literal: how can you again indulge the sly and wicked and repeat harsh oppression—can regret for such matters happen twice!
translations.idiomatic: how can you again indulge the sly and wicked and repeat harsh oppression—can regret for such matters happen twice!

sentences.zh: 臣又竊慮陛下納彼盜言，墮其奸計，以為搏噬拏攫，怨集有司，積聚豐盈，利歸君上，是又大謬，所宜慎思。

translations.literal: Your subject also privately fears that Your Majesty may accept those thieving words and fall into that wicked scheme, thinking that seizing and plundering will concentrate resentment on the offices, while hoarding and filling will bring profit to the ruler above—this too is greatly mistaken and should be carefully considered.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject also privately fears that Your Majesty may accept those thieving words and fall into that wicked scheme, thinking that seizing and plundering will concentrate resentment on the offices, while hoarding and filling will bring profit to the ruler above—this too is greatly mistaken and should be carefully considered.

sentences.zh: 夫人主昏明，系於所任，咎繇、夔、契之道長，而虞舜享浚哲之名；

translations.literal: Whether a ruler is dull or clear depends on whom he employs; when the Way of Gao Yao, Kui, and Qi was long, Yu Shun enjoyed the name of profound wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: Whether a ruler is dull or clear depends on whom he employs; when the Way of Gao Yao, Kui, and Qi was long, Yu Shun enjoyed the name of profound wisdom;

sentences.zh: 皇甫、棸、楀之嬖行，而周厲嬰顛覆之禍。

translations.literal: when the favored conduct of Huangfu, Li, and Yu was practiced, King Li of Zhou met the calamity of overturning.
translations.idiomatic: when the favored conduct of Huangfu, Li, and Yu was practiced, King Li of Zhou met the calamity of overturning.

sentences.zh: 自古何嘗有小人柄用，而災患不及邦國者乎！

translations.literal: From antiquity, when has there ever been a case in which petty men held power yet calamity did not reach the state!
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, when has there ever been a case in which petty men held power yet calamity did not reach the state!

sentences.zh: 譬猶操兵以刃人，天下不委罪於兵而委罪於所操之主；

translations.literal: It is like wielding a weapon to cut people—all under Heaven does not lay blame on the weapon but lays blame on the one who wields it;
translations.idiomatic: It is like wielding a weapon to cut people—all under Heaven does not lay blame on the weapon but lays blame on the one who wields it;

sentences.zh: 畜蠱以殃物，天下不歸咎於蠱而歸咎於所畜之家；

translations.literal: like keeping poisonous insects to harm things—all under Heaven does not blame the poison but blames the household that keeps it;
translations.idiomatic: like keeping poisonous insects to harm things—all under Heaven does not blame the poison but blames the household that keeps it;

sentences.zh: 理有必然，不可不察。

translations.literal: the principle is necessarily so and cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: the principle is necessarily so and cannot go unexamined.

sentences.zh: 臣伏慮陛下以延齡之進，獨出宸衷，延齡之言，多順聖旨，今若以罪置辟，則似為眾所擠，故欲保持，用彰堅斷。

translations.literal: Your subject fears that because Yanling's advancement came solely from Your Majesty's inner intent and Yanling's words mostly accord with the sacred intent, if he were now punished and executed it would seem as though he were excluded by the multitude; therefore you wish to preserve him to display firm resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject fears that because Yanling's advancement came solely from Your Majesty's inner intent and Yanling's words mostly accord with the sacred intent, if he were now punished and executed it would seem as though he were excluded by the multitude; therefore you wish to preserve him to display firm resolution.

sentences.zh: 若然，陛下與人終始之意則美矣。

translations.literal: If so, Your Majesty's intent to see a person through from start to finish is admirable.
translations.idiomatic: If so, Your Majesty's intent to see a person through from start to finish is admirable.

sentences.zh: 其於改過勿吝、去邪勿疑之道，或未盡善。

translations.literal: Yet as to the Way of correcting faults without stinginess and removing the wicked without doubt, it may not yet be fully good.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as to the Way of correcting faults without stinginess and removing the wicked without doubt, it may not yet be fully good.

sentences.zh: 今希旨自默，浸以成風，獎之使言，猶懼不既，若又阻抑，誰當貢誠？

translations.literal: Now those who conform to the intent keep silent, and this gradually becomes custom; even when rewarded to speak, one still fears it is not enough—if you again obstruct and suppress, who will offer sincerity?
translations.idiomatic: Now those who conform to the intent keep silent, and this gradually becomes custom; even when rewarded to speak, one still fears it is not enough—if you again obstruct and suppress, who will offer sincerity?

sentences.zh: 或恐未亮斯言，請以一事為證。

translations.literal: Lest this statement not be understood, I request that one matter serve as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Lest this statement not be understood, I request that one matter serve as proof.

sentences.zh: 只如延齡兇妄，流布寰區，上自公卿近臣，下迨輿臺賤品，喧喧談議，億萬為徒，能以上言，其人有幾？

translations.literal: Take only Yanling's wicked falsehood, spread throughout the realm—from high ministers and close officials above to carriage attendants and lowly ranks below, clamorous talk and discussion, millions in number: how many are there who can memorialize above?
translations.idiomatic: Take only Yanling's wicked falsehood, spread throughout the realm—from high ministers and close officials above to carriage attendants and lowly ranks below, clamorous talk and discussion, millions in number: how many are there who can memorialize above?

sentences.zh: 陛下誠令親信博采輿詞，參較比來所聞，足鑒人間情偽。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly ordered trusted intimates broadly to gather public talk and compare what has been heard lately, it would be enough to mirror the truth and falsehood among the people.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly ordered trusted intimates broadly to gather public talk and compare what has been heard lately, it would be enough to mirror the truth and falsehood among the people.

sentences.zh: 臣以卑鄙，位當臺衡，既極崇高，又承渥澤。

translations.literal: Your subject, base and lowly, holds the post of chief minister—I have reached the utmost height and also receive generous grace.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, base and lowly, holds the post of chief minister—I have reached the utmost height and also receive generous grace.

sentences.zh: 豈不知觀時附會，足保舊恩，隨眾沈浮，免貽厚責。

translations.literal: Would I not know that observing the times and joining the crowd is enough to preserve old favor, and drifting with the multitude avoids heavy blame?
translations.idiomatic: Would I not know that observing the times and joining the crowd is enough to preserve old favor, and drifting with the multitude avoids heavy blame?

sentences.zh: 謝病黜退，獲知幾之名；

translations.literal: To plead illness and withdraw would win the name of knowing when to stop;
translations.idiomatic: To plead illness and withdraw would win the name of knowing when to stop;

sentences.zh: 黨奸茍容，無見嫉之患。

translations.literal: to party with the wicked and tolerate them would avoid the worry of arousing jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: to party with the wicked and tolerate them would avoid the worry of arousing jealousy.

sentences.zh: 何急自苦，獨當豺狼，上違歡情，下餌讒口。

translations.literal: Why urgently torment myself and alone confront wolves—going against favor above and feeding slander below?
translations.idiomatic: Why urgently torment myself and alone confront wolves—going against favor above and feeding slander below?

sentences.zh: 良以內顧庸昧，一無所堪，夙蒙眷知，唯以誠直，綢繆帷扆，一紀於茲，聖慈既襎此見容，愚臣亦以此自負。

translations.literal: Truly because looking inward I am mediocre and dull and capable of nothing, yet from old I have received gracious trust and rely only on sincerity and straightness; intimate counsel at the curtain for a full cycle until now—the sacred kindness has abundantly shown this tolerance, and your foolish subject also takes pride in this.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because looking inward I am mediocre and dull and capable of nothing, yet from old I have received gracious trust and rely only on sincerity and straightness; intimate counsel at the curtain for a full cycle until now—the sacred kindness has abundantly shown this tolerance, and your foolish subject also takes pride in this.

sentences.zh: 從陛下歷播遷之危，睹陛下致興復之難，至今追思，猶為心悸；

translations.literal: Following Your Majesty through the peril of displacement and witnessing the difficulty of your restoration—even now recalling it, my heart still trembles;
translations.idiomatic: Following Your Majesty through the peril of displacement and witnessing the difficulty of your restoration—even now recalling it, my heart still trembles;

sentences.zh: 所以畏覆車而駭慮，懼毀室而悲鳴，蓋情激於衷，雖欲罷而不能自默也！

translations.literal: therefore I fear the overturned cart and am alarmed in thought, fear the ruined house and cry out in grief—emotion stirred in the breast; though I wish to stop, I cannot keep silent!
translations.idiomatic: therefore I fear the overturned cart and am alarmed in thought, fear the ruined house and cry out in grief—emotion stirred in the breast; though I wish to stop, I cannot keep silent!

sentences.zh: 因事陳請，雖已頻煩，天聽尚高，未垂諒察，輒申悃款，以極愚誠。

translations.literal: Memorializing on affairs, though already frequent, the heavenly hearing is still high and has not yet granted understanding; I again declare my earnest sincerity to the utmost of foolish loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Memorializing on affairs, though already frequent, the heavenly hearing is still high and has not yet granted understanding; I again declare my earnest sincerity to the utmost of foolish loyalty.

sentences.zh: 憂深故語煩，意懇故詞切，以微臣自固之謀則過，於陛下慮患之計則忠。

translations.literal: Anxiety deep, therefore words are numerous; intent earnest, therefore terms are sharp—as a plan for your subject's self-preservation it is excessive, but as a plan for Your Majesty's consideration of peril it is loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Anxiety deep, therefore words are numerous; intent earnest, therefore terms are sharp—as a plan for your subject's self-preservation it is excessive, but as a plan for Your Majesty's consideration of peril it is loyal.

sentences.zh: 糜軀奉君，所不敢避；

translations.literal: To waste my body in serving the ruler is what I dare not avoid;
translations.idiomatic: To waste my body in serving the ruler is what I dare not avoid;

sentences.zh: 沽名衒直，亦不忍為。

translations.literal: to buy a name and parade straightness is also what I cannot bear to do.
translations.idiomatic: to buy a name and parade straightness is also what I cannot bear to do.

sentences.zh: 願回睿聰，為國熟慮，社稷是賴，豈唯微臣。

translations.literal: I wish that sagely understanding would turn back, that the state be deeply considered—the altars of soil and grain rely on this, not your subject alone.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that sagely understanding would turn back, that the state be deeply considered—the altars of soil and grain rely on this, not your subject alone.

sentences.zh: 書奏，德宗不悅，待延齡益厚。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Dezong was displeased and treated Yanling all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Dezong was displeased and treated Yanling all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 時鹽鐵轉運使張滂、京兆尹李充、司農卿李銛，以事相關，皆證延齡矯妄。

translations.literal: At that time Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Zhang Pang, metropolitan magistrate Li Chong, and Director of Grain Li Xian, because their affairs were connected, all testified to Yanling's falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Zhang Pang, metropolitan magistrate Li Chong, and Director of Grain Li Xian, because their affairs were connected, all testified to Yanling's falsehood.

sentences.zh: 德宗罷陸贄知政事，為太子賓客；

translations.literal: Dezong removed Lu Zhi from managing state affairs and made him Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: Dezong removed Lu Zhi from managing state affairs and made him Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent;

sentences.zh: 滂、充、銛悉罷職左遷。

translations.literal: Pang, Chong, and Xian were all dismissed from office and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Pang, Chong, and Xian were all dismissed from office and demoted.

sentences.zh: 十一年春暮，上數畋於苑中，時久旱，人情憂惴，延齡遽上疏曰：「陸贄、李充等失權，心懷怨望，今專大言於眾曰：『天下炎旱，人庶流亡，度支多欠闕諸軍糧草。』

translations.literal: In the late spring of the eleventh year, the emperor several times hunted in the park; the drought had been long and popular sentiment was anxious and fearful; Yanling hastily submitted a memorial: "Lu Zhi, Li Chong, and the others have lost power and harbor resentment; they now speak broadly to the masses: 'All under Heaven suffers scorching drought; the people flee and scatter; the Department of Public Works owes much in grain and fodder to the various armies.'
translations.idiomatic: In the late spring of the eleventh year, the emperor several times hunted in the park; the drought had been long and popular sentiment was anxious and fearful; Yanling hastily submitted a memorial, "Lu Zhi, Li Chong, and the others have lost power and harbor resentment; they now speak broadly to the masses, 'All under Heaven suffers scorching drought; the people flee and scatter; the Department of Public Works owes much in grain and fodder to the various armies.'

sentences.zh: 以激怒群情。」

translations.literal: —to inflame the feelings of the masses."
translations.idiomatic: —to inflame the feelings of the masses."

sentences.zh: 後數日，上又幸苑中，適會神策軍人訴度支欠廄馬芻草。

translations.literal: Several days later the emperor again visited the park and happened to meet Shence Army men complaining that the Department of Public Works owed fodder for stable horses.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the emperor again visited the park and happened to meet Shence Army men complaining that the Department of Public Works owed fodder for stable horses.

sentences.zh: 上思延齡言，即時回駕，下詔斥逐贄、充、滂、銛等，朝廷中外惴恐。

translations.literal: The emperor thought of Yanling's words, immediately turned the carriage back, and issued an edict expelling Zhi, Chong, Pang, Xian, and the others; throughout the court, inner and outer, there was fearful anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought of Yanling's words, immediately turned the carriage back, and issued an edict expelling Zhi, Chong, Pang, Xian, and the others; throughout the court, inner and outer, there was fearful anxiety.

sentences.zh: 延齡謀害在朝正直之士，會諫議大夫陽城等伏閣切諫，事遂且止。

translations.literal: Yanling plotted to harm upright men at court; Remonstrating Official Yang Cheng and others knelt at the gate in urgent remonstrance, and the matter was for the time halted.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling plotted to harm upright men at court; Remonstrating Official Yang Cheng and others knelt at the gate in urgent remonstrance, and the matter was for the time halted.

sentences.zh: 贄、充等雖已貶黜，延齡憾之未已，乃掩捕李充腹心吏張忠，捶掠楚痛，令為之詞，雲「前後隱沒官錢五十余萬貫，米麥稱是，其錢物多結托權勢，充妻常於犢車中將金寶繒帛遺陸贄妻。」

translations.literal: Though Zhi, Chong, and the others had already been demoted, Yanling's resentment did not cease; he then secretly arrested Li Chong's trusted clerk Zhang Zhong, beat and tortured him with the cudgel, and made him compose words stating: "In former and latter times he concealed and embezzled more than five hundred thousand strings of official cash; rice and wheat were commensurate; the funds and goods were mostly entrusted to the powerful; Chong's wife often in an ox-cart carried gold, treasures, silks, and brocades as gifts to Lu Zhi's wife."
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhi, Chong, and the others had already been demoted, Yanling's resentment did not cease; he then secretly arrested Li Chong's trusted clerk Zhang Zhong, beat and tortured him with the cudgel, and made him compose words stating, "In former and latter times he concealed and embezzled more than five hundred thousand strings of official cash; rice and wheat were commensurate; the funds and goods were mostly entrusted to the powerful; Chong's wife often in an ox-cart carried gold, treasures, silks, and brocades as gifts to Lu Zhi's wife."

sentences.zh: 忠不勝楚毒，並依延齡教抑之辭，具於款占。

translations.literal: Zhong could not endure the torture and, following Yanling's coached words, set it all down in the confession.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong could not endure the torture and, following Yanling's coached words, set it all down in the confession.

sentences.zh: 忠妻、母於光順門投匭訴冤，詔御史臺推問，一宿得其實狀，事皆虛，乃釋忠。

translations.literal: Zhong's wife and mother submitted a petition of grievance at the Guangshun Gate; an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate, and in one night the true facts were obtained—the matter was entirely false, and Zhong was released.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's wife and mother submitted a petition of grievance at the Guangshun Gate; an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate, and in one night the true facts were obtained—the matter was entirely false, and Zhong was released.

sentences.zh: 延齡又奏京兆府妄破用錢穀，請令比部勾覆，以比部郎中崔元嘗為陸贄所黜故也。

translations.literal: Yanling again memorialized that the metropolitan government had wantonly spent funds and grain without authorization and requested that the Ministry of Revenue audit them—because Ministry of Revenue Section Chief Cui Yuan had once been demoted by Lu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling again memorialized that the metropolitan government had wantonly spent funds and grain without authorization and requested that the Ministry of Revenue audit them—because Ministry of Revenue Section Chief Cui Yuan had once been demoted by Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 及崔元勾覆錢穀，又無交涉。

translations.literal: When Cui Yuan audited the funds and grain, again there was no connection.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yuan audited the funds and grain, again there was no connection.

sentences.zh: 延齡既銳意以苛刻剝下附上為功，每奏對際，皆恣騁詭怪虛妄，他人莫敢言者，延齡言之不疑，亦人之所未嘗聞。

translations.literal: Yanling, intent on making harshness and paring away below to please above his achievement, at every audience memorial freely poured forth devious, bizarre falsehoods; others dared not speak, yet Yanling spoke without doubt—matters no one had ever heard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling, intent on making harshness and paring away below to please above his achievement, at every audience memorial freely poured forth devious, bizarre falsehoods; others dared not speak, yet Yanling spoke without doubt—matters no one had ever heard.

sentences.zh: 德宗頗知其誕妄，但以其敢言無隱，且欲訪聞外事，故斷意用之。

translations.literal: Dezong somewhat knew his absurdity, but because he spoke boldly without concealment and because he wished to hear news of outside affairs, he therefore resolutely used him.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong somewhat knew his absurdity, but because he spoke boldly without concealment and because he wished to hear news of outside affairs, he therefore resolutely used him.

sentences.zh: 延齡恃之，謂必得宰相，尤好慢罵，毀詆朝臣，班行為之側目。

translations.literal: Yanling relied on this, thinking he would surely become chancellor; he especially loved to insult and revile, slandering court officials, and the ranks of office glanced sideways at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling relied on this, thinking he would surely become chancellor; he especially loved to insult and revile, slandering court officials, and the ranks of office glanced sideways at him.

sentences.zh: 及臥病，載度支官物置於私家，亦無敢言者。

translations.literal: When he fell ill he loaded Department of Public Works goods into his private residence, and again none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he loaded Department of Public Works goods into his private residence, and again none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年卒，時年六十九。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he died, at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he died, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 延齡死，中外相賀，唯德宗悼惜不已，冊贈太子少保。

translations.literal: When Yan Yanling died, court and countryside alike rejoiced; only Dezong grieved and mourned without end, enfeoffing him posthumously as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Yanling died, the court and the realm rejoiced alike; only Dezong mourned him without cease and posthumously enfeoffed him as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 韋渠牟，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Qumou was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qumou was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 六代祖範，魏西陽太守，後周封郿城公。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Fan served as governor of Xiyang in Wei and was enfeoffed as Duke of Mei in Later Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Fan had served as governor of Xiyang in Wei and was enfeoffed as Duke of Mei in Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 渠牟少慧悟，涉覽經史。

translations.literal: Qumou in youth was clever and perceptive, and read widely in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Qumou was clever and perceptive, and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 初為道士，後為僧。

translations.literal: At first he was a Daoist priest; later he became a Buddhist monk.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a Daoist priest; later he became a Buddhist monk.

sentences.zh: 興元中，韓滉鎮浙西，奏授試秘書郎，累轉四門博士。

translations.literal: In the Xingyuan era, when Han Huang commanded Zhexi, he memorialized for Qumou's appointment as acting secretary of the Palace Library; he was promoted successively to erudite of the Four Gates.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xingyuan era, when Han Huang commanded Zhexi, he memorialized for Qumou's appointment as acting secretary of the Palace Library; Qumou was promoted successively to erudite of the Four Gates.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年四月，德宗誕日，禦麟德殿，召給事中徐岱、兵部郎中趙需、禮部郎中許孟容與渠牟及道士萬參成、沙門譚延等十二人，講論儒、道、釋三教。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year of Zhenyuan, on Dezong's birthday, he held court in Qinde Hall and summoned Supervising Secretary Xu Dai, Bureau Director Zhao Xu of the Ministry of War, Bureau Director Xu Mengrong of the Ministry of Rites, Qumou, the Daoist Wan Shengcheng, the monk Tan Yan, and twelve others in all to discourse on the three teachings of Confucianism, Daoism, and Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twelfth year of Zhenyuan, on Dezong's birthday, he held court in Qinde Hall and summoned Supervising Secretary Xu Dai, Bureau Director Zhao Xu of the Ministry of War, Bureau Director Xu Mengrong of the Ministry of Rites, Qumou, the Daoist Wan Shengcheng, the monk Tan Yan, and twelve others in all to discourse on the three teachings of Confucianism, Daoism, and Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 渠牟枝詞遊說，捷口水註；

translations.literal: Qumou branched into ornamental rhetoric and lobby talk, swift as flowing water in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Qumou trafficked in ornamental rhetoric and lobby talk, swift as flowing water in debate.

sentences.zh: 上謂其講耨有素，聽之意動。

translations.literal: The emperor judged that his cultivation of exposition had long been thorough, and was moved as he listened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that his cultivation of exposition had long been thorough, and was moved as he listened.

sentences.zh: 數日，轉秘書郎，奏詩七十韻，旬日，遷右補闕、內供奉，僚列初不有之。

translations.literal: Within several days he was transferred to secretary of the Palace Library; he submitted a poem of seventy rhymes, and within ten days was promoted to Right Remonstrance and Palace Attendant—a post that had not existed among his colleagues before.
translations.idiomatic: Within several days he was transferred to secretary of the Palace Library; he submitted a poem of seventy rhymes, and within ten days was promoted to Right Remonstrance and Palace Attendant—a post that had not existed among his colleagues before.

sentences.zh: 在延英既對宰相，多使中貴人召渠牟於官次，同輩始註目矣。

translations.literal: At Yanying audiences, after facing the chancellors, the emperor often had eunuchs summon Qumou from his office; his peers then took notice.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanying audiences, after facing the chancellors, the emperor often had eunuchs summon Qumou from his office; his peers then took notice.

sentences.zh: 歲終，遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At year's end he was promoted to Right Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end he was promoted to Right Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 時延英對秉政賦之臣，晝漏率下二三刻為常，渠牟奏事，率漏下五六刻，上笑語款狎，往往外聞。

translations.literal: At that time, when chancellors who held power attended Yanying audiences, the day clepsydra typically ran down by two or three quarter-hours as the norm; when Qumou reported, it usually ran down by five or six quarter-hours, and the emperor laughed and spoke with intimate familiarity, which often reached those outside.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, when chancellors who held power attended Yanying audiences, the day clepsydra typically ran down by two or three quarter-hours as the norm; when Qumou reported, it usually ran down by five or six quarter-hours, and the emperor laughed and spoke with intimate familiarity, which often reached those outside.

sentences.zh: 渠牟形神佻躁，無士君子器，誌向不根道德，眾雅知不能以正道開悟上意。

translations.literal: Qumou in bearing and spirit was frivolous and restless, lacking the capacity of a gentleman; his ambitions were not rooted in virtue, and all the refined knew he could not open the emperor's mind by the right path.
translations.idiomatic: Qumou in bearing and spirit was frivolous and restless, lacking the capacity of a gentleman; his ambitions were not rooted in virtue, and all the refined knew he could not open the emperor's mind by the right path.

sentences.zh: 陸贄免相後，上躬親庶政，不復委成宰相，廟堂備員，行文書而已。

translations.literal: After Lu Zhi was dismissed from the chancellorship, the emperor personally attended to government and no longer entrusted matters to chancellors; the hall of government had placeholder officials who merely processed documents.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Zhi was dismissed from the chancellorship, the emperor personally attended to government and no longer entrusted matters to chancellors; the hall of government had placeholder officials who merely processed documents.

sentences.zh: 除守宰、御史，皆帝自選擇。

translations.literal: Appointments of prefects and censors were all chosen by the emperor himself.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments of prefects and censors were all chosen by the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 然居深宮，所狎而取信者裴延齡、李齊運、王紹、李實、韋執誼洎渠牟，皆權傾相府。

translations.literal: Yet dwelling deep in the palace, those he favored and trusted—Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, Wang Shao, Li Shi, Wei Zhiyi, and Qumou—all wielded power rivaling the chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Yet dwelling deep in the palace, those he favored and trusted—Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, Wang Shao, Li Shi, Wei Zhiyi, and Qumou—all wielded power rivaling the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 延齡、李實，奸欺多端，甚傷國體；

translations.literal: Yanling and Li Shi were treacherous and deceitful in many ways, greatly harming the body of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling and Li Shi were treacherous and deceitful in many ways, greatly harming the body of the state.

sentences.zh: 紹無所發明；

translations.literal: Shao had nothing to contribute.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had nothing to contribute.

sentences.zh: 而渠牟名素輕，頗張恩勢以招趨向者，門庭填委。

translations.literal: But Qumou's reputation had always been slight; he greatly extended favor and power to attract followers, and his gate and courtyard were packed.
translations.idiomatic: But Qumou's reputation had always been slight; he greatly extended favor and power to attract followers, and his gate and courtyard were packed.

sentences.zh: 茅山處士崔芊征至闕下，鄭隨自山人再至補闕，馮伉自醴泉令為給事中、皇太子侍讀，皆渠牟延薦之。

translations.literal: The Mount Mao recluse Cui Qian was summoned to the capital; Zheng Sui, a mountain recluse, was again appointed Remonstrance; Feng Kang went from magistrate of Liquan to Supervising Secretary and tutor to the crown prince—all were recommended and introduced by Qumou.
translations.idiomatic: The Mount Mao recluse Cui Qian was summoned to the capital; Zheng Sui, a mountain recluse, was again appointed Remonstrance; Feng Kang went from magistrate of Liquan to Supervising Secretary and tutor to the crown prince—all were recommended and introduced by Qumou.

sentences.zh: 上既偏有所聽，浮薄率背本衒進，不復藏器蘊德，皆奔馳請謁，剚蹄甘辭以附渠牟。

translations.literal: Since the emperor was partial in whom he listened to, the frivolous and shallow, turning their backs on their roots to flaunt advancement, no longer concealed their talents and cultivated virtue; all rushed to seek audience, offering mincing flattery to attach themselves to Qumou.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor was partial in whom he listened to, the frivolous and shallow, turning their backs on their roots to flaunt advancement, no longer concealed their talents and cultivated virtue; all rushed to seek audience, offering mincing flattery to attach themselves to Qumou.

sentences.zh: 居無何，遷太府卿，賜金紫，又轉太常卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and granted the gold seal and purple robe; he was then transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and granted the gold seal and purple robe; he was then transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 貞元十七年卒，時年五十三，贈刑部尚書，仍謚曰忠。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged fifty-three; he was posthumously appointed Minister of Justice and given the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged fifty-three; he was posthumously appointed Minister of Justice and given the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 李齊運者，蔣王惲之孫也。

translations.literal: Li Qiyun was a grandson of Prince of Jiang, Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun was a grandson of Prince of Jiang, Yun.

sentences.zh: 解褐寧王府東閣祭酒，七遷至監察御史。

translations.literal: Upon entering service he became Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Ning's mansion; through seven promotions he reached investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering service he became Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Ning's mansion; through seven promotions he reached investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 江淮都統李峘辟為幕府，累轉工部郎中，為長安縣令，職事修理。

translations.literal: Li Kun, overall commander of the Jiang-Huai region, recruited him to his staff; he was promoted successively to bureau director of the Ministry of Public Works and served as magistrate of Chang'an, where his official duties were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kun, overall commander of the Jiang-Huai region, recruited him to his staff; he was promoted successively to bureau director of the Ministry of Public Works and served as magistrate of Chang'an, where his official duties were well ordered.

sentences.zh: 歷京兆少尹、陜府長史。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice magistrate of Jingzhao and chief administrator of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice magistrate of Jingzhao and chief administrator of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建中末，改河中尹、晉絳慈隰觀察使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianzhong era he was changed to metropolitan governor of Hezhong and military commissioner of Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Li.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianzhong era he was changed to metropolitan governor of Hezhong and military commissioner of Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Li.

sentences.zh: 時李懷光自山東卷甲奔難，晝夜倍道，比至河中，力疲，休兵三日，齊運傾力犒設，軍人皆悅。

translations.literal: At that time Li Huaiguang, armored from east of the mountains, rushed to the rescue by forced marches day and night; when he reached Hezhong his strength was spent, and after resting the army three days Qiyun exhausted all efforts in provisioning and feasting the troops, and the soldiers were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Huaiguang, armored from east of the mountains, rushed to the rescue by forced marches day and night; when he reached Hezhong his strength was spent, and after resting the army three days Qiyun exhausted all efforts in provisioning and feasting the troops, and the soldiers were all pleased.

sentences.zh: 懷光既反，驅兵還保河中，齊運不能敵，棄城而走，除為京兆尹，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Once Huaiguang rebelled, he drove his troops back to hold Hezhong; Qiyun could not resist and abandoned the city and fled; he was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huaiguang rebelled, he drove his troops back to hold Hezhong; Qiyun could not resist and abandoned the city and fled; he was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時賊據京城，李晟軍東渭橋，齊運擾攘之中，征募工役，版築城壘，飛芻輓粟以應晟。

translations.literal: At that time rebels held the capital; Li Sheng's army was at East Wei Bridge; amid the turmoil Qiyun recruited laborers, built ramparts and fortifications, and rushed fodder and grain to supply Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time rebels held the capital; Li Sheng's army was at East Wei Bridge; amid the turmoil Qiyun recruited laborers, built ramparts and fortifications, and rushed fodder and grain to supply Sheng.

sentences.zh: 收復之際，頗有力焉。

translations.literal: At the time of recovery he contributed considerably.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of recovery he contributed considerably.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，蝗旱方熾，齊運無政術，乃以韓洄代之，改宗正卿，兼御史大夫、閑廄宮苑使。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, locusts and drought were raging; Qiyun had no skill in governance, and so Han Hui replaced him; he was changed to Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Imperial Stud and Palace Parks.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era, locusts and drought were raging; Qiyun had no skill in governance, and so Han Hui replaced him; he was changed to Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Imperial Stud and Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 改檢校禮部尚書，兼殿中監。

translations.literal: He was changed to Acting Minister of Rites and Concurrent Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Acting Minister of Rites and Concurrent Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 尋正拜禮部尚書，兼殿中監使如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was formally appointed Minister of Rites, retaining his concurrent posts as Director of the Palace Domestic Service and commissioner as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was formally appointed Minister of Rites, retaining his concurrent posts as Director of the Palace Domestic Service and commissioner as before.

sentences.zh: 其後十余歲，宰臣內殿對後，齊運常次進，貢其計慮，以決群議。

translations.literal: For more than ten years thereafter, after chancellors had audience in the inner hall, Qiyun would regularly follow to present his calculations and settle collective deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years thereafter, after chancellors had audience in the inner hall, Qiyun would regularly follow to present his calculations and settle collective deliberation.

sentences.zh: 齊運無學術，不知大體，但甘言取信而已。

translations.literal: Qiyun had no learning and did not understand great principles; he merely won trust with sweet words.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun had no learning and did not understand great principles; he merely won trust with sweet words.

sentences.zh: 薦李锜為浙西觀察使，受賂數十萬計。

translations.literal: He recommended Li Gao as military commissioner of Zhexi and received bribes amounting to several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Li Gao as military commissioner of Zhexi and received bribes amounting to several hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 舉李詞為湖州刺史，既而邑人告其贓犯，上以齊運故，不問而遣之。

translations.literal: He nominated Li Ci as prefect of Hu Prefecture; afterward the people of the district reported his corruption, but because of Qiyun the emperor did not investigate and sent him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: He nominated Li Ci as prefect of Hu Prefecture; afterward the people of the district reported his corruption, but because of Qiyun the emperor did not investigate and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 齊運被疾，歲余不能朝請，朝廷除授，往往降中人就宅咨決。

translations.literal: Qiyun fell ill; for more than a year he could not attend court audiences, and for court appointments eunuchs were often sent to his residence for consultation and decision.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun fell ill; for more than a year he could not attend court audiences, and for court appointments eunuchs were often sent to his residence for consultation and decision.

sentences.zh: 末以妾衛氏為正室，身為禮部尚書，冕服以行其禮，人士嗤誚。

translations.literal: In the end he made his concubine Lady Wei his principal wife; though he was Minister of Rites, he wore ceremonial robes to perform the rites, and gentlemen mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he made his concubine Lady Wei his principal wife; though he was Minister of Rites, he wore ceremonial robes to perform the rites, and gentlemen mocked him.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年卒，時年七十二，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged seventy-two; he was posthumously appointed Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged seventy-two; he was posthumously appointed Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 李實者，道王元慶玄孫。

translations.literal: Li Shi was a great-great-grandson of Prince of Dao, Yuangqing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi was a great-great-grandson of Prince of Dao, Yuangqing.

sentences.zh: 以廕入仕，六轉至潭州司馬。

translations.literal: He entered service through hereditary privilege; through six promotions he reached vice prefect of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through hereditary privilege; through six promotions he reached vice prefect of Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洪州節度使、嗣曹王臯辟為判官，遷蘄州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Gao, military commissioner of Hong Prefecture and Prince of Cao, recruited him as staff judge; he was promoted to prefect of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao, military commissioner of Hong Prefecture and Prince of Cao, recruited him as staff judge; he was promoted to prefect of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 臯為山南東道節度使，復用為節度判官、檢校太子賓客、員外郎。

translations.literal: When Gao became military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, he again employed Shi as circuit staff judge, Acting Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and outer-office director.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao became military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, he again employed Shi as circuit staff judge, Acting Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and outer-office director.

sentences.zh: 臯卒，新帥未至，實知留後，刻薄軍士衣食，軍士怨叛，謀殺之，實夜縋城而出，歸詣京師，用為司農少卿，加檢校工部尚書、司農卿。

translations.literal: When Gao died and the new commander had not yet arrived, Shi acted as regent; he was harsh in cutting soldiers' food and clothing, and the soldiers resented and rebelled, plotting to kill him; Shi let himself down by rope from the wall by night, returned to the capital, and was appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, with additional appointment as Acting Minister of Public Works and Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died and the new commander had not yet arrived, Shi acted as regent; he was harsh in cutting soldiers' food and clothing, and the soldiers resented and rebelled, plotting to kill him; Shi let himself down by rope from the wall by night, returned to the capital, and was appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, with additional appointment as Acting Minister of Public Works and Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 貞元十九年，為京兆尹，卿及兼官如故。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan he became metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, retaining his directorate and concurrent posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan he became metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, retaining his directorate and concurrent posts as before.

sentences.zh: 尋封嗣道王。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dao.

sentences.zh: 自為京尹，恃寵強愎，不顧文法，人皆側目。

translations.literal: Once he was metropolitan governor, relying on favor he was domineering and obstinate, heedless of law and precedent, and people all looked askance at him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was metropolitan governor, relying on favor he was domineering and obstinate, heedless of law and precedent, and people all looked askance at him.

sentences.zh: 二十年春夏旱，關中大歉，實為政猛暴，方務聚斂進奉，以固恩顧，百姓所訴，一不介意。

translations.literal: In the spring and summer of the twentieth year there was drought; Guanzhong suffered great famine; Shi's governance was fierce and brutal, and he devoted himself to amassing wealth for imperial tribute to secure favor, utterly indifferent to the people's complaints.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring and summer of the twentieth year there was drought; Guanzhong suffered great famine; Shi's governance was fierce and brutal, and he devoted himself to amassing wealth for imperial tribute to secure favor, utterly indifferent to the people's complaints.

sentences.zh: 因入對，德宗問人疾苦，實奏曰：「今年雖旱，谷田甚好。」

translations.literal: On entering audience Dezong asked about the people's hardships; Shi reported: "Though this year has drought, the grain fields are in very good condition."
translations.idiomatic: On entering audience Dezong asked about the people's hardships; Shi reported, "Though this year has drought, the grain fields are in very good condition."

sentences.zh: 由是租稅皆不免，人窮無告，乃徹屋瓦木，賣麥苗以供賦斂。

translations.literal: Because of this, land tax and levies were all left unremitted; people were destitute with nowhere to turn, and so tore off roof tiles and timber and sold wheat seedlings to meet tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, land tax and levies were all left unremitted; people were destitute with nowhere to turn, and so tore off roof tiles and timber and sold wheat seedlings to meet tax collection.

sentences.zh: 優人成輔端因戲作語，為秦民艱苦之狀云：「秦城城池二百年，何期如此賤田園，一頃麥苗五碩米，三間堂屋二千錢。」

translations.literal: The entertainer Cheng Fuduan improvised lines in a performance depicting the hardships of the people of Qin, saying: "The walls of Qin have stood two hundred years—who would have thought farmland could be so cheap! One qing of wheat seedlings for five shi of grain; three bays of hall for two thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: The entertainer Cheng Fuduan improvised lines in a performance depicting the hardships of the people of Qin, saying, "The walls of Qin have stood two hundred years—who would have thought farmland could be so cheap! One qing of wheat seedlings for five shi of grain; three bays of hall for two thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 凡如此語有數十篇。

translations.literal: There were several dozen such pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: There were several dozen such pieces in all.

sentences.zh: 實聞之怒，言輔端誹謗國政，德宗遽令決殺，當時言者曰：「瞽誦箴諫，取其詼諧以托諷諫，優伶舊事也。

translations.literal: When Shi heard of it he was enraged, saying Cheng Fuduan had slandered state affairs; Dezong immediately ordered him executed by decapitation; commentators at the time said: "The blind recite admonitions and remonstrances, taking wit and humor to convey indirect criticism—this is an old practice of performers.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi heard of it he was enraged, saying Cheng Fuduan had slandered state affairs; Dezong immediately ordered him executed by decapitation; commentators at the time said, "The blind recite admonitions and remonstrances, taking wit and humor to convey indirect criticism—this is an old practice of performers.

sentences.zh: 設謗木，采芻蕘，本欲達下情，存諷議，輔端不可加罪。」

translations.literal: Setting up the rebuke board and gathering counsel from the common people were meant to reach the feelings below and preserve admonishing discussion. Cheng Fuduan should not have been punished."
translations.idiomatic: Setting up the rebuke board and gathering counsel from the common people were meant to reach the feelings below and preserve admonishing discussion. Cheng Fuduan should not have been punished."

sentences.zh: 德宗亦深悔，京師無不切齒以怒實。

translations.literal: Dezong too deeply regretted it; throughout the capital all gnash their teeth in rage at Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong too deeply regretted it; throughout the capital all gnash their teeth in rage at Shi.

sentences.zh: 故事，府官避臺官。

translations.literal: By precedent, metropolitan officials yielded the way to censorate officials.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, metropolitan officials yielded the way to censorate officials.

sentences.zh: 實常遇侍御史王播於道，實不肯避，導從如常。

translations.literal: Shi often met Attending Censor Wang Bo on the road; Shi would not yield, and his attendants proceeded as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Shi often met Attending Censor Wang Bo on the road; Shi would not yield, and his attendants proceeded as usual.

sentences.zh: 播詰其從者，實怒，奏播為三原令，謝之日，庭詬之。

translations.literal: Bo questioned his attendants; Shi was enraged, memorialized to appoint Bo magistrate of Sanyuan, and on the day of thanksgiving berated him in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Bo questioned his attendants; Shi was enraged, memorialized to appoint Bo magistrate of Sanyuan, and on the day of thanksgiving berated him in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 陵轢公卿百執事，隨其喜怒，誣奏遷逐者相繼，朝士畏而惡之。

translations.literal: He trampled dukes, ministers, and officials of every rank, and according to his pleasure or anger sent false memorials for transfer and banishment in succession; court gentlemen feared and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: He trampled dukes, ministers, and officials of every rank, and according to his pleasure or anger sent false memorials for transfer and banishment in succession; court gentlemen feared and hated him.

sentences.zh: 又誣奏萬年令李眾，貶虔州司馬，奏虞部員外郎房啟代眾，升黜如其意，怙勢之色，謷然在眉睫間。

translations.literal: He also falsely memorialized against Wannian magistrate Li Zhong, demoting him to vice prefect of Qian Prefecture; he memorialized for Fang Qi of the Ministry of Works to replace Zhong, promoting and demoting as he wished; the color of relying on power was plainly visible between his brows and lashes.
translations.idiomatic: He also falsely memorialized against Wannian magistrate Li Zhong, demoting him to vice prefect of Qian Prefecture; he memorialized for Fang Qi of the Ministry of Works to replace Zhong, promoting and demoting as he wished; the color of relying on power was plainly visible between his brows and lashes.

sentences.zh: 故事，吏部將奏科目，奧密，朝官不通書問，而實身詣選曹迫趙宗儒，且以勢恐之。

translations.literal: By precedent, when the Ministry of Personnel was about to report examination subjects, the matter was highly confidential and court officials did not exchange letters; yet Shi went in person to the selection office to press Zhao Zongru and moreover intimidated him with his power.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when the Ministry of Personnel was about to report examination subjects, the matter was highly confidential and court officials did not exchange letters; yet Shi went in person to the selection office to press Zhao Zongru and moreover intimidated him with his power.

sentences.zh: 前歲，權德輿為禮部侍郎，實托私薦士，不能如意，後遂大錄二十人迫德輿曰：「可依此第之；

translations.literal: The previous year Quan Deyu was Vice Minister of Rites; Shi privately recommended examinees and could not get his way; afterward he drew up a list of twenty men and pressed Deyu, saying: "You may rank them according to this list;
translations.idiomatic: The previous year Quan Deyu was Vice Minister of Rites; Shi privately recommended examinees and could not get his way; afterward he drew up a list of twenty men and pressed Deyu, saying, "You may rank them according to this list;

sentences.zh: 不爾，必出外官，悔無及也。」

translations.literal: otherwise they are certain to be posted to outer offices, and it will be too late for regret."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise they are certain to be posted to outer offices, and it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 德輿雖不從，然頗懼其誣奏。

translations.literal: Though Deyu did not comply, he was quite afraid of Shi's false memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Though Deyu did not comply, he was quite afraid of Shi's false memorials.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，有詔蠲畿內逋租，實違詔征之，百姓大困，官吏多遭笞罰，剝割掊斂，聚錢三十萬貫，胥吏或犯者，即按之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year there was an edict remitting overdue rents within the capital region; Shi defied the edict and collected them; the people were greatly distressed, and many officials were beaten and punished; through extortion and squeezing he amassed three hundred thousand strings of cash, and whenever clerks offended him he prosecuted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year there was an edict remitting overdue rents within the capital region; Shi defied the edict and collected them; the people were greatly distressed, and many officials were beaten and punished; through extortion and squeezing he amassed three hundred thousand strings of cash, and whenever clerks offended him he prosecuted them.

sentences.zh: 有乞丐絲發固死；

translations.literal: There was a beggar who clung to a single hair and was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: There was a beggar who clung to a single hair and was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 無者，且曰「死亦不屈」，亦杖殺之。

translations.literal: When there was none, he would say "I would rather die than yield" and beat him to death as well.
translations.idiomatic: When there was none, he would say, "I would rather die than yield," and beat him to death as well.

sentences.zh: 京帥貴賤同苦其暴虐。

translations.literal: High and low in the capital alike suffered his brutality.
translations.idiomatic: High and low in the capital alike suffered his brutality.

sentences.zh: 順宗在諒陰逾月，實斃人於府者十數，遂議逐之，乃貶通州長史。

translations.literal: While Shunzong was in mourning seclusion for over a month, Shi had beaten more than ten men to death in his office; deliberation then turned to banishing him, and he was demoted to chief administrator of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While Shunzong was in mourning seclusion for over a month, Shi had beaten more than ten men to death in his office; deliberation then turned to banishing him, and he was demoted to chief administrator of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 制出，市人皆袖瓦石投其首；

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, people in the markets all tucked tiles and stones in their sleeves to throw at his head.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, people in the markets all tucked tiles and stones in their sleeves to throw at his head.

sentences.zh: 實知之，由月營門自苑西出，人人相賀。

translations.literal: Shi learned of it and went out west from the park through the Moon Camp Gate; everyone congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Shi learned of it and went out west from the park through the Moon Camp Gate; everyone congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 後遇赦量移虢州，在道卒。

translations.literal: Later, when an amnesty permitted transfer, he was moved to Guo Prefecture and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when an amnesty permitted transfer, he was moved to Guo Prefecture and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 韋執誼者，京兆人。

translations.literal: Wei Zhiyi was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyi was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父浼，官卑。

translations.literal: His father Mei held a low office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mei held a low office.

sentences.zh: 執誼幼聰俊有才，進士擢第，應制策高等，拜右拾遺，召入翰林為學士，年才二十余。

translations.literal: Zhiyi in youth was clever and talented; he passed the jinshi examination, ranked high in the imperial policy examination, was appointed Right Collector of Lost Writings, and was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as academician at just over twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi in youth was clever and talented; he passed the jinshi examination, ranked high in the imperial policy examination, was appointed Right Collector of Lost Writings, and was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as academician at just over twenty.

sentences.zh: 德宗尤寵異，相與唱和歌詩，與裴延齡、韋渠牟等出入禁中，略備顧問。

translations.literal: Dezong especially favored him; they exchanged responsive poems in song, and with Pei Yanling, Wei Qumou, and others he went in and out of the forbidden precincts, broadly serving as adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong especially favored him; they exchanged responsive poems in song, and with Pei Yanling, Wei Qumou, and others he went in and out of the forbidden precincts, broadly serving as adviser.

sentences.zh: 德宗載誕日，皇太子獻佛像，德宗命執誼為畫像贊，上令太子賜執誼縑帛以酬之。

translations.literal: On Dezong's birthday the crown prince presented a Buddhist image; Dezong ordered Zhiyi to compose an inscription for the painted image, and ordered the crown prince to reward Zhiyi with silk to repay him.
translations.idiomatic: On Dezong's birthday the crown prince presented a Buddhist image; Dezong ordered Zhiyi to compose an inscription for the painted image, and ordered the crown prince to reward Zhiyi with silk to repay him.

sentences.zh: 執誼至東宮謝太子，卒然無以藉言，太子因曰：「學士知王叔文乎？

translations.literal: Zhiyi went to the Eastern Palace to thank the crown prince and suddenly had nothing to say; the crown prince then said: "Does the Academician know Wang Shuwen?
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi went to the Eastern Palace to thank the crown prince and suddenly had nothing to say; the crown prince then said, "Does the Academician know Wang Shuwen?

sentences.zh: 彼偉才也。」

translations.literal: He is a man of great talent."
translations.idiomatic: He is a man of great talent."

sentences.zh: 執誼因是與叔文交甚密。

translations.literal: Because of this Zhiyi became very close with Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this Zhiyi became very close with Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 俄丁母憂，服闋，起為南宮郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was bereaved of his mother; when mourning was complete he was recalled as an official of the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was bereaved of his mother; when mourning was complete he was recalled as an official of the Southern Palace.

sentences.zh: 德宗時，召入禁中。

translations.literal: In Dezong's time he was summoned into the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: In Dezong's time he was summoned into the forbidden precincts.

sentences.zh: 初，貞元十九年，補闕張正一因上書言事得召見，王仲舒、韋成季、劉伯芻、裴茝、常仲孺、呂洞等以嘗同官相善，以正一得召見，偕往賀之。

translations.literal: At first, in the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan, Remonstrance Zhang Zhengyi, having submitted a memorial on state affairs, was granted audience; Wang Zhongshu, Wei Chengji, Liu Bochou, Pei Zhi, Chang Zhongru, and Lü Dong, who had once served together and were friendly, because Zhengyi had been granted audience went together to congratulate him.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan, Remonstrance Zhang Zhengyi, having submitted a memorial on state affairs, was granted audience; Wang Zhongshu, Wei Chengji, Liu Bochou, Pei Zhi, Chang Zhongru, and Lü Dong, who had once served together and were friendly, because Zhengyi had been granted audience went together to congratulate him.

sentences.zh: 或告執誼曰：「正一等上疏論君與王叔文朋黨事。」

translations.literal: Someone reported to Zhiyi: "Zhengyi and the others submitted memorials discussing your factional dealings with Wang Shuwen."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported to Zhiyi, "Zhengyi and the others submitted memorials discussing your factional dealings with Wang Shuwen."

sentences.zh: 執誼信然之，因召對，奏曰：「韋成季等朋聚覬望。」

translations.literal: Zhiyi believed it and, on being summoned to audience, reported: "Wei Chengji and the others have formed a clique in hopes of advancement."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi believed it and, on being summoned to audience, reported, "Wei Chengji and the others have formed a clique in hopes of advancement."

sentences.zh: 德宗令金吾伺之，得其相過從飲食數度，於是盡逐成季等六七人，當時莫測其由。

translations.literal: Dezong ordered the Imperial Guard to watch them and found that they had visited one another and shared food and drink on several occasions; thereupon Chengji and six or seven others were all banished, and at the time none could fathom the reason.
