translations.idiomatic: Dezong ordered the Imperial Guard to watch them and found that they had visited one another and shared food and drink on several occasions; thereupon Chengji and six or seven others were all banished, and at the time none could fathom the reason.

sentences.zh: 及順宗即位，久疾不任朝政，王叔文用事，乃用執誼為宰相，乃自朝議郎、吏部郎中、騎都尉賜緋魚袋，授尚書左丞、同平章事，仍賜金紫。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, long ill and unable to attend to government, Wang Shuwen held power; Zhiyi was then made chancellor—from Court Gentleman for Consultation, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Commandant of Cavalry he was granted the crimson robe and fish tally, appointed Vice Minister of the Left and Concurrent Regular Second-Rank Counselor, and still granted the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong took the throne, long ill and unable to attend to government, Wang Shuwen held power; Zhiyi was then made chancellor—from Court Gentleman for Consultation, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Commandant of Cavalry he was granted the crimson robe and fish tally, appointed Vice Minister of the Left and Concurrent Regular Second-Rank Counselor, and still granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 叔文欲專政，故令執誼為宰相於外，己自專於內。

translations.literal: Shuwen wished to monopolize government, and so had Zhiyi serve as chancellor on the outside while he himself held exclusive control within.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen wished to monopolize government, and so had Zhiyi serve as chancellor on the outside while he himself held exclusive control within.

sentences.zh: 執誼既為叔文引用，不敢負情，然迫於公議，時時立異，密令人謝叔文曰：「不敢負約為異，欲共成國家之事故也。」

translations.literal: Zhiyi, having been brought in by Shuwen, dared not betray their bond; yet pressed by public opinion he sometimes took opposing stands, and secretly sent someone to apologize to Shuwen, saying: "I do not dare break our pact by differing with you; I wish only that together we may accomplish the affairs of state."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi, having been brought in by Shuwen, dared not betray their bond; yet pressed by public opinion he sometimes took opposing stands, and secretly sent someone to apologize to Shuwen, saying, "I do not dare break our pact by differing with you; I wish only that together we may accomplish the affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 叔文詬怒，遂成仇怨；

translations.literal: Shuwen cursed him in rage, and enmity was thus formed.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen cursed him in rage, and enmity was thus formed.

sentences.zh: 執誼既因之得位，亦欲矛盾掩其跡。

translations.literal: Zhiyi, having gained his position through Shuwen, also wished to contradict him to cover his tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi, having gained his position through Shuwen, also wished to contradict him to cover his tracks.

sentences.zh: 及憲宗受內禪，王伾、王叔文徒黨並逐，尚以執誼是宰相杜黃裳之婿，故數月後貶崖州司戶。

translations.literal: When Xianzong received the inner abdication, Wang Pi, Wang Shuwen, and their faction were all banished; because Zhiyi was son-in-law of Chancellor Du Huangshang, several months later he was demoted to registrar of Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong received the inner abdication, Wang Pi, Wang Shuwen, and their faction were all banished; because Zhiyi was son-in-law of Chancellor Du Huangshang, several months later he was demoted to registrar of Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，執誼自卑官，常忌諱不欲人言嶺南州縣名。

translations.literal: At first, from his low office, Zhiyi was always superstitious and did not wish people to speak the names of Lingnan prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: At first, from his low office, Zhiyi was always superstitious and did not wish people to speak the names of Lingnan prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 為郎官時，嘗與同舍詣職方觀圖，每至嶺南州，執誼遽命去之，閉目不視。

translations.literal: When he was a bureau official he once went with colleagues in the same lodging to the Bureau of Appointments to view maps; whenever they reached a Lingnan prefecture Zhiyi immediately ordered it removed and closed his eyes without looking.
translations.idiomatic: When he was a bureau official he once went with colleagues in the same lodging to the Bureau of Appointments to view maps; whenever they reached a Lingnan prefecture Zhiyi immediately ordered it removed and closed his eyes without looking.

sentences.zh: 及拜相，還所坐堂，見北壁有圖，不就省，七八日，試觀之，乃崖州圖也，以為不祥，甚惡之，不敢出口。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor he returned to the hall where he sat and saw a map on the north wall; he did not approach to examine it; after seven or eight days he tried looking and found it was a map of Ya Prefecture; he regarded it as ill-omened, greatly loathed it, and dared not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: When he became chancellor he returned to the hall where he sat and saw a map on the north wall; he did not approach to examine it; after seven or eight days he tried looking and found it was a map of Ya Prefecture; he regarded it as ill-omened, greatly loathed it, and dared not speak of it.

sentences.zh: 及坐叔文之貶，果往崖州，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: When he was punished along with Shuwen's banishment, he was indeed sent to Ya Prefecture and died in banishment.
translations.idiomatic: When he was punished along with Shuwen's banishment, he was indeed sent to Ya Prefecture and died in banishment.

sentences.zh: 王叔文者，越州山陰人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen was a native of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen was a native of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以棋待詔，粗知書，好言理道。

translations.literal: He served as chess attendant awaiting imperial summons; he had rough knowledge of books and loved to speak of principle and the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chess attendant awaiting imperial summons; he had rough knowledge of books and loved to speak of principle and the Way.

sentences.zh: 德宗令直東宮。

translations.literal: Dezong ordered him to serve in attendance at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong ordered him to serve in attendance at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太子嘗與侍讀論政道，因言宮市之弊，太子曰：「寡人見上，當極言之。」

translations.literal: The crown prince once discussed the way of government with his tutors and, speaking of the abuses of the palace market, said: "When I see the emperor, I shall speak out to the full."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince once discussed the way of government with his tutors and, speaking of the abuses of the palace market, said, "When I see the emperor, I shall speak out to the full."

sentences.zh: 諸生稱贊其美，叔文獨無言。

translations.literal: The students praised his excellence; only Shuwen said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The students praised his excellence; only Shuwen said nothing.

sentences.zh: 罷坐，太子謂叔文曰：「向論宮市，君獨無言何也」？

translations.literal: When the session ended the crown prince said to Shuwen: "When we discussed the palace market just now, why did you alone say nothing?"
translations.idiomatic: When the session ended the crown prince said to Shuwen, "When we discussed the palace market just now, why did you alone say nothing?"

sentences.zh: 叔文曰：「皇太子之事上也，視膳問安之外，不合輒預外事。

translations.literal: Shuwen said: "In serving the emperor, the crown prince's duties are to oversee meals and inquire after his health; beyond that he ought not casually intervene in external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen said, "In serving the emperor, the crown prince's duties are to oversee meals and inquire after his health; beyond that he ought not casually intervene in external affairs.

sentences.zh: 陛下在位歲久，如小人離間，謂殿下收取人情，則安能自解？」

translations.literal: The emperor has reigned many years; if petty men sow discord and say the crown prince is cultivating personal ties, how can you clear yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has reigned many years; if petty men sow discord and say the crown prince is cultivating personal ties, how can you clear yourself?"

sentences.zh: 太子謝之曰：「茍無先生，安得聞此言？」

translations.literal: The crown prince thanked him, saying: "Were it not for you, sir, how could I have heard these words?"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince thanked him, saying, "Were it not for you, sir, how could I have heard these words?"

sentences.zh: 由是重之，宮中之事，倚之裁決。

translations.literal: From this the crown prince valued him; affairs within the palace were entrusted to him for decision.
translations.idiomatic: From this the crown prince valued him; affairs within the palace were entrusted to him for decision.

sentences.zh: 每對太子言，則曰：「某可為相，某可為將，幸異日用之。」

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke to the crown prince he would say: "So-and-so can serve as chancellor, so-and-so can serve as general—may they be employed on another day."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke to the crown prince he would say, "So-and-so can serve as chancellor, so-and-so can serve as general—may they be employed on another day."

sentences.zh: 密結當代知名之士而欲僥幸速進者，與韋執誼、陸質、呂溫、李景儉、韓曄、韓泰、陳諫、柳宗元、劉禹錫等十數人，定為死交；

translations.literal: He secretly joined with renowned men of the age who wished to advance by chance—Wei Zhiyi, Lu Zhi, Lü Wen, Li Jingjian, Han Ye, Han Tai, Chen Jian, Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, and more than ten others—and fixed them as sworn friends.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly joined with renowned men of the age who wished to advance by chance—Wei Zhiyi, Lu Zhi, Lü Wen, Li Jingjian, Han Ye, Han Tai, Chen Jian, Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, and more than ten others—and fixed them as sworn friends.

sentences.zh: 而淩準，程异，又因其黨以進；

translations.literal: Ling Zhun and Cheng Yi too advanced through their faction.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Zhun and Cheng Yi too advanced through their faction.

sentences.zh: 籓鎮侯伯，亦有陰行賂遺請交者。

translations.literal: Regional lords and marquises also secretly sent bribes and gifts requesting association.
translations.idiomatic: Regional lords and marquises also secretly sent bribes and gifts requesting association.

sentences.zh: 德宗崩，已宣遺詔，時上寢疾久，不復關庶政，深居施簾帷，閹官李忠言、美人牛昭容侍左右，百官上議，自帷中可其奏。

translations.literal: When Dezong died and the testamentary edict had already been proclaimed, the emperor had long been ill in bed and no longer attended to government; dwelling deep within behind curtained screens, eunuch Li Zhongyan and the favored consort Niu Zhaorong attended at his side; when officials above presented deliberations, he approved their memorials from within the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong died and the testamentary edict had already been proclaimed, the emperor had long been ill in bed and no longer attended to government; dwelling deep within behind curtained screens, eunuch Li Zhongyan and the favored consort Niu Zhaorong attended at his side; when officials above presented deliberations, he approved their memorials from within the curtain.

sentences.zh: 王伾常諭上屬意叔文，宮中諸黃門稍稍知之。

translations.literal: Wang Pi often told the emperor of his regard for Shuwen; the palace eunuchs gradually came to know it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi often told the emperor of his regard for Shuwen; the palace eunuchs gradually came to know it.

sentences.zh: 其日，召自右銀臺門，居於翰林，為學士。

translations.literal: That day Shuwen was summoned from the Right Yintai Gate and lodged in the Hanlin Academy as academician.
translations.idiomatic: That day Shuwen was summoned from the Right Yintai Gate and lodged in the Hanlin Academy as academician.

sentences.zh: 叔文與吏部郎中韋執誼相善，請用為宰相。

translations.literal: Shuwen was on good terms with Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wei Zhiyi and requested that he be made chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was on good terms with Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wei Zhiyi and requested that he be made chancellor.

sentences.zh: 叔文因王伾，伾因李忠言，忠言因牛昭容，轉相結構。

translations.literal: Shuwen relied on Wang Pi; Pi relied on Li Zhongyan; Zhongyan relied on Niu Zhaorong—they linked one to another in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen relied on Wang Pi; Pi relied on Li Zhongyan; Zhongyan relied on Niu Zhaorong—they linked one to another in succession.

sentences.zh: 事下翰林，叔文定可否，宣於中書，俾執誼承奏於外。

translations.literal: When matters descended to the Hanlin Academy, Shuwen decided what was permissible; he proclaimed it in the Central Secretariat, and had Zhiyi receive and report on the outside.
translations.idiomatic: When matters descended to the Hanlin Academy, Shuwen decided what was permissible; he proclaimed it in the Central Secretariat, and had Zhiyi receive and report on the outside.

sentences.zh: 與韓泰、柳宗元、劉禹錫、陳諫、淩準、韓曄唱和，曰管，曰葛，曰伊，曰周，凡其黨僴然自得，謂天下無人。

translations.literal: With Han Tai, Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, Chen Jian, Ling Zhun, and Han Ye he exchanged responsive verses, calling one Guan, one Ge, one Yi, one Zhou; all his faction were complacently pleased, thinking no one in the realm matched them.
translations.idiomatic: With Han Tai, Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, Chen Jian, Ling Zhun, and Han Ye he exchanged responsive verses, calling one Guan, one Ge, one Yi, one Zhou; all his faction were complacently pleased, thinking no one in the realm matched them.

sentences.zh: 叔文賤時，每言錢穀為國大本，將可以盈縮兵賦，可操柄市士。

translations.literal: When Shuwen was lowly he often declared, "Revenue and grain are the great foundation of the state, by which one can expand or contract military levies and wield control over the marketplace of talent."
translations.idiomatic: When Shuwen was lowly he often declared, "Revenue and grain are the great foundation of the state, by which one can expand or contract military levies and wield control over the marketplace of talent."

sentences.zh: 叔文初入翰林，自蘇州司功為起居郎，俄兼充度支、鹽鐵副使，以杜佑領使，其實成於叔文。

translations.literal: When Shuwen first entered the Hanlin Academy he went from Recorder of Suzhou to Diarist; soon he also served concurrently as Vice Commissioner of the Revenue and Salt Iron Commissions, with Du You as nominal commissioner while the real power rested with Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuwen first entered the Hanlin Academy he went from Recorder of Suzhou to Diarist; soon he also served concurrently as Vice Commissioner of the Revenue and Salt Iron Commissions, with Du You as nominal commissioner while the real power rested with Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 數月，轉尚書戶部侍郎，領使、學士如故。

translations.literal: Within several months he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, retaining his commissioner and academician posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: Within several months he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, retaining his commissioner and academician posts as before.

sentences.zh: 內官俱文珍惡其弄權，乃削去學士之職。

translations.literal: The inner eunuch Ju Wenjing hated his manipulation of power and stripped him of his academician post.
translations.idiomatic: The inner eunuch Ju Wenjing hated his manipulation of power and stripped him of his academician post.

sentences.zh: 制出，叔文大駭，謂人曰：「叔文須時至此商量公事，若不帶此職，無由入內。」

translations.literal: When the edict was issued Shuwen was greatly alarmed and told others: "I, Shuwen, must at times come here to discuss official business; without this post there is no way to enter the inner palace."
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued Shuwen was greatly alarmed and told others, "I, Shuwen, must at times come here to discuss official business; without this post there is no way to enter the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 王伾為之論請，乃許三、五日一入翰林，竟削內職。

translations.literal: Wang Pi pleaded on his behalf, and he was permitted to enter the Hanlin Academy once every three or five days; in the end his inner post was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi pleaded on his behalf, and he was permitted to enter the Hanlin Academy once every three or five days; in the end his inner post was cut.

sentences.zh: 叔文始入內廷，陰構密命，機形不見，因騰口善惡進退之。

translations.literal: When Shuwen first entered the inner court he secretly shaped confidential orders, his designs invisible; he then broadcast judgments on promotion and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuwen first entered the inner court he secretly shaped confidential orders, his designs invisible; he then broadcast judgments on promotion and demotion.

sentences.zh: 人未窺其本，信為奇才。

translations.literal: People had not yet discerned his root and believed him a rare talent.
translations.idiomatic: People had not yet discerned his root and believed him a rare talent.

sentences.zh: 及司兩使利柄，齒於外朝，愚智同曰：「城狐山鬼，必夜號窟居以禍福人，亦神而畏之；

translations.literal: Once he held the profit lever of the two commissions and stood among the outer court, wise and foolish alike said: "The fox in the city wall and the ghost in the mountain must by night cry from their dens to bring fortune or disaster upon people—thus they are deemed supernatural and feared;
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the profit lever of the two commissions and stood among the outer court, wise and foolish alike said, "The fox in the city wall and the ghost in the mountain must by night cry from their dens to bring fortune or disaster upon people—thus they are deemed supernatural and feared;

sentences.zh: 一旦晝出路馳，無能必矣。」

translations.literal: but once they run out by day, they are surely powerless."
translations.idiomatic: but once they run out by day, they are surely powerless."

sentences.zh: 叔文在省署，不復舉其職事，引其黨與竊語，謀奪內官兵柄，乃以故將範希朝統京西北諸鎮行營兵馬使，韓泰副之。

translations.literal: Shuwen in the ministry offices no longer performed his duties but gathered his faction for whispered counsel, plotting to seize control of the inner palace army; he therefore appointed the former general Fan Xichao overall commander of the field armies of the northwest capital commands, with Han Tai as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen in the ministry offices no longer performed his duties but gathered his faction for whispered counsel, plotting to seize control of the inner palace army; he therefore appointed the former general Fan Xichao overall commander of the field armies of the northwest capital commands, with Han Tai as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 初，中人尚未悟，會邊上諸將各以狀辭中尉，且言方屬希朝，中人始悟兵柄為叔文所奪，中尉乃止諸鎮無以兵馬入。

translations.literal: At first the eunuchs had not yet understood; then frontier generals each sent memorials declining the chief eunuch and saying they were now under Xichao's command; the eunuchs then realized military power had been seized by Shuwen, and the chief eunuch thereupon forbade the various commands to bring troops in.
translations.idiomatic: At first the eunuchs had not yet understood; then frontier generals each sent memorials declining the chief eunuch and saying they were now under Xichao's command; the eunuchs then realized military power had been seized by Shuwen, and the chief eunuch thereupon forbade the various commands to bring troops in.

sentences.zh: 希朝、韓泰已至奉天，諸將不至，乃還。

translations.literal: Xichao and Han Tai had already reached Fengtian, but the generals did not come; they then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao and Han Tai had already reached Fengtian, but the generals did not come; they then returned.

sentences.zh: 無幾，叔文母死。

translations.literal: Before long Shuwen's mother died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shuwen's mother died.

sentences.zh: 前一日，叔文置酒饌於翰林院，宴諸學士及內官李忠言、俱文珍、劉光奇等。

translations.literal: The day before, Shuwen set out food and drink in the Hanlin Academy and feasted the academicians and the inner eunuchs Li Zhongyan, Ju Wenjing, and Liu Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, Shuwen set out food and drink in the Hanlin Academy and feasted the academicians and the inner eunuchs Li Zhongyan, Ju Wenjing, and Liu Guangqi.

sentences.zh: 中飲，叔文白諸人曰：「叔文母疾病，比來盡心戮力為國家事，不避好惡難易者，欲以報聖人之重知也。

translations.literal: Mid-feast Shuwen addressed the assembly, saying: "My mother is ill. Lately I have devoted myself wholeheartedly to affairs of state, not shunning what is agreeable or difficult, wishing to repay the sage emperor's great trust.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-feast Shuwen addressed the assembly, saying, "My mother is ill. Lately I have devoted myself wholeheartedly to affairs of state, not shunning what is agreeable or difficult, wishing to repay the sage emperor's great trust.

sentences.zh: 若一去此職，百謗斯至，誰肯助叔文一言者，望諸君開懷見察。」

translations.literal: If I leave this post, a hundred slanders will at once arise—who will speak a word in my defense? I hope you gentlemen will open your hearts and understand."
translations.idiomatic: If I leave this post, a hundred slanders will at once arise—who will speak a word in my defense? I hope you gentlemen will open your hearts and understand."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「羊士諤非毀叔文，欲杖殺之，而韋執誼懦不遂。

translations.literal: He also said: "Yang Shiyu did not slander me; I wished to have him beaten to death, but Wei Zhiyi was cowardly and would not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Yang Shiyu did not slander me; I wished to have him beaten to death, but Wei Zhiyi was cowardly and would not carry it out.

sentences.zh: 叔文生平不識劉闢，乃以韋臯意求領三川，辟排門相幹，欲執叔文手，豈非兇人耶！

translations.literal: In life I never knew Liu Bi, yet at Wei Gao's request he sought to take command of the Three Rivers; Bi pushed through the gate to interfere and wished to seize my hand—is he not a violent man!
translations.idiomatic: In life I never knew Liu Bi, yet at Wei Gao's request he sought to take command of the Three Rivers; Bi pushed through the gate to interfere and wished to seize my hand—is he not a violent man!

sentences.zh: 叔文已令掃木場，將斬之，韋執誼苦執不可。」

translations.literal: I had already ordered the timber yard cleared to behead him, but Wei Zhiyi bitterly held fast and would not permit it."
translations.idiomatic: I had already ordered the timber yard cleared to behead him, but Wei Zhiyi bitterly held fast and would not permit it."

sentences.zh: 叔文無以對。

translations.literal: Shuwen had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen had no reply.

sentences.zh: 叔文未欲立皇太子。

translations.literal: Shuwen did not yet wish to establish a crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen did not yet wish to establish a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 順宗既久疾未平，群臣中外請立太子，既而詔下立廣陵王為太子，天下皆悅；

translations.literal: Shunzong had long been ill without recovery; court and countryside alike petitioned to establish a crown prince; soon an edict was issued establishing the Prince of Guangling as crown prince, and all under heaven rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong had long been ill without recovery; court and countryside alike petitioned to establish a crown prince; soon an edict was issued establishing the Prince of Guangling as crown prince, and all under heaven rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 叔文獨有憂色，而不敢言其事，但吟杜甫題諸葛亮祠堂詩末句云：「出師未捷身先死，長使英雄淚滿襟。」

translations.literal: Only Shuwen wore a troubled look and dared not speak of the matter; he merely recited the closing line of Du Fu's poem on Zhuge Liang's shrine: "He marched forth before victory was won, and died—forever leaving heroes with tears soaking their collars."
translations.idiomatic: Only Shuwen wore a troubled look and dared not speak of the matter; he merely recited the closing line of Du Fu's poem on Zhuge Liang's shrine, "He marched forth before victory was won, and died—forever leaving heroes with tears soaking their collars."

sentences.zh: 因歔欷泣下，人皆竊笑之。

translations.literal: He then sighed and wept; people all secretly laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: He then sighed and wept; people all secretly laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 皇太子監國，貶為渝州司戶，明年誅之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince supervised the state he was demoted to registrar of Yu Prefecture; the following year he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince supervised the state he was demoted to registrar of Yu Prefecture; the following year he was executed.

sentences.zh: 王伾，杭州人。

translations.literal: Wang Pi was a native of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi was a native of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 始為翰林侍書待詔，累遷至正議大夫、殿中丞、皇太子侍書。

translations.literal: He began as Hanlin attendant scribe awaiting summons; he was promoted successively to Regular Grand Master, Palace Aide, and tutor scribe to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Hanlin attendant scribe awaiting summons; he was promoted successively to Regular Grand Master, Palace Aide, and tutor scribe to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，遷左散騎常侍，依前翰林待詔。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant, retaining his former post as Hanlin attendant awaiting summons.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong took the throne he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant, retaining his former post as Hanlin attendant awaiting summons.

sentences.zh: 伾阘茸，不如叔文，唯招賄賂，無大志，貌寢陋，吳語，素為太子之所褻狎；

translations.literal: Pi was coarse and inferior, not matching Shuwen; he only solicited bribes and had no grand ambitions. His appearance was homely and ugly, he spoke the Wu dialect, and the crown prince had long treated him with familiar intimacy;
translations.idiomatic: Pi was crude and unimpressive compared with Shuwen; he did nothing but solicit bribes and had no great ambitions. He was homely and ugly, spoke the Wu dialect, and had long been on familiar terms with the crown prince;

sentences.zh: 而叔文頗任氣自許，粗知書，好言事，順宗稍敬之，不得如伾出入無間。

translations.literal: whereas Shuwen was rather headstrong and self-confident, had a rough knowledge of books, and liked to discuss affairs of state. Emperor Shunzong respected him somewhat but could not enjoy with him the same unobstructed access in and out as with Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen, by contrast, was headstrong and self-assured, knew books in a rough way, and liked to talk politics. Emperor Shunzong respected him somewhat, yet he could not come and go as freely as Pi.

sentences.zh: 叔文入止翰林，而伾入至柿林院，見李忠言、牛昭容等。

translations.literal: Shuwen on entering stopped at the Hanlin Academy, while Pi entered as far as the Persimmon Grove Academy to see Li Zhongyan, Niu Zhaorong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuwen entered the palace he stopped at the Hanlin Academy, while Pi went on to the Persimmon Grove Academy to see Li Zhongyan, Niu Zhaorong, and others.

sentences.zh: 然各有所主：伾主往來傳授；

translations.literal: Yet each had his role: Pi was in charge of relaying messages back and forth;
translations.idiomatic: Yet each had his role: Pi handled communication back and forth;

sentences.zh: 王叔文主決斷；

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen was in charge of making decisions;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen made the decisions;

sentences.zh: 韋執誼為文誥；

translations.literal: Wei Zhiyi drafted official documents;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyi drafted official documents;

sentences.zh: 劉禹錫、陳諫、韓曄、韓泰、柳宗元、房啟、淩準等謀議唱和，采聽外事。

translations.literal: Liu Yuxi, Chen Jian, Han Ye, Han Tai, Liu Zongyuan, Fang Qi, Ling Zhun, and others deliberated in concert, advising and appraising external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuxi, Chen Jian, Han Ye, Han Tai, Liu Zongyuan, Fang Qi, Ling Zhun, and others plotted together, advising and gathering intelligence on outside affairs.

sentences.zh: 而伾與叔文及諸朋黨之門，車馬填湊，而伾門尤盛，珍玩賂遺，歲時不絕。

translations.literal: The gates of Pi, Shuwen, and the other faction members were crowded with carriages and horses, and Pi's gate was especially busy; precious curios and gifts flowed in unceasingly throughout the year.
translations.idiomatic: The gates of Pi, Shuwen, and their faction were jammed with carriages and horses, Pi's gate most of all; precious gifts poured in without cease through the seasons.

sentences.zh: 室中為無門大櫃，唯開一竅，足以受物，以藏金寶，其妻或寢臥於上。

translations.literal: In his room he had a large cabinet without doors, opened only with a single aperture large enough to receive objects, used to store gold and jewels; his wife would sometimes sleep on top of it.
translations.idiomatic: In his room stood a doorless great cabinet with only a single opening large enough to pass things through, where he stored gold and jewels; his wife sometimes slept on top of it.

sentences.zh: 與叔文同貶開州司馬。

translations.literal: He was banished together with Shuwen to the post of aide to the prefect of Kai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished together with Shuwen to serve as aide to the prefect of Kai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王叔文最所重者，李景儉、呂溫。

translations.literal: Those Wang Shuwen valued most were Li Jingjian and Lü Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Those Wang Shuwen valued most were Li Jingjian and Lü Wen.

sentences.zh: 叔文用事時，景儉居喪於東都；

translations.literal: When Shuwen was in power, Jingjian was in mourning at the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: While Shuwen held power, Jingjian was in mourning at the Eastern Capital;

sentences.zh: 呂溫使吐蕃，留半歲，叔文敗方歸。

translations.literal: Lü Wen was on a mission to Tibet and stayed half a year; he returned only after Shuwen's fall.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wen was on a mission to Tibet and remained half a year, returning only after Shuwen's downfall.

sentences.zh: 陸質為皇太子侍讀，尋卒。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi served as tutor to the crown prince and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi served as tutor to the crown prince and soon died.

sentences.zh: 伾、叔文既逐，詔貶其黨韓曄饒州司馬，韓泰虔州司馬，陳諫臺州司馬，柳宗元永州司馬，劉禹錫朗州司馬，淩準連州司馬，程异郴州司馬，韋執誼崖州司馬。

translations.literal: After Pi and Shuwen were expelled, an edict banished their faction: Han Ye to aide of Rao Prefecture, Han Tai to aide of Qian Prefecture, Chen Jian to aide of Tai Prefecture, Liu Zongyuan to aide of Yong Prefecture, Liu Yuxi to aide of Lang Prefecture, Ling Zhun to aide of Lian Prefecture, Cheng Yi to aide of Chen Prefecture, and Wei Zhiyi to aide of Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Pi and Shuwen were expelled, an edict banished their faction: Han Ye as aide to the prefect of Rao, Han Tai as aide to Qian, Chen Jian as aide to Tai, Liu Zongyuan as aide to Yong, Liu Yuxi as aide to Lang, Ling Zhun as aide to Lian, Cheng Yi as aide to Chen, and Wei Zhiyi as aide to Ya.

sentences.zh: 韓曄，宰相滉之族子，有俊才，依附韋執誼，累遷尚書司封郎中。

translations.literal: Han Ye was a clansman of Chancellor Han Huang's son; he had outstanding talent, attached himself to Wei Zhiyi, and was promoted repeatedly to Director of the Ministry of Rites' Department of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ye was a clansman of Chancellor Han Huang's family; gifted and ambitious, he attached himself to Wei Zhiyi and rose to Director of the Department of Enfeoffment in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 叔文敗，貶池州刺史，尋改饒州司馬，量移汀州刺史，又轉永州卒。

translations.literal: After Shuwen's fall he was demoted to prefect of Chi Prefecture, soon changed to aide of Rao Prefecture, transferred by measure to prefect of Ting Prefecture, then moved again to Yong Prefecture, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuwen's fall he was demoted to prefect of Chi, soon reassigned as aide of Rao, transferred by measure to prefect of Ting, then moved again to Yong, where he died.

sentences.zh: 陳諫至叔文敗，已出為河中少尹，自臺州司馬量移封州刺史，轉通州卒。

translations.literal: By the time Chen Jian fell with Shuwen he had already gone out as vice governor of Hezhong; from aide of Tai Prefecture he was transferred by measure to prefect of Feng Prefecture, then moved to Tong Prefecture, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Chen Jian fell with Shuwen he had already left office as vice governor of Hezhong; from aide of Tai he was transferred by measure to prefect of Feng, then moved to Tong, where he died.

sentences.zh: 淩準，貞元二十年自浙東觀察判官、侍御史召入，王叔文與準有舊，引用為翰林學士，轉員外郎。

translations.literal: Ling Zhun, in the twentieth year of Zhenyuan, was summoned from Zhedong observation aide and attendant censor; Wang Shuwen, who had old ties with Zhun, brought him in as Hanlin academician and then promoted him to supernumerary official.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Zhenyuan, Ling Zhun was summoned from his posts as Zhedong observation aide and attendant censor; Wang Shuwen, who had known him before, brought him in as Hanlin academician and then promoted him to supernumerary official.

sentences.zh: 坐叔文貶連州。

translations.literal: He was implicated in Shuwen's case and banished to Lian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in Shuwen's case, he was banished to Lian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 準有史學，尚古文，撰《邠志》二卷。

translations.literal: Zhun had learning in history, favored ancient-style prose, and compiled the Bin Gazetteer in two scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun was learned in history, favored ancient-style prose, and compiled the Bin Gazetteer in two scrolls.

sentences.zh: 韓泰，貞元中累遷至戶部郎中，王叔文用為範希朝神策行營節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Han Tai, in the Zhenyuan era, was promoted repeatedly to Director of the Ministry of Revenue; Wang Shuwen employed him as military aide to Fan Xichao, commander of the Shence expeditionary forces.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan, Han Tai rose repeatedly to Director of the Ministry of Revenue; Wang Shuwen appointed him military aide to Fan Xichao, commander of the Shence expeditionary forces.

sentences.zh: 泰最有籌畫，能決陰事，深為伾、叔文之所重，坐貶，自虔州司馬量移漳州刺史，遷郴州。

translations.literal: Tai was most skilled in planning and could decide covert affairs; Pi and Shuwen valued him deeply. Implicated in banishment, he was transferred by measure from aide of Qian Prefecture to prefect of Zhang Prefecture, then moved to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was the best planner among them and could settle secret matters; Pi and Shuwen relied on him heavily. After banishment he was transferred by measure from aide of Qian to prefect of Zhang, then moved to Chen.

sentences.zh: 柳宗元、劉禹錫自有傳。

translations.literal: Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi have their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 程异，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍父疾，鄉里以孝悌稱。

translations.literal: He once attended his father in illness and was praised in his home district for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He once nursed his father through illness and was praised in his home district for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 明經及第，釋褐揚州海陵主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the classics examination, took his first office as recorder of Hailing in Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the classics examination and took his first post as recorder of Hailing in Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登《開元禮》科，授華州鄭縣尉。

translations.literal: He passed the Kaiyuan Rites examination and was appointed bailiff of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Kaiyuan Rites examination and was appointed bailiff of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 精於吏職，剖判無滯。

translations.literal: He was skilled in administrative duties and rendered judgments without delay.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in administrative work and rendered judgments without delay.

sentences.zh: 杜確刺同州，帥河中，皆從為賓佐。

translations.literal: When Du Que governed Tong Prefecture and then commanded Hezhong, Yi followed him as staff aide in both posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Que governed Tong Prefecture and then commanded Hezhong, Yi served as his staff aide in both posts.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，擢授監察御史，遷虞部員外郎，充鹽鐵轉運、揚子院留後。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan he was promoted to investigating censor, then Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, and acting salt and iron transport commissioner and Yangzi depot superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhenyuan he was promoted to investigating censor, then Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, and acting salt and iron transport commissioner and Yangzi depot superintendent.

sentences.zh: 時王叔文用事，由逕放利者皆附之，异亦被引用。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shuwen was in power; all who profited by irregular means attached themselves to him, and Yi too was brought into service.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Shuwen held power; everyone who profited by irregular means attached himself to Shuwen, and Yi too was brought into service.

sentences.zh: 叔文敗，坐貶岳州刺史，改郴州司馬。

translations.literal: After Shuwen's fall he was implicated and demoted to prefect of Yue Prefecture, then changed to aide of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuwen's fall he was implicated and demoted to prefect of Yue, then reassigned as aide of Chen.

sentences.zh: 元和初，鹽鐵使李巽薦異曉達錢穀，請棄瑕錄用，擢為侍御史，復為揚子留後，累檢校兵部郎中、淮南等五道兩稅使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, salt commissioner Li Xun recommended Yi as expert in currency and grain accounts and asked that his faults be overlooked and his talent employed; he was promoted to attendant censor, again made Yangzi depot superintendent, and successively made acting Director of the Ministry of War and dual-tax commissioner for the five circuits of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe, salt commissioner Li Xun recommended Yi as expert in currency and grain accounts and asked that his faults be overlooked; he was promoted to attendant censor, again made Yangzi depot superintendent, and successively made acting Director of the Ministry of War and dual-tax commissioner for the five Huainan circuits.

sentences.zh: 异自悔前非，厲己竭節，江淮錢穀之弊，多所鏟革。

translations.literal: Yi repented his former errors, disciplined himself and devoted his integrity; he reformed many abuses in Jianghuai currency and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yi repented his former errors, disciplined himself, and devoted his integrity; he reformed many abuses in Jianghuai currency and grain.

sentences.zh: 入為太府少卿、太卿，轉衛尉卿，兼御史中丞，充鹽鐵轉運副使。

translations.literal: He entered service as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then Director, then Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and deputy salt and iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then Director, then Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and deputy salt and iron transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時淮西用兵，國用不足，异使江表以調征賦，且諷有土者以饒羨入貢，至則不剝下，不浚財，經費以贏，人頗便之。

translations.literal: At that time troops were deployed in Huai-Xi and state revenue was insufficient; Yi went to the lower Yangzi to adjust tax levies and also urged landowners to contribute surplus wealth as tribute. When he arrived he did not strip the people below or drain wealth; expenses were met with surplus, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: At that time troops were deployed in Huai-Xi and state revenue was insufficient; Yi went to the lower Yangzi to adjust tax levies and urged landowners to contribute surplus wealth as tribute. When he arrived he did not strip the common people or drain wealth; expenses were met with surplus, and the people found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 由是專領鹽鐵轉運使、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: From this he was given sole charge as salt and iron transport commissioner, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: From this he was given sole charge as salt and iron transport commissioner, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年九月，轉工部侍郎、同中書門下平章事，領使如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and Regular Second-Rank Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, retaining his commission as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and Regular Second-Rank Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, retaining his commission as before.

sentences.zh: 議者以異起錢穀吏，一旦位冠百僚，人情大為不可。

translations.literal: Commentators held that Yi had risen from a grain-and-currency clerk to rank above the hundred officials at a stroke; public sentiment found this greatly unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that Yi had risen from a grain-and-currency clerk to rank above the hundred officials overnight; public sentiment found this deeply unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 異自知叨據，以謙遜自牧，月餘日，不敢知印秉筆。

translations.literal: Yi knew he had received an unmerited post and cultivated humility; for more than a month he dared not handle the seal or wield the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had received an unmerited post, Yi cultivated humility; for more than a month he dared not handle the seal or wield the brush.

sentences.zh: 异知西北邊軍政不理，建議置巡邊使，上問誰可使者，异請自行。

translations.literal: Yi knew that military administration on the northwestern frontier was in disorder and proposed establishing frontier inspection commissioners; when the emperor asked who could be sent, Yi requested to go himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yi knew military administration on the northwestern frontier was in disorder and proposed establishing frontier inspection commissioners; when the emperor asked who could be sent, Yi volunteered to go himself.

sentences.zh: 議未決，無疾而卒，元和十四年四月也。

translations.literal: Before the proposal was decided he died without illness, in the fourth month of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Before the proposal was decided he died without illness, in the fourth month of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 贈左僕射，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 异性廉約，歿官第，家無餘財，人士多之。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was frugal and restrained; he died in his official residence with no surplus wealth, and men of standing praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's nature was frugal and restrained; he died in his official residence with no surplus wealth, and men of standing praised him.

sentences.zh: 皇甫鎛，安定朝那人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo was a native of Chaona in Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo was a native of Chaona in Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖鄰幾，汝州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Linji was prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Linji was prefect of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父愉，常州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yu was prefect of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was prefect of Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鎛貞元初登進士第，登賢良文學制科，授監察御史。

translations.literal: Bo at the beginning of Zhenyuan passed the jinshi examination and the special examination in worthy and cultivated literary composition, and was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Bo at the beginning of Zhenyuan passed the jinshi examination and the special examination in worthy and cultivated literary composition, and was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，免喪，坐居喪時薄遊，除詹事府司直。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office for mourning; after mourning ended he was punished for light travel during mourning and was appointed aide of straight conduct in the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office for mourning; after mourning ended he was punished for light travel during mourning and was appointed aide of straight conduct in the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部員外郎、判南曹，凡三年，頗鈐制奸吏。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and controller of the Southern Bureau; for three years in all he kept corrupt clerks firmly in check.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and controller of the Southern Bureau; for three years in all he kept corrupt clerks firmly in check.

sentences.zh: 改吏部郎中，三遷司農卿、兼御史中丞，賜金紫，判度支，俄拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted three times to Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries, Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, granted the gold seal and purple ribbon, and given charge of the Department of Public Works; soon he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted three times to Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries, Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, granted the gold seal and purple ribbon, and given charge of the Department of Public Works; soon he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時方討淮西，切於饋運，鎛勾剝嚴急，儲供辦集，益承寵遇，加兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: At that time the Huai-Xi campaign was underway and supply transport was urgent; Bo's exactions were severe and strict, stores were assembled, and his favor increased; he was additionally made Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Huai-Xi campaign was underway and supply transport was urgent; Bo's exactions were severe and strict, stores were assembled, and his favor increased; he was additionally made Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，與鹽鐵使程异同日以本官同平章事，領使如故。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he and salt commissioner Cheng Yi were on the same day made Regular Second-Rank Counselors in their existing offices, retaining their commissions as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he and salt commissioner Cheng Yi were on the same day made Regular Second-Rank Counselors in their existing offices, retaining their commissions as before.

sentences.zh: 鎛雖有吏才，素無公望，特以聚斂媚上，刻削希恩。

translations.literal: Though Bo had administrative talent, he had never enjoyed public esteem; he relied solely on amassing revenue to flatter the emperor and on harsh exactions to seek favor.
translations.idiomatic: Though Bo had administrative talent, he had never enjoyed public esteem; he relied solely on amassing revenue to flatter the emperor and on harsh exactions to seek favor.

sentences.zh: 詔書既下，物情駭異，至於賈販無識，亦相嗤誚。

translations.literal: Once the edict was issued, public sentiment was shocked and dismayed; even peddlers without understanding joined in ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Once the edict was issued, public sentiment was shocked and dismayed; even ignorant peddlers joined in ridicule.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔群、裴度以物議上聞，憲宗怒而不聽。

translations.literal: Chancellors Cui Qun and Pei Du reported public opinion to the throne; Emperor Xianzong was angry and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Cui Qun and Pei Du reported public opinion to the throne; Emperor Xianzong was angry and would not listen.

sentences.zh: 度上疏乞罷知政事，因論之曰：

translations.literal: Pei Du submitted a memorial requesting to be relieved of his duties in governance, and in the course of argument wrote:
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du submitted a memorial requesting to be relieved of his duties in governance, and in the course of argument wrote:

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下睿哲文明，唯在所授，凡所閱視，洞達無遺。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty is wise, perceptive, and cultivated in the arts; whatever you appoint, whatever you examine, you penetrate completely without omission.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit that Your Majesty is wise, perceptive, and cultivated in the arts; whatever you appoint, whatever you examine, you see through completely without omission.

sentences.zh: 所以比來選任宰相，縱道不周物，才不濟時，公望所歸，皆有可取。

translations.literal: Therefore in recent selections of chancellors, even if their conduct did not embrace all things or their talents did not meet the needs of the times, those in whom public esteem converged all had something to commend them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in recent selections of chancellors, even when conduct did not embrace all things or talent did not meet the needs of the times, those in whom public esteem converged all had something to commend them.

sentences.zh: 況皇甫鎛自掌財賦，唯事割剝，以苛為察，以刻為明。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Huangfu Bo took charge of fiscal affairs, he has devoted himself only to extortion—taking harshness as discernment and severity as clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since Huangfu Bo took charge of fiscal affairs, he has devoted himself only to extortion—taking harshness for discernment and severity for clarity.

sentences.zh: 自京北、京西城鎮及百司並遠近州府，應是仰給度支之處，無不苦口切齒，願食其肉；

translations.literal: From the garrisons north and west of the capital and from the hundred offices to distant and nearby prefectures—every place that depends on supplies from the Department of Public Works—none fail to gnash their teeth in bitterness and wish to eat his flesh;
translations.idiomatic: From the garrisons north and west of the capital and from the hundred offices to distant and nearby prefectures—every place that depends on supplies from the Department of Public Works—none fail to gnash their teeth in bitterness and wish to eat his flesh;

sentences.zh: 猶賴臣等每加勸誡，或為奏論，庶事之中，抑令通濟。

translations.literal: we have still relied on us repeatedly to admonish and counsel, or to memorialize on their behalf, restraining matters so that supplies could get through.
translations.idiomatic: we have still had to admonish and counsel repeatedly, or memorialize on their behalf, restraining matters so that supplies could get through.

sentences.zh: 比者淮西諸軍糧料，所破五成錢，其實只與一成、兩成，士卒怨怒，皆欲離叛。

translations.literal: Recently the grain funds of the Huai-Xi armies were supposed to be disbursed at fifty percent, but in fact only ten or twenty percent were given; the soldiers were resentful and angry and all wished to desert.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the grain funds of the Huai-Xi armies were supposed to be disbursed at fifty percent, but in fact only ten or twenty percent were given; the soldiers were resentful and angry and all wished to desert.

sentences.zh: 臣到行營，方且慰喻，直其遷延不進，供軍漸難，俱能前行，必有優賞，以此約定，然後切勒供軍官，且支九月一日兩成已上錢，俱容努力，方將小安，不然必有潰散。

translations.literal: When I reached the expeditionary camp I was just comforting and instructing them; I excused their delay in advancing, explained that supply was growing difficult, promised that if they all advanced there would certainly be generous rewards, and on that basis made an agreement; then I strictly ordered the supply officers to disburse at least twenty percent of the funds due on the first day of the ninth month, so that with effort they might find some relief—otherwise there would certainly be collapse and dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: When I reached the expeditionary camp I was just comforting and instructing them; I excused their delay in advancing, explained that supply was growing difficult, promised generous rewards if they all advanced, and on that basis made an agreement; then I strictly ordered the supply officers to disburse at least twenty percent of the funds due on the first day of the ninth month, so that with effort they might find some relief—otherwise there would certainly be collapse and dispersal.

sentences.zh: 今舊兵悉向淄青討伐，忽聞此人入相，則必相與驚擾，以為更有前時之事，則無告訴之憂。

translations.literal: Now the veteran troops are all marching to campaign against Ziqing; if they suddenly hear this man has entered the chancellorship, they will surely be alarmed together, thinking there will be more of what happened before—then there will be no recourse for their complaints.
translations.idiomatic: Now the veteran troops are all marching to campaign against Ziqing; if they suddenly hear this man has entered the chancellorship, they will surely be alarmed together, thinking there will be more of what happened before—then there will be no recourse for their complaints.

sentences.zh: 雖侵刻不少，然漏落亦多，所以罷兵之後，經費錢數一千三十萬貫，此事猶可。

translations.literal: Though his exactions were considerable, his leakages were also great; thus after the troops were disbanded there remained 10.3 million strings of cash in expenses—this matter is still tolerable.
translations.idiomatic: Though his exactions were considerable, his leakages were also great; thus after the troops were disbanded there remained 10.3 million strings of cash in expenses—this matter is still tolerable.

sentences.zh: 直以性惟狡詐，言不誠實，朝三暮四，天下共知，惟能上惑聖聰，足見奸邪之極。

translations.literal: It is simply that his nature is solely crafty and deceitful, his words insincere—changing morning and evening, known to all under Heaven; that he can only delude the sacred understanding shows the extreme of wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply that his nature is solely crafty and deceitful, his words insincere—changing morning and evening, known to all under Heaven; that he can only delude the sacred understanding shows the extreme of wickedness.

sentences.zh: 程异雖人品凡俗，然心事和平，處之煩劇，或亦得力，但升之相位，便在公卿之上，實亦非宜。

translations.literal: Though Cheng Yi is vulgar in character, his mind is peaceful, and in handling demanding affairs he may prove useful; but to raise him to the chancellorship, placing him above the highest nobles, is truly also inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cheng Yi is vulgar in character, his mind is peaceful, and in handling demanding affairs he may prove useful; but to raise him to the chancellorship, placing him above the highest nobles, is truly also inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 如皇甫镈，天下之人，怨入骨髓，陛下今日收為股肱，列在臺鼎，切恐不可，伏惟圖之。

translations.literal: As for Huangfu Bo—the people of the realm hate him to the marrow; if Your Majesty today takes him as your arm and leg and seats him among the highest ministers, I fear deeply this cannot be done—I beg Your Majesty to consider it.
translations.idiomatic: As for Huangfu Bo—the people of the realm hate him to the marrow; if Your Majesty today takes him as your arm and leg and seats him among the highest ministers, I fear deeply this cannot be done—I beg Your Majesty to consider it.

sentences.zh: 倘陛下納臣懇款，速賜移易，以副天下之望，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty accepts my earnest plea and promptly grants a change, fulfilling the hopes of all under Heaven, then the realm will be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty accepts my earnest plea and promptly grants a change, fulfilling the hopes of all under Heaven, then the realm will be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 伏聞李翛疾病，亦求入來，如浙西觀察使，且與亦得。

translations.literal: I have heard that Li Xiao is ill and also seeks to return from his post; appointment as Zhexi observation commissioner, or the like, would also be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Li Xiao is ill and also seeks to return from his post; appointment as Zhexi observation commissioner, or the like, would also be acceptable.

sentences.zh: 臣知一言出口，必犯天威，但使言行，甘心獲戾。

translations.literal: I know that one word from my mouth will surely offend celestial wrath, but so long as my words match my deeds, I willingly accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I know that one word from my mouth will surely offend celestial wrath, but so long as my words match my deeds, I willingly accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 今者臣若不退，天下之人謂臣有負恩寵；

translations.literal: If I do not withdraw now, the people of the realm will say I have betrayed Your Majesty's grace and favor;
translations.idiomatic: If I do not withdraw now, the people of the realm will say I have betrayed Your Majesty's grace and favor;

sentences.zh: 今退毀未許，言又不聽，如火燒心，若箭攢體。

translations.literal: yet withdrawal is not permitted and my words are not heeded—it is like fire burning my heart, like arrows piercing my body.
translations.idiomatic: yet withdrawal is not permitted and my words are not heeded—it is like fire burning my heart, like arrows piercing my body.

sentences.zh: 臣自無足惜，惜陛下今日事勢。

translations.literal: I myself am not worth regretting; what I regret is Your Majesty's present situation.
translations.idiomatic: I myself am not worth regretting; what I regret is Your Majesty's present situation.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 淮西蕩定，河北咸寧，承宗斂手削地，程權束身赴闕，韓弘輿疾討賊，此豈京師氣力能制其命，祗是朝廷處置能服其心。

translations.literal: Huai-Xi has been pacified, Hebei is at peace, Chengzong has submitted and surrendered territory, Cheng Quan has bound himself and come to court, and Han Hong, though ill, has campaigned against the rebels—this is not because the capital's strength alone could command their lives, but because the court's handling could win their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Huai-Xi has been pacified, Hebei is at peace, Chengzong has submitted and surrendered territory, Cheng Quan has bound himself and come to court, and Han Hong, though ill, has campaigned against the rebels—this is not because the capital's strength alone could command their lives, but because the court's handling could win their hearts.

sentences.zh: 今既開中興，再造區夏，陛下何忍卻自破除，使億萬之眾離心，四方諸侯解體？

translations.literal: Now that restoration has begun and the realm is being rebuilt, how can Your Majesty bear to destroy it yourself, causing hundreds of millions to lose heart and the lords of the four quarters to disintegrate?
translations.idiomatic: Now that restoration has begun and the realm is being rebuilt, how can Your Majesty bear to destroy it yourself, causing hundreds of millions to lose heart and the lords of the four quarters to disintegrate?

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，皆欲慟哭。

translations.literal: All the gentlemen wish to weep in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: All the gentlemen wish to weep in anguish.

sentences.zh: 況陛下任臣之意，豈比常人；

translations.literal: Moreover, the trust Your Majesty places in me—is it comparable to that of ordinary men?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the trust Your Majesty places in me—is it comparable to that of ordinary men?

sentences.zh: 臣事陛下之心，敢同眾士？

translations.literal: The devotion with which I serve Your Majesty—dare I be the same as the multitude?
translations.idiomatic: The devotion with which I serve Your Majesty—dare I be the same as the multitude?

sentences.zh: 所以昧死重封以聞，如不足觀，臣當引領受責。

translations.literal: Therefore I risk death to seal this again and report it; if it is not worth considering, I shall stretch my neck to accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I risk death to seal this again and report it; if it is not worth considering, I shall stretch my neck to accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 陛下引一市肆商徒，與臣同列，在臣亦有何損，陛下實有所傷，不勝憤懣惶恐之至。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has brought in a marketplace peddler to rank with me—what loss is that to me? But Your Majesty will truly be harmed. I am overwhelmed with indignation, distress, and dread beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has brought in a marketplace peddler to rank with me—what loss is that to me? But Your Majesty will truly be harmed. I am overwhelmed with indignation, distress, and dread beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 時憲宗以世道漸平，欲肆意娛樂，池臺館宇，稍增崇飾，而异、鎛探知上旨，數貢羨餘，以備經構，故帝獨排物議相之；

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xianzong, believing the age was growing peaceful, wished to indulge freely in pleasure; pools, terraces, and halls were gradually made more splendid, and Yi and Bo, discerning the emperor's intent, repeatedly presented surplus revenue to supply construction—therefore the emperor alone overrode public opinion to make them chancellors;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xianzong, believing the age was growing peaceful, wished to indulge freely in pleasure; pools, terraces, and halls were gradually made more splendid, and Yi and Bo, discerning the emperor's intent, repeatedly presented surplus revenue to supply construction—therefore the emperor alone overrode public opinion to make them chancellors;

sentences.zh: 見裴度疏，以為朋黨，竟不省覽。

translations.literal: when he saw Pei Du's memorial he took it for factionalism and would not read it at all.
translations.idiomatic: when he saw Pei Du's memorial he took it for factionalism and would not read it at all.

sentences.zh: 鎛知公議不可，益以巧媚自固，奏減內外官俸錢以贍國用；

translations.literal: Bo knew public opinion could not be withstood and all the more used clever flattery to secure himself; he memorialized to reduce the salary payments of inner and outer officials to supply state expenses;
translations.idiomatic: Bo knew public opinion could not be withstood and all the more used clever flattery to secure himself; he memorialized to reduce the salary payments of inner and outer officials to supply state expenses;

sentences.zh: 敕下，給事中崔祐封還詔書，其事方罷。

translations.literal: once the edict was issued, Supervising Secretary Cui You returned the edict unapproved, and the matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: once the edict was issued, Supervising Secretary Cui You returned the edict unapproved, and the matter was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 時內出積年庫物付度支估價，例皆陳朽，鎛盡以善價買之，以給邊軍。

translations.literal: At that time stored goods from years past in the inner treasury were handed to the Department of Public Works for valuation; by rule they were all decayed and worn, yet Bo bought them all at good prices to supply the border armies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time stored goods from years past in the inner treasury were handed to the Department of Public Works for valuation; by rule they were all decayed and worn, yet Bo bought them all at good prices to supply the border armies.

sentences.zh: 羅縠繒彩，觸風斷裂，隨手散壞，軍士怨怒，皆聚而焚之。

translations.literal: Silks and brocades snapped and tore at a touch and fell apart in the hand; the soldiers were resentful and angry and all gathered to burn them.
translations.idiomatic: Silks and brocades snapped and tore at a touch and fell apart in the hand; the soldiers were resentful and angry and all gathered to burn them.

sentences.zh: 裴度奏事，因言邊軍焚賜之意，鎛因引其足奏曰：「此靴乃內庫出者，臣以俸二千買之，堅韌可以久服，所言不可用，皆詐也。」

translations.literal: Pei Du was reporting on affairs and spoke of the border troops' burning of gifts; Huangfu Bo then drew up his foot and memorialized: "These boots came from the inner treasury; I bought them for two thousand strings of my salary—they are sturdy and durable for long wear. What has been said about their uselessness is all fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du was reporting on affairs and spoke of the border troops' burning of gifts; Huangfu Bo then drew up his foot and memorialized, "These boots came from the inner treasury; I bought them for two thousand strings of my salary—they are sturdy and durable for long wear. What has been said about their uselessness is all fraud."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，由是鎛益無忌憚。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct, and from this Bo became all the more unbridled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought this correct, and from this Bo became all the more unbridled.

sentences.zh: 裴度有用兵伐叛之功，鎛心嫉之，與宰相李逢吉、令狐楚合勢擠度出鎮太原。

translations.literal: Pei Du had merit in campaigning against rebellion; Bo resented him in his heart and, with chancellors Li Fengji and Linghu Chu, combined forces to force Du out to command Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du had merit in campaigning against rebellion; Bo resented him in his heart and, with chancellors Li Fengji and Linghu Chu, combined forces to force Du out to command Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 崔群有公望，為搢紳所重，屢言時政之弊，鎛惡之，因議憲宗尊號，乃奏曰：「昨群臣議上徽號，崔群於陛下惜『孝德』兩字。」

translations.literal: Cui Qun enjoyed public esteem and was respected by the gentry; he repeatedly spoke of abuses in current policy, and Bo hated him; on the occasion of deliberating Emperor Xianzong's honorific title he memorialized: "When the officials recently deliberated the honorific title, Cui Qun begrudged Your Majesty the two characters 'Filial' and 'Virtuous.'"
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun enjoyed public esteem and was respected by the gentry; he repeatedly spoke of abuses in current policy, and Bo hated him; on the occasion of deliberating Emperor Xianzong's honorific title he memorialized, "When the officials recently deliberated the honorific title, Cui Qun begrudged Your Majesty the two characters 'Filial' and 'Virtuous.'"

sentences.zh: 憲宗怒，黜群為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was angry and demoted Qun to Zhexi observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was angry and demoted Qun to Zhexi observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又與金吾將軍李道古恊為奸謀，薦引方士柳泌、僧大通，言可致長生。

translations.literal: He also joined with Gold Crowns General Li Daogu in wicked plotting, recommending and bringing in the adept Liu Bi and the monk Datong, saying they could bring long life.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined with Gold Crowns General Li Daogu in wicked plotting, recommending and bringing in the adept Liu Bi and the monk Datong, saying they could bring long life.

sentences.zh: 中尉吐突承璀恩寵莫二，鎛厚賂結其歡心，故及相位。

translations.literal: Chief Palace Intendant Tuchi Chenghui enjoyed favor without rival; Bo lavished bribes to win his goodwill, and thus reached the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Palace Intendant Tuchi Chenghui enjoyed favor without rival; Bo lavished bribes to win his goodwill, and thus reached the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 穆宗在東宮，備聞鎛之奸邪，及居諒闇，聽政之日，詔：「皇甫鎛器本凡近，性惟險狹，行靡所顧，文無可觀，雖早踐朝倫，而素乖公望。

translations.literal: Muzong, while heir apparent, had fully heard of Bo's wickedness; on the day he assumed mourning and began to govern, an edict read: "Huangfu Bo's capacity is fundamentally commonplace, his nature solely treacherous and narrow, his conduct heedless of consequences, his writing unworthy of note; though he long trod the court ranks, he had always fallen short of public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong, while heir apparent, had fully heard of Bo's wickedness; on the day he assumed mourning and began to govern, an edict read, "Huangfu Bo's capacity is fundamentally commonplace, his nature solely treacherous and narrow, his conduct heedless of consequences, his writing unworthy of note; though he long trod the court ranks, he had always fallen short of public esteem.

sentences.zh: 自掌邦計，屬當軍興，以剝下為徇公，既鼓眾怒；

translations.literal: Once he took charge of state finance, at a time of military mobilization, he made stripping the people below his public service and thereby roused the anger of the masses;
translations.idiomatic: Once he took charge of state finance, at a time of military mobilization, he made stripping the people below his public service and thereby roused the anger of the masses;

sentences.zh: 以矯跡為孤立，用塞人言。

translations.literal: he used affected conduct to pose as isolated, thereby silencing men's words.
translations.idiomatic: he used affected conduct to pose as isolated, thereby silencing men's words.

sentences.zh: 洎塵臺司，益蠹時政，不知經國之大體，不慮安邊之遠圖，三軍多凍餒之憂，百姓深雕瘵之弊。

translations.literal: When he reached the censorate he further corrupted current policy, ignorant of the great principles of governing the state and heedless of the far-reaching plan of securing the borders; the three armies suffered much from cold and hunger, and the common people bore deep wounds of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the censorate he further corrupted current policy, ignorant of the great principles of governing the state and heedless of the far-reaching plan of securing the borders; the three armies suffered much from cold and hunger, and the common people bore deep wounds of ruin.

sentences.zh: 事皆罔蔽，言悉虛誣，遠近咸知，朝野同怨。

translations.literal: His affairs were all concealed and deceived, his words entirely false; near and far alike knew it, court and countryside shared the resentment.
translations.idiomatic: His affairs were all concealed and deceived, his words entirely false; near and far alike knew it, court and countryside shared the resentment.

sentences.zh: 而又恣求方士，上惑先朝，潛通奸人，罪在難舍。

translations.literal: Moreover he recklessly sought out adepts, deluding the former emperor, and secretly communicated with wicked men—crimes that cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he recklessly sought out adepts, deluding the former emperor, and secretly communicated with wicked men—crimes that cannot be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 合加竄殛，以正刑章，俾黜遐荒，尚存寬典。」

translations.literal: He should be further banished and executed to rectify the penal code; yet demotion to remote exile still preserves the lenient statute."
translations.idiomatic: He should be further banished and executed to rectify the penal code; yet demotion to remote exile still preserves the lenient statute."

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「山人柳泌輒懷左道，上惑先朝，固求牧人，貴欲疑眾，自知虛誕，仍便奔逃。

translations.literal: Another edict read: "The mountain man Liu Bi presumptuously harbored heterodox ways, deluding the former emperor; he insisted on governing the people, clearly intending to deceive the multitude; knowing his own fraud, he then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read, "The mountain man Liu Bi presumptuously harbored heterodox ways, deluding the former emperor; he insisted on governing the people, clearly intending to deceive the multitude; knowing his own fraud, he then fled.

sentences.zh: 僧大通醫方不精，藥術皆妄。

translations.literal: The monk Datong was unskilled in medical formulas; his drug arts were all false.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Datong was unskilled in medical formulas; his drug arts were all false.

sentences.zh: 既延禍釁，俱是奸邪，邦國固有常刑，人神所宜共棄，宜付京兆府決重杖一頓處死。」

translations.literal: Having brought calamity and offense, both are wicked men; the state has its regular punishments, and gods and men alike should cast them out—let the metropolitan prefecture decide: heavy beating once, then execution."
translations.idiomatic: Having brought calamity and offense, both are wicked men; the state has its regular punishments, and gods and men alike should cast them out—let the metropolitan prefecture decide: heavy beating once, then execution."

sentences.zh: 柳泌本曰楊仁力，少習醫術，言多誕妄。

translations.literal: Liu Bi was originally named Yang Renli; in youth he studied medicine and his words were mostly wild and false.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bi was originally named Yang Renli; in youth he studied medicine and his words were mostly wild and false.

sentences.zh: 李道古奸回巧宦，與泌密謀求進，言之於皇甫镈，因征入禁中。

translations.literal: Li Daogu was a treacherous and crafty official; he plotted secretly with Bi to seek advancement and spoke of him to Huangfu Bo, who then summoned him into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daogu was a treacherous and crafty official; he plotted secretly with Bi to seek advancement and spoke of him to Huangfu Bo, who then summoned him into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 自雲能致靈藥，言：「天臺山多靈草，君仙所會，臣嘗知之，而力不能致。

translations.literal: He claimed he could obtain elixir drugs and said: "Mount Tiantai has many spirit herbs and is where immortals gather; I have known this, but my strength could not obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed he could obtain elixir drugs and said, "Mount Tiantai has many spirit herbs and is where immortals gather; I have known this, but my strength could not obtain them.

sentences.zh: 願為天臺長吏，因以求之。」

translations.literal: I wish to become prefect of Tiantai and thereby seek them."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to become prefect of Tiantai and thereby seek them."

sentences.zh: 起徒步為臺州刺史，仍賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was raised from commoner to prefect of Tai Prefecture and also granted the gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised from commoner to prefect of Tai Prefecture and also granted the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 諫官論奏曰：「列聖亦有好方士者，亦與官號，未嘗令賦政臨民。」

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials memorialized: "The successive sage emperors also had adepts they favored and gave them titles, but they never let them govern and face the people."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials memorialized, "The successive sage emperors also had adepts they favored and gave them titles, but they never let them govern and face the people."

sentences.zh: 憲宗曰：「煩一郡之力而致神仙長年，臣子於君父何愛焉！」

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong said: "What is troubling one prefecture's resources to obtain immortality and long life—what would a subject withhold from his lord and father!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong said, "What is troubling one prefecture's resources to obtain immortality and long life—what would a subject withhold from his lord and father!"

sentences.zh: 由是莫取有言者。

translations.literal: From this no one dared speak further.
translations.idiomatic: From this no one dared speak further.

sentences.zh: 裴潾以極言被黜。

translations.literal: Pei Zuan was demoted for speaking to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zuan was demoted for speaking to the limit.

sentences.zh: 泌到天臺，驅役吏民於山谷間，聲言采藥，鞭笞躁急。

translations.literal: When Bi reached Tiantai he drove officials and commoners in the mountain valleys, claiming to gather herbs, with urgent beatings.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi reached Tiantai he drove officials and commoners in the mountain valleys, claiming to gather herbs, with urgent beatings.

sentences.zh: 歲余一無所得，懼詐發獲罪，舉家入山谷。

translations.literal: After more than a year he obtained nothing; fearing exposure of his fraud and punishment, he took his whole family into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he obtained nothing; fearing exposure of his fraud and punishment, he took his whole family into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 浙東觀察使追捕，送於京師，镈與李道古懇保證之，必能可致靈藥，乃待詔翰林院。

translations.literal: The Zhedong observation commissioner pursued and sent him to the capital; Bo and Li Daogu earnestly guaranteed that he could certainly obtain elixir drugs, and so he awaited orders in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhedong observation commissioner pursued and sent him to the capital; Bo and Li Daogu earnestly guaranteed that he could certainly obtain elixir drugs, and so he awaited orders in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 憲宗服泌藥，日益煩躁，喜怒不常，內官懼非罪見戮，遂為弒逆。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong took Bi's drugs and grew daily more restless; his joy and anger were irregular, and inner attendants feared being killed without cause and then committed regicide.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong took Bi's drugs and grew daily more restless; his joy and anger were irregular, and inner attendants feared being killed without cause and then committed regicide.

sentences.zh: 大通自雲壽一百五十歲，久得藥力。

translations.literal: Datong claimed for himself a lifespan of one hundred fifty years and long enjoyment of the drug's power.
translations.idiomatic: Datong claimed for himself a lifespan of one hundred fifty years and long enjoyment of the drug's power.

sentences.zh: 又有田佐元者，鳳翔虢人，自言有奇術，能變瓦礫為金，白衣授虢縣令。

translations.literal: There was also Tian Zuoyuan, a native of Guo in Fengxiang, who claimed strange arts and could transform rubble into gold; in commoner's dress he was appointed magistrate of Guo County.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Tian Zuoyuan, a native of Guo in Fengxiang, who claimed strange arts and could transform rubble into gold; in commoner's dress he was appointed magistrate of Guo County.

sentences.zh: 初，柳泌系京兆府，獄吏叱之曰：「何苦作此虛矯？」

translations.literal: At first Liu Bi was held in the metropolitan prefecture prison; the jailer rebuked him: "Why go to such trouble with this empty pretense?"
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Bi was held in the metropolitan prefecture prison; the jailer rebuked him, "Why go to such trouble with this empty pretense?"

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「吾本無此心，是李道古教我，且雲壽四百歲。」

translations.literal: Liu Bi said: "I never had this intention—it was Li Daogu who taught me, and he claimed I would live four hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bi said, "I never had this intention—it was Li Daogu who taught me, and he claimed I would live four hundred years."

sentences.zh: 府吏防虞周密，恐其隱化；

translations.literal: The prefectural officers guarded him with meticulous care, fearing he might vanish by transformation;
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural officers guarded him with meticulous care, fearing he might vanish by transformation;

sentences.zh: 及解衣就誅，一無變異，但灸灼之瘢痕浹身而已。

translations.literal: when he stripped for execution there was no transformation at all—only the burn scars from cauterization covered his body.
translations.idiomatic: when he stripped for execution there was no transformation at all—only the burn scars from cauterization covered his body.

sentences.zh: 镈卒於貶所。

translations.literal: Bo died in his place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Bo died in his place of banishment.

sentences.zh: 镈弟鏞，端士也。

translations.literal: Bo's younger brother Yong was an upright gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's younger brother Yong was an upright gentleman.

sentences.zh: 亦進士擢第，累歷宣歙、鳳翔使府從事，入為殿中侍御史，轉比部員外郎、河南縣令、都官郎中、河南少尹。

translations.literal: He too passed the jinshi examination, served successively as staff member in the Xuanchen and Fengxiang commissionerates, entered service as attendant censor within the palace, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, magistrate of Henan County, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and Vice Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He too passed the jinshi examination, served successively as staff member in the Xuanchen and Fengxiang commissionerates, entered service as attendant censor within the palace, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, magistrate of Henan County, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and Vice Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時镈為宰相，領度支，恩寵殊異。

translations.literal: At that time Bo was chancellor and in charge of the Department of Public Works, enjoying extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bo was chancellor and in charge of the Department of Public Works, enjoying extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 鏞惡其太盛，每弟兄宴語，即極言之，镈頗不悅。

translations.literal: Yong hated his excessive power; whenever the brothers feasted and talked together he spoke against it to the utmost, and Bo was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yong hated his excessive power; whenever the brothers feasted and talked together he spoke against it to the utmost, and Bo was quite displeased.

sentences.zh: 乃求為分司，除右庶子。

translations.literal: He then requested a detached-office post and was appointed Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested a detached-office post and was appointed Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 及镈獲罪，朝廷素知鏞有先見之明，不之罪，征為國子祭酒，改太子賓客、秘書監。

translations.literal: When Bo was punished, the court had long known Yong had foresight and did not punish him; he was summoned as Director of the Directorate of Education, then changed to Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo was punished, the court had long known Yong had foresight and did not punish him; he was summoned as Director of the Directorate of Education, then changed to Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開成初，除太子少保分司，卒年四十九。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he was appointed Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent in detached office and died at age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaicheng he was appointed Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent in detached office and died at age forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 鏞能文，尤工詩什，樂道自怡，不屑世務，當時名士皆與之交。

translations.literal: Yong could write, was especially skilled in poetry, delighted in the Way and found joy in himself, disdained worldly affairs, and the celebrated men of the time all associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong could write, was especially skilled in poetry, delighted in the Way and found joy in himself, disdained worldly affairs, and the celebrated men of the time all associated with him.

sentences.zh: 有集十八卷，著《性言》十四篇。

translations.literal: He left a collection in eighteen scrolls and composed Fourteen Chapters on Nature.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection in eighteen scrolls and composed Fourteen Chapters on Nature.

sentences.zh: 【贊】=史臣曰：奸邪害正，自古有之；

translations.literal: [Praise] The chronicler states: Wicked men harming the upright has existed since antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: [Praise] The chronicler states: Wicked men harming the upright has existed since antiquity;

sentences.zh: 而矯誕無忌，妒賢傷善，未有如延齡、皇甫之甚也。

translations.literal: yet feigned extravagance without restraint, envying talent and harming the good—none have been as extreme as Yanling and Huangfu Bo.
translations.idiomatic: yet feigned extravagance without restraint, envying talent and harming the good—none have been as extreme as Yanling and Huangfu Bo.

sentences.zh: 臣每讀陸丞相論延齡疏，未嘗不泣下沾衿，其守正效忠，為宗社大計，非端士益友，安能感激犯難如此？

translations.literal: Whenever I read Chancellor Lu's memorial against Yanling, I never fail to weep until my collar is wet; his upholding rectitude and loyal service for the great plan of the altars of soil and grain—without an upright gentleman and good friend, who could be stirred to brave difficulty like this?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read Chancellor Lu's memorial against Yanling, I never fail to weep until my collar is wet; his upholding rectitude and loyal service for the great plan of the altars of soil and grain—without an upright gentleman and good friend, who could be stirred to brave difficulty like this?

sentences.zh: 異哉德宗之為人主也，忠良不用，讒慝是崇，乃至身播國屯，幾將覆滅，尚獨保延齡之是，不悟盧杞之非，悲夫！

translations.literal: How strange that Dezong as lord was such: the loyal and good he would not employ, slanderers he exalted—until he himself was driven abroad and the state brought to near ruin, yet he still upheld Yanling as right and did not perceive Lu Qi's wrong. Pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: How strange that Dezong as lord was such: the loyal and good he would not employ, slanderers he exalted—until he himself was driven abroad and the state brought to near ruin, yet he still upheld Yanling as right and did not perceive Lu Qi's wrong. Pitiful!

sentences.zh: 執誼、叔文，乘時多僻，而欲斡運六合，斟酌萬幾；

translations.literal: Wei Zhiyi and Wang Shuwen, seizing an irregular time with many perversities, yet wished to turn the six directions and weigh the myriad affairs of state;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyi and Wang Shuwen, seizing an irregular time with many perversities, yet wished to turn the six directions and weigh the myriad affairs of state;

sentences.zh: 劉、柳諸生，逐臭市利，何狂妄之甚也！

translations.literal: Liu Yuxi, Liu Zongyuan, and the other scholars, chasing stench for market profit—how extreme their arrogance!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuxi, Liu Zongyuan, and the other scholars, chasing stench for market profit—how extreme their arrogance!

sentences.zh: 章武雄材睿斷，翦削厲階；

translations.literal: Zhangwu had heroic talent and keen judgment, cutting away dangerous steps;
translations.idiomatic: Zhangwu had heroic talent and keen judgment, cutting away dangerous steps;

sentences.zh: 洎逐群、度而相異、镈，蓋季年之妖惑也，夫何言哉！

translations.literal: yet when he expelled Qun and Du and made Yi and Bo chancellors, that was the bewitchment of his late years—what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: yet when he expelled Qun and Du and made Yi and Bo chancellors, that was the bewitchment of his late years—what more is there to say!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：貞元之風，好佞惡忠。

translations.literal: The praise reads: The wind of Zhenyuan favored flatterers and hated the loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The praise reads: The wind of Zhenyuan favored flatterers and hated the loyal.

sentences.zh: 齡、镈害善，為國蠹蟲。

translations.literal: Yanling and Bo harmed the good and were worms devouring the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling and Bo harmed the good and were worms devouring the state.

sentences.zh: 裴、陸獻替，嫉惡如風。

translations.literal: Pei and Lu offered correction, hating evil like a gale.
translations.idiomatic: Pei and Lu offered correction, hating evil like a gale.

sentences.zh: 天聽匪諶，吾道斯窮。

translations.literal: Heaven's hearing was not true; our Way was thus at an end.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's hearing was not true; our Way was thus at an end.
